chapters.title: Chapter 667
paragraphs: Infiltration. Assault. Finish.

The sequence of events could only be described as a Quick Attack. It lasted no more than a few moments, and the twenty warriors guarding the area around the underground prison collapsed helplessly before the unexpected ambush.
“I-intrud—!”
Sssht—thud!
The urgent voice that burst from someone’s lips died out before it could become a shout.
Moving like a streak of light, Yayul Mok struck the Bai warrior’s Mute Acupoint, then his Dizziness Acupoint. He caught the man as he collapsed and lowered him quietly to the ground.
Sss.
That had been close. A moment later, and the whole operation might have gone wrong.
“Whew.”
Yayul Mok let out the breath he had been holding and swept his gaze around the area.
Some twenty figures dressed in black, each wearing a different mask, watched every direction as they hid the subdued warriors in the grass.
—Report.
—All of them subdued.
The answer came through Sound Transmission from a man in a monkey mask.
The fact that he and six of the other men in black were the Seven Miao Tigers, the most outstanding warriors among the Miao people, was a secret known only to them and the Beast Miao King.
—One seemed to be missing, but I counted again. The man you just subdued was the last of them, Young Palace Lord. He probably stepped away to relieve himself.
—Any casualties on our side?
—None.
—Good. We nearly ruined everything before we even began.
—That would have been a problem.
Given what they were doing, a problem was putting it mildly.

On the surface, Jin Taekyung was a criminal imprisoned for an unforgivable offense. If word got out that Yayul Mok had tried to free him, even his position as Young Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace would not protect him.
But we have to do it.
Yayul Mok wiped the cold sweat from his forehead.
Young though he was, he understood how bold and dangerous this was. He also believed it was right.
Jin Taekyung is our ally. He came to help us. He even saved our warriors when they were in danger on Ailao Mountain.
Like most people of Nanman, Yayul Mok had grown up with little love for the Han Chinese. That had remained true until he met Jin Taekyung and the members of the Fire Dragon Pavilion.
Thinking well of Jin Taekyung did not mean he trusted all Han Chinese. An individual was an individual; a group was a group.
But he knew what was right and wrong here.
Just as his father, the Beast Miao King, did. The man he respected more than anyone.
—Do you have the keys to the underground prison?
—Of course.
The man in the monkey mask nodded and handed over the bundle of keys in his hand.
Opening the prison required five keys to be inserted in precisely the right order to activate the mechanism. They already knew how.
Click. Rumble.
The massive iron door began to move. As soon as the stairs leading underground came into view, everyone—including Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers—turned their clothes inside out.
Sssht. Flutter.
The wind stirred the torchlight across their white garments. In an instant, they looked like Bai warriors. They took up positions around the prison as though nothing had happened.
They would hold the post until the next shift arrived, half an hour from now.
We can only hope nothing happens before then.
They had mapped out the routes and guard positions beforehand, but no one could know how the operation would unfold.
Yayul Mok descended with the Seven Miao Tigers, his white clothes feeling especially strange today.
Jin Taekyung is on the fourth floor.
He knew where the cell was. He also knew wardens and guards were posted inside the prison.
They muffled even their footsteps as they went. Before long, faint voices reached them from somewhere ahead.
“Damn it. You didn’t cheat, did you?”
“Don’t be ridiculous. Just admit you lost.”
“Shit. I can’t make sense of it. Five games in a row? I’ve lost two nyang already.”
Wardens often gambled to pass the time. Their carelessness was a welcome sight to the intruders.
“Damn it. Turn your hand over.”
“Oh, give it a rest. Stop whining and keep your voice down. The higher-ups are already on edge over that Han Chinese bastard. If they catch us slacking off...”
Sssht—thud!
The voices in the dimness cut off.

The Seven Miao Tigers were among the finest warriors of the Miao people—Peak masters whose skill was recognized even in the Central Plains. The wardens never sensed them approaching. In an instant, their pressure points had been struck, their keys taken, and they themselves locked in an empty cell.
—Gisan. Dogok. Stay here.
—As you command.
—Not even an ant will get past us.
Leaving the post empty would invite suspicion.
Yayul Mok left two of the Seven Miao Tigers behind and increased his pace. Faster than an ordinary walk, but not so fast as to invite suspicion.
Step. Step.
Six figures made their way through the underground prison’s maze of corridors.
But things did not go as Yayul Mok had hoped.
“Hmm? Who are those men?”
Security on the fourth floor, where Jin Taekyung was held, was far tighter than usual. Besides the wardens, plenty of warriors guarded the prison’s interior.
“You there. Stop.”
Yayul Mok stopped without protest. As he steadied his breathing, he counted the men blocking their path.
Twenty.
Five of them were Peak masters.
These were elite Bai warriors. Yayul Mok kept his voice calm as he answered.
He had already removed his mask, and the few torches did little to light the prison. The darkness would help hide his face.
“We’re here on the Great Chieftain’s orders.”
“The Great Chieftain?”
The Bai warrior who appeared to be their captain deliberately furrowed his brow.
“He only just left. What does he want?”
“Nothing urgent. He said to give the prisoner another Force-Sealing Pill, just in case.”
“Hmm. Did he?”
“He must be worried about an escape. I’ve only heard the rumors myself, but the man sounds like a monster.”
The Bai warrior gave a short laugh.
“So I’ve heard. Now he’s just waiting to die.”
“I think so too, but you never know what might happen.”
“True enough. You sound young. Unless you’re here to relieve us, get on with it. You’ve got seven or eight minutes.”
“We won’t be long.”
Yayul Mok shrugged and walked toward them, his head lowered slightly to keep his face out of view.
Then he noticed one warrior’s hand gripping his scabbard tight.
They’ve already figured it out—!
Shing! Slice!
A flash grazed his shoulder. A few drops of blood flew with a faint sting as Yayul Mok twisted aside, evading two swords.
A shout like a thunderclap shook the prison.
“Intruders! Intruders!”
Peeeeep!
A shrill whistle sounded with the cry. Hurried footsteps broke the silence as warriors rushed from their posts throughout the prison.
Sensing them converging, Yayul Mok bit down hard and shouted, “Attack!”
At once, brilliant sword light flashed behind him.
Sssshh-shing!
Blades met in the dim torchlight.
Clang! Clang-clang!
Slice!
“Gah!”
A dozen weapons clashed in an instant. Blood flew, and men screamed.
The two men left at the wardens’ post realized what was happening and joined the fight. Within moments, half of the twenty Bai warriors had fallen wounded.
But...
Peep! Peeeeep!
“Stop them, whatever it takes! They’re after Jin Taekyung!”
“There aren’t many of them! Capture them if you can!”
The security was far tighter than their information had suggested. For every man they brought down, five more appeared. Bring down five, and ten took their place.
Worse, Yayul Mok and his men had sworn not to kill their fellow Nanman people while rescuing Jin Taekyung. It was one obstacle piled on another.
Sssshh-shing!
“Keep pushing!”
Bai warriors charged from every direction, their blades honed to sharp edges.
Surrounded by more than fifty enemies in the blink of an eye, Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers gritted their teeth and fought back.
Clang-clang-clang!
Slice!
Their hopes were one thing. The reality was another.
The enemy kept coming, too many for their small party to overcome. Worse still, Peak masters were scattered among them, each attack dangerous in its own right.
Sssht—thunk!
“Ugh!”
Small wounds multiplied. The bleeding did not stop.
Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers had brought down plenty of Bai warriors, yet the enemy’s numbers kept growing. Guards from the other floors had joined the fight.
Damn it.
Cold sweat soaked Yayul Mok’s back.
He had known this would not be easy. But they had been discovered too soon, and the prison was far more heavily guarded than he had been told.
If they capture us here...
Everything would end in the worst possible way.

As the Young Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, Yayul Mok would not lose his life. But his father, the Beast Miao King, would lose his political standing, while Jin Taekyung and the Fire Dragon Pavilion members—the original targets of the rescue—would be executed.
And then war will begin.
Not the Great Faction War they had once fought against the Demonic Cult. A war against the Murim of the Central Plains.
If Jin Taekyung died, nothing could be undone. That was one of the greatest reasons the father and son were risking their lives to rescue him.
There’s no other choice.
Yayul Mok bit his lip until it bled. His lips moved.
—Wonhu. I’m counting on you.
The Sound Transmission was brief, but it was enough.
Wonhu, the middle-aged man in the monkey mask and eldest of the Seven Miao Tigers, sent his sword flashing out and shouted, “Open a path!”
There was only one way forward now: break through, regardless of the cost, and rescue Jin Taekyung.
It was why they had all come here despite the danger. Yayul Mok could see no other way out.
If Jin Taekyung gets out of this prison, he can resolve everything.
Yayul Mok felt the hard wooden case inside his robes.
What he had told the guards before the fight—that he had come to give Jin Taekyung a Force-Sealing Pill—had not been entirely false.
Only it was not a Force-Sealing Pill, but an antidote that would lift the seal on his internal energy.
Clang-clang-clang!
Thrust! Slice!
“Gah!”
With defeat looming, the narrow prison corridor was their one advantage.
Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers drove toward a single point, ignoring the attacks coming from all sides. At last, a dark corridor opened before them.
“Go! Hurry!”
Yayul Mok left his loyal guard’s urgent cry behind and gathered all his strength to launch himself forward.
Or he would have.
Sssshh-shing! Grab!
A hand reached out of the darkness and caught his shoulder.
“Where are you going? Got somewhere to be?”
For a brief moment, Yayul Mok fell silent, oblivious to the battle raging around him. Then he spoke.
“...Why are you coming out of there?”

sentences.text: Infiltration.
Assault.
Finish.
The sequence of events could only be described as a Quick Attack.
It lasted no more than a few moments, and the twenty warriors guarding the area around the underground prison collapsed helplessly before the unexpected ambush.
“I-intrud—!”
Sssht—thud!
The urgent voice that burst from someone’s lips died out before it could become a shout.
Moving like a streak of light, Yayul Mok struck the Bai warrior’s Mute Acupoint, then his Dizziness Acupoint.
He caught the man as he collapsed and lowered him quietly to the ground.
Sss.
That had been close.
A moment later, and the whole operation might have gone wrong.
“Whew.”
Yayul Mok let out the breath he had been holding and swept his gaze around the area.
Some twenty figures dressed in black, each wearing a different mask, watched every direction as they hid the subdued warriors in the grass.
—Report.
—All of them subdued.
The answer came through Sound Transmission from a man in a monkey mask.
The fact that he and six of the other men in black were the Seven Miao Tigers, the most outstanding warriors among the Miao people, was a secret known only to them and the Beast Miao King.
—One seemed to be missing, but I counted again.
The man you just subdued was the last of them, Young Palace Lord.
He probably stepped away to relieve himself.
—Any casualties on our side?
—None.
—Good.
We nearly ruined everything before we even began.
—That would have been a problem.
Given what they were doing, a problem was putting it mildly.
On the surface, Jin Taekyung was a criminal imprisoned for an unforgivable offense.
If word got out that Yayul Mok had tried to free him, even his position as Young Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace would not protect him.
But we have to do it.
Yayul Mok wiped the cold sweat from his forehead.
Young though he was, he understood how bold and dangerous this was.
He also believed it was right.
Jin Taekyung is our ally.
He came to help us.
He even saved our warriors when they were in danger on Ailao Mountain.
Like most people of Nanman, Yayul Mok had grown up with little love for the Han Chinese.
That had remained true until he met Jin Taekyung and the members of the Fire Dragon Pavilion.
Thinking well of Jin Taekyung did not mean he trusted all Han Chinese.
An individual was an individual; a group was a group.
But he knew what was right and wrong here.
Just as his father, the Beast Miao King, did.
The man he respected more than anyone.
—Do you have the keys to the underground prison?
—Of course.
The man in the monkey mask nodded and handed over the bundle of keys in his hand.
Opening the prison required five keys to be inserted in precisely the right order to activate the mechanism.
They already knew how.
Click.
Rumble.
The massive iron door began to move.
As soon as the stairs leading underground came into view, everyone—including Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers—turned their clothes inside out.
Sssht.
Flutter.
The wind stirred the torchlight across their white garments.
In an instant, they looked like Bai warriors.
They took up positions around the prison as though nothing had happened.
They would hold the post until the next shift arrived, half an hour from now.
We can only hope nothing happens before then.
They had mapped out the routes and guard positions beforehand, but no one could know how the operation would unfold.
Yayul Mok descended with the Seven Miao Tigers, his white clothes feeling especially strange today.
Jin Taekyung is on the fourth floor.
He knew where the cell was.
He also knew wardens and guards were posted inside the prison.
They muffled even their footsteps as they went.
Before long, faint voices reached them from somewhere ahead.
“Damn it.
You didn’t cheat, did you?”
“Don’t be ridiculous.
Just admit you lost.”
“Shit.
I can’t make sense of it.
Five games in a row?
I’ve lost two nyang already.”
Wardens often gambled to pass the time.
Their carelessness was a welcome sight to the intruders.
“Damn it.
Turn your hand over.”
“Oh, give it a rest.
Stop whining and keep your voice down.
The higher-ups are already on edge over that Han Chinese bastard.
If they catch us slacking off...”
Sssht—thud!
The voices in the dimness cut off.
The Seven Miao Tigers were among the finest warriors of the Miao people—Peak masters whose skill was recognized even in the Central Plains.
The wardens never sensed them approaching.
In an instant, their pressure points had been struck, their keys taken, and they themselves locked in an empty cell.
—Gisan.
Dogok.
Stay here.
—As you command.
—Not even an ant will get past us.
Leaving the post empty would invite suspicion.
Yayul Mok left two of the Seven Miao Tigers behind and increased his pace.
Faster than an ordinary walk, but not so fast as to invite suspicion.
Step.
Step.
Six figures made their way through the underground prison’s maze of corridors.
But things did not go as Yayul Mok had hoped.
“Hmm?
Who are those men?”
Security on the fourth floor, where Jin Taekyung was held, was far tighter than usual.
Besides the wardens, plenty of warriors guarded the prison’s interior.
“You there.
Stop.”
Yayul Mok stopped without protest.
As he steadied his breathing, he counted the men blocking their path.
Twenty.
Five of them were Peak masters.
These were elite Bai warriors.
Yayul Mok kept his voice calm as he answered.
He had already removed his mask, and the few torches did little to light the prison.
The darkness would help hide his face.
“We’re here on the Great Chieftain’s orders.”
“The Great Chieftain?”
The Bai warrior who appeared to be their captain deliberately furrowed his brow.
“He only just left.
What does he want?”
“Nothing urgent.
He said to give the prisoner another Force-Sealing Pill, just in case.”
“Hmm.
Did he?”
“He must be worried about an escape.
I’ve only heard the rumors myself, but the man sounds like a monster.”
The Bai warrior gave a short laugh.
“So I’ve heard.
Now he’s just waiting to die.”
“I think so too, but you never know what might happen.”
“True enough.
You sound young.
Unless you’re here to relieve us, get on with it.
You’ve got seven or eight minutes.”
“We won’t be long.”
Yayul Mok shrugged and walked toward them, his head lowered slightly to keep his face out of view.
Then he noticed one warrior’s hand gripping his scabbard tight.
They’ve already figured it out—!
Shing!
Slice!
A flash grazed his shoulder.
A few drops of blood flew with a faint sting as Yayul Mok twisted aside, evading two swords.
A shout like a thunderclap shook the prison.
“Intruders!
Intruders!”
Peeeeep!
A shrill whistle sounded with the cry.
Hurried footsteps broke the silence as warriors rushed from their posts throughout the prison.
Sensing them converging, Yayul Mok bit down hard and shouted, “Attack!”
At once, brilliant sword light flashed behind him.
Sssshh-shing!
Blades met in the dim torchlight.
Clang!
Clang-clang!
Slice!
“Gah!”
A dozen weapons clashed in an instant.
Blood flew, and men screamed.
The two men left at the wardens’ post realized what was happening and joined the fight.
Within moments, half of the twenty Bai warriors had fallen wounded.
But...
Peep!
Peeeeep!
“Stop them, whatever it takes!
They’re after Jin Taekyung!”
“There aren’t many of them!
Capture them if you can!”
The security was far tighter than their information had suggested.
For every man they brought down, five more appeared.
Bring down five, and ten took their place.
Worse, Yayul Mok and his men had sworn not to kill their fellow Nanman people while rescuing Jin Taekyung.
It was one obstacle piled on another.
Sssshh-shing!
“Keep pushing!”
Bai warriors charged from every direction, their blades honed to sharp edges.
Surrounded by more than fifty enemies in the blink of an eye, Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers gritted their teeth and fought back.
Clang-clang-clang!
Slice!
Their hopes were one thing.
The reality was another.
The enemy kept coming, too many for their small party to overcome.
Worse still, Peak masters were scattered among them, each attack dangerous in its own right.
Sssht—thunk!
“Ugh!”
Small wounds multiplied.
The bleeding did not stop.
Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers had brought down plenty of Bai warriors, yet the enemy’s numbers kept growing.
Guards from the other floors had joined the fight.
Damn it.
Cold sweat soaked Yayul Mok’s back.
He had known this would not be easy.
But they had been discovered too soon, and the prison was far more heavily guarded than he had been told.
If they capture us here...
Everything would end in the worst possible way.
As the Young Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, Yayul Mok would not lose his life.
But his father, the Beast Miao King, would lose his political standing, while Jin Taekyung and the Fire Dragon Pavilion members—the original targets of the rescue—would be executed.
And then war will begin.
Not the Great Faction War they had once fought against the Demonic Cult.
A war against the Murim of the Central Plains.
If Jin Taekyung died, nothing could be undone.
That was one of the greatest reasons the father and son were risking their lives to rescue him.
There’s no other choice.
Yayul Mok bit his lip until it bled.
His lips moved.
—Wonhu.
I’m counting on you.
The Sound Transmission was brief, but it was enough.
Wonhu, the middle-aged man in the monkey mask and eldest of the Seven Miao Tigers, sent his sword flashing out and shouted, “Open a path!”
There was only one way forward now: break through, regardless of the cost, and rescue Jin Taekyung.
It was why they had all come here despite the danger.
Yayul Mok could see no other way out.
If Jin Taekyung gets out of this prison, he can resolve everything.
Yayul Mok felt the hard wooden case inside his robes.
What he had told the guards before the fight—that he had come to give Jin Taekyung a Force-Sealing Pill—had not been entirely false.
Only it was not a Force-Sealing Pill, but an antidote that would lift the seal on his internal energy.
Clang-clang-clang!
Thrust!
Slice!
“Gah!”
With defeat looming, the narrow prison corridor was their one advantage.
Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers drove toward a single point, ignoring the attacks coming from all sides.
At last, a dark corridor opened before them.
“Go!
Hurry!”
Yayul Mok left his loyal guard’s urgent cry behind and gathered all his strength to launch himself forward.
Or he would have.
Sssshh-shing!
Grab!
A hand reached out of the darkness and caught his shoulder.
“Where are you going?
Got somewhere to be?”
For a brief moment, Yayul Mok fell silent, oblivious to the battle raging around him.
Then he spoke.
“...Why are you coming out of there?”

chapters.title: Chapter 668
paragraphs: Sometimes, things happen in life that you just can’t explain.
Like right now.
“Where are you going? Got somewhere to be?”
For a brief moment, time seemed to stop in the middle of its headlong rush.

The Seven Miao Tigers, who had been rampaging like beasts despite wounds all over their bodies; the Bai warriors, who now filled the underground prison’s corridors; and Yayul Mok—all stood frozen like statues, staring blankly at the person who had emerged from beyond the thick darkness.
How?
It was the question on everyone’s mind. He couldn’t be here. He wasn’t supposed to be here.

But while everyone inside the underground prison wore the expression of someone who had seen a ghost, only Yayul Mok, whose shoulder was caught in his powerful grip, realized that this unbelievable situation was real.
He had to ask.
“...Why are you coming out of there?”
Yayul Mok’s eyes were vacant, his voice dazed. The answer he got was remarkably short.
“I just came out.”
“I was locked up in there, right? So that’s where I came out of.”
What the fuck is he talking about?
Yayul Mok and everyone else were thinking the same thing.
So what the hell? We’re asking how the bastard who was supposed to be locked in the underground prison crawled out.
He hadn’t simply been locked in a cell, either. They’d heard he had iron balls weighing more than ten thousand geun hanging off him like jewelry, and that his internal energy had been sealed.
And the bars on every side of his cell had meteorite iron mixed into them. The prison had been built for that one monster alone.
So how?
It made no sense.
The Bai warriors instinctively suspected a traitor on the inside. Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers wondered if their information had been wrong. And he took a casual step forward.
Step.
His footfall broke the silence.
The man emerged from the dark corridor into the flickering torchlight. Jin Taekyung frowned.
“Ugh, that’s bright. Hey, you.”
At Jin Taekyung’s pointed finger, the Bai warrior holding his torch high asked with a vacant expression,
“Me?”
“Yeah, you.”
“Wh-why?”
“Why do you think, you clueless bastard? My eyes hurt. Put your arm down. What are you doing, giving a presentation? Crossing the street without your parents?”
“No, sir.”
The Bai warrior answered blankly, though he had no idea what Jin Taekyung meant. Somehow, answering felt like the thing to do. So did addressing him politely.
“Look at this bastard, still crossing on green. I’ll give you three seconds to lower your arm. If the light turns red before you do, you’re dead. Three.”
“Ah, I’m sorry.”
“To hell with sorry. Put your arm down. Two.”
“Yes, sir.”
Whoosh!
The Bai warrior hastily lowered his arm. The already faint torchlight dimmed further, and Jin Taekyung nodded in satisfaction.
“Hmm. Much better. Good job.”
“It was nothing...”
The Bai warrior felt an odd swell of pride at the praise. Then he stopped.
Huh?
Wait. This wasn’t right.
As realization struck, an unfamiliar sound whipped past his ear.
Thwack! Thud.
Sizzle.
He crumpled, and his torch fell into a puddle. The Bai captain who had struck his foolish subordinate across the jaw without hesitation growled.
“You idiot.”
His icy voice snapped the Bai warriors out of their daze. They had watched the whole exchange unfold as if it were the most natural thing in the world.
What the hell?
It was like waking from a deep sleep. All at once, they understood: impossible as it seemed, this was real, and the battle wasn’t over.
And...
“Now he’s even putting out the fire for us. How thoughtful.”
They had to subdue the monster who had escaped his restraints.
The realization came like a bolt of lightning. The shout that followed was thunder.
“Attack!”
The shout, filled with powerful internal energy, shook the underground prison.
At the same time as he ordered the attack, the captain of the Bai warriors was the first to leap forward. He kicked off the wall and shot toward Jin Taekyung.
Tap-tap—whoosh!
He was fast enough to rival a Peak master from a major sect.
The Seven Miao Tigers recovered half a beat too late. They tried to intercept him, but weapons came at them from every direction.
Swish-swish-swish—clang!
Wonhu, the eldest of the Seven Miao Tigers, blocked the attacks and shouted, “Hurry! Give him the antidote—!”
Clang!
The clash cut off his cry. Seeing Yayul Mok reach hurriedly inside his robes, the Bai captain knew.
Just as I thought. Not yet.
Jin Taekyung.
He did not know how that young monster from the Central Plains had escaped the underground prison, but there was no doubt that the boy had not yet released the seal on his internal energy.
Then I can do this.

Even a Supreme Peak master was little more than an unusually capable ordinary man without his internal energy. The martial arts Jin Taekyung had learned and the principles he had mastered hadn’t vanished, of course. But unarmed, he could hardly hope to face a swordsman who had reached the Peak realm long ago.
I’ll capture him myself.
The prospect of earning a feat no one else could match, together with his certainty of victory, made the captain feel lighter than ever. The sword in his hand blazed with dazzling light.
Ssssss!
Sword Energy surged along the sharp blade. Yayul Mok glanced back instinctively, and the captain saw his eyes tremble.
This would be the sharpest, most powerful strike of his life. He was sure of it.
Now!
Ssshhhiiing!
The motion was flawless. A perfect draw.
Sword Energy burst from the blade, cutting through the darkness toward both men. The captain cried out in triumph.
“Got—!”
Slice!
His Sword Energy cut through empty air.
What?
The captain blinked.
They were gone. Nothing remained where his Sword Energy had passed—not Yayul Mok, not Jin Taekyung. Both had vanished like apparitions.
How?
The next moment, an answer came to the question he had asked only in his mind.
“Oh. You were just thinking how, weren’t you?”
The voice came from behind him.
Goose bumps climbed the captain’s spine as he spun, his sword following through a motion ingrained by years of practice.
Whoosh!
Once again, his sword cut through the air.
No. It almost did.
Grgrgrk.
The tip trembled faintly. Another question surfaced in his suddenly empty mind.
What... is this?
The blade, brimming with Sword Energy, had stopped before an unarmed palm.
No. He hasn’t even blocked it with his hand.
Barely one chi separated the trembling blade from the palm. In that gap, an invisible force pushed his sword back.
Slowly, but powerfully.
Grgrgrk.
With eyes trembling as fiercely as his sword, the captain squeezed out his voice.
“S-Seizing an Object Through Empty Space?”
The carefully polished blade glinted in the darkness. Beyond it, white teeth showed in a slight grin.
“Seizing an Object Through Empty Space? Well, it’s similar.”
“H-how? Your internal energy was sealed—”
“I said similar. I didn’t say it was the same thing.”
What?
“Don’t try to understand. You couldn’t even if you tried.”
It was a cruel truth. Even if the captain devoted the rest of his life to martial arts, he would never reach the threshold of the Middle Dantian.
“Wh-what is this...?”
That was a realm the captain, who had devoted his entire life to martial arts, could not understand. Unfortunately, Jin Taekyung was not the sort of kind person who would patiently tutor a dunce.
“Get lost.”
At the moment the captain’s wide eyes reflected Jin Taekyung’s fist, wrapped tightly in chains—
Bam!
Pain unlike anything he had ever known exploded through his abdomen and swept over his body.
“Guh-heok!”
It was a punch so powerful that Jin Taekyung had to have recovered his internal energy.
But the captain was only human—a little more capable than most. He had no hope of withstanding a blow driven by strength and speed far beyond human limits.
Whoosh!
He could feel his body hurtling backward, hear the air shriek around it. His consciousness faded beneath the pain.
That insane... monster.
That was his final thought.

The captain’s already unconscious body grazed past the Seven Miao Tigers, who were still fighting desperately, then crashed like a cannonball into the Bai warriors filling the underground prison’s corridor.
Boom! Crack!
“Argh!”
“Wh-what was that?”
The underground prison descended into chaos. The Bai warriors realized what had struck them and stared, openmouthed.
“C-Captain?”
“But how...?”
The murmurs died almost as quickly as they had begun. There was only one person here who could have defeated the captain—a high-ranking Bai warrior, a Peak master, and the strongest among them.
“J-Jin Taekyung.”
The name slipped from someone’s lips. Every eye turned in the same direction.
Splash. Clatter.
A man walked through a puddle of filthy water, the chains severed from his iron balls dangling from both hands.
“Yeah, that’s me. Someone call?”
In complete contrast to the dark atmosphere of the underground prison, the smile around Jin Taekyung’s lips was as bright as sunlight.
Like a predator spotting prey.
No. Like a Fiend.
“Anyone want the shit beaten out of them with a chain? Hands?”
The Bai warriors froze as a chill ran through them. But not all of them stayed frozen.
“Attack him!”
“We outnumber them! Push forward!”
Swish-swish-swish!
A dozen or so figures sprang off the walls and charged. They were squad captains, each a Peak master. Though none was as strong as their fallen captain, the Bai warriors felt their courage return.
Or almost did.
Whoooosh!
A chain hurtled toward the charging men with a heavy rush of air.
Bam-bam-bam-bam-bam!
The chain swept through the dozen or so squad captains charging forward, knocking them away all at once.
Boom! Crash-crash-crash!
The underground prison shook. Everyone swallowed as they watched a thick cloud of dust rise. Then a low voice reached them.
“Is it summer already? Why are there so many damn flies...”
“Anyway. Who’s next? Hands?”
No one stepped forward this time.
The Bai warriors stared at the man standing before them like the Grim Reaper, then retreated as though by agreement.
But...
Boom. Boom.
An ominous sound rose from the stairs behind them, snuffing out even the faintest hope of escape.
“Oh, right. Forgot to tell you.”
Jin Taekyung grinned and pointed toward the stairs.
“Something big’s coming.”
The next moment, the Bai warriors heard a chilling roar.
“Taishan. Hungryyyyyyyyy!”
It was the roar of a starving beast.
No—of Taishan.

The captain’s already unconscious body grazed past the Seven Miao Tigers, who were still fighting desperately, then crashed like a cannonball into the Bai warriors filling the underground prison’s corridor.
Boom!
Crack!
“Argh!”
“Wh-what was that?”
The underground prison descended into chaos.
The Bai warriors realized what had struck them and stared, openmouthed.
“C-Captain?”
“But how...?”
The murmurs died almost as quickly as they had begun.
There was only one person here who could have defeated the captain—a high-ranking Bai warrior, a Peak master, and the strongest among them.
“J-Jin Taekyung.”
The name slipped from someone’s lips.
Every eye turned in the same direction.
Splash.
Clatter.
A man walked through a puddle of filthy water, the chains severed from his iron balls dangling from both hands.
“Yeah, that’s me.
Someone call?”
In complete contrast to the dark atmosphere of the underground prison, the smile around Jin Taekyung’s lips was as bright as sunlight.
Like a predator spotting prey.
No.
Like a Fiend.
“Anyone want the shit beaten out of them with a chain?
Hands?”
The Bai warriors froze as a chill ran through them.
But not all of them stayed frozen.
“Attack him!”
“We outnumber them!
Push forward!”
Swish-swish-swish!
A dozen or so figures sprang off the walls and charged.
They were squad captains, each a Peak master.
Though none was as strong as their fallen captain, the Bai warriors felt their courage return.
Or almost did.
Whoooosh!
A chain hurtled toward the charging men with a heavy rush of air.
Bam-bam-bam-bam-bam!
The chain swept through the dozen or so squad captains charging forward, knocking them away all at once.
Boom!
Crash-crash-crash!
The underground prison shook.
Everyone swallowed as they watched a thick cloud of dust rise.
Then a low voice reached them.
“Is it summer already?
Why are there so many damn flies...”
“Anyway.
Who’s next?
Hands?”
No one stepped forward this time.
The Bai warriors stared at the man standing before them like the Grim Reaper, then retreated as though by agreement.
But...
Boom.
Boom.
An ominous sound rose from the stairs behind them, snuffing out even the faintest hope of escape.
“Oh, right.
Forgot to tell you.”
Jin Taekyung grinned and pointed toward the stairs.
“Something big’s coming.”
The next moment, the Bai warriors heard a chilling roar.
“Taishan.
Hungryyyyyyyyy!”
It was the roar of a starving beast.
No—of Taishan.

chapters.title: Chapter 669
paragraphs: The time it takes to drink a cup of tea.
No, perhaps mere moments.
It took less than the time needed to drink a cup of tea to settle everything in the underground prison.
Taishan, half-crazed with hunger, blocked the stairs. I advanced at the front with Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers behind me, and the Bai warriors lost their will to fight.
That was fortunate for me.
We needed to escape the underground prison as quickly as possible, but I was also beginning to feel my limits. I still had not completely grasped the full utility of the Middle Dantian.

Breaking my restraints had already consumed an enormous amount of mental strength. After one brief fight on top of that, my stomach was churning and my chest had begun to hurt. Taishan’s arrival was like getting an entire army as reinforcements.
“Gwoooooooh!”
Hmm. Actually, he was closer to the Hulk.
And it wasn’t just the presence of a Supreme Peak master that made the enemy surrender so quickly. Taishan’s eerie muttering had a lot to do with it.
“Gasp!”
His eyes gleamed with hunger.
To the Bai warriors, the sight of Taishan approaching while spitting out incomprehensible words at machine-gun speed must have been terrifying. But I knew exactly what his incantation meant.
“Roast duck! Maechae Guyuk! Fish-Fragrant Shredded Pork! Beijing Sauce Shredded Pork! Garlic Pork! Twice-Cooked Pork! Sweet and Sour Pork! Soy-Braised Beef! Dongpo Pork! Mapo Tofu!”
“Kung Pao Chicken! Stir-Fried Mushrooms and Vegetables! King-Size Dumplings! Beggar’s Chicken! Sweet-and-Sour Carp! Aaaaaaah!”
Hmm.
Good thing they couldn’t understand Han Chinese. Then again, a man slowly approaching while chanting food names like he was possessed might have been even scarier.
“Hungryyyyyyyyy!”
“Eek! Dark arts! That monster’s about to use dark arts!”
“I surrender! I surrender!”
That bastard was a Saiyan, at least by Nanman standards.
Judging by their reactions, you’d think he’d shouted “Kamehameha!” instead of “I’m hungry!”
Whatever I thought of it, his cry of hunger worked. Even the few brave men who stepped forward despite it got smashed by Taishan, and that settled the matter.
“Don’t be afraid! Charge!”
“We can do this! Strike him!”
The men who came forward were skilled enough to be considered decent Supreme First Rate masters even in the Central Plains.
Their only problem was who they’d chosen to fight.
Thud! Craaack!
Crack-crack!
Taishan swung his log-thick arms and legs, sending bodies flying in every direction.
The Bai warriors swallowed hard and lowered their weapons. Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers stared at me in disbelief.
“What? What are you looking at?”
“No, it’s just... wasn’t your internal energy sealed?”
“Yeah. It was. I still can’t use it.”
“...Then how?”
“Mine’s a long story. That guy was born like that.”

The human body had limits. I’d surpassed them by an absurd margin thanks to the System, but Taishan was a naturally occurring monster. Even without internal energy, he could beat down a First Rate master as easily as a rat.
Was he exposed to gamma radiation as a kid or something?
A reasonable suspicion, but it didn’t matter right now.
I looked at the Bai warriors who had lost their will to fight and disarmed themselves, then muttered quietly.
“All right. Let’s deal with this lot first.”
The short version is that the Bai warriors who surrendered survived. More precisely, Yayul Mok spared them.
Thud. Slump.

A warrior struck by a Pressure-Point Strike lost consciousness and fell. The Seven Miao Tigers, whom I’d gotten to know a few days earlier on the way to Ailao Mountain, gathered the unconscious warriors in one place and locked them in the underground prison. Then we headed straight for the stairs to the surface.
Squelch.
“I told you before... you’re going to regret this.”
I said it as we walked. Yayul Mok understood what I meant and shook his head.
“No, I won’t.”
“Our faces are out in the open. Once they wake up, whose name do you think they’ll give first?”

Yayul Mok was the Young Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace. That alone said enough. The Seven Miao Tigers were also well-known warriors who represented the Miao people. Their tribes might be different, but some of the prisoners had probably recognized them already.
“It’s only a matter of time before this comes out. We should’ve silenced them.”
“It doesn’t matter.”
“Like hell it doesn’t. You said we weren’t going to flee along this path, so why wouldn’t it matter? If we remain here...”
“Our identities will be revealed. Our lives won’t be in immediate danger, but we’ll pay dearly for defying the Tribal Grand Council’s decision.”
“I hate to ask, but do you enjoy getting fucked over? Is being locked in the underground prison on your bucket list?”
“Bucki... I can hardly pronounce it. I don’t know what that is, but I knew the risk when I did this.”
Yayul Mok continued quietly.
“Our tribes are different, but we’re all Nanman people. We’ve lived together on this land for a long time. If we kill our own people, we become monsters too.”
His words brought someone to mind. A man who had become a monster for the sake of revenge.
Baeksang.
Maybe that was the difference between a human being and a monster: refusing to sacrifice lives for your own ends.
Even so, I spoke with a heavy heart.
“We should’ve killed them all.”
“You do like killing. Are all Han Chinese like you?”
“You crazy bastard. Do you think I’m some kind of fiend? It’s just...”
“That’s enough. I already know.”
“What?”
I turned to find Yayul Mok smiling silently.
“You’re worried about us. You feel guilty because we got ourselves into trouble trying to save you.”
“The Central Plains and Nanman have different languages, but we have a word for friend too. Perhaps that’s what you and I have become without realizing it. Unless I’m the only one who thinks so.”
Damn it. I had no idea what to say.
While I stood there speechless, the seemingly endless stairs finally came to an end. The entrance to the underground prison was before us.
“Wonhu.”

At Yayul Mok’s call, the middle-aged man nodded and stepped forward. He looked like a monkey. He tried the keys on a large ring one after another, and the enormous iron door began to open with a heavy rumble.
Grooooan.
Faint moonlight slipped through the widening gap. Yayul Mok took two small wooden cases from inside his robes.

“An antidote to lift the seal on your internal energy. It’s made with a secret Bai technique, so I could only get two. Once your internal energy is restored, you should be able to lead the others out of Nanman.”
“The others?”
“I don’t know if it was because they’re old and injured, but security around them was remarkably lax. Uncle Baeksang isn’t usually so careless.”
As Yayul Mok spoke, I saw them beyond the fully opened door: two unconscious people lying across a White Tiger’s back.
“Lord! Namho!”
Seeing the familiar faces, Taishan hurriedly ran out of the underground prison. I stared at Yayul Mok with complicated emotions.
“Go. We’ll buy you as much time as we can. They’ll discover what happened within half a shichen at most, but even that should help.”
I didn’t know what to say.
What would have happened without their help?

Taishan and I might have escaped the underground prison on our own, but we could never have gotten out of the Nanman Beast Palace this quickly. As long as Namho and Sama Pyo were being held somewhere in the Inner Palace, I was bound more tightly than I’d been by ten thousand geun of iron balls.
I might’ve been captured again trying to get them out.
But these people had given everything they had to help me, knowing the danger it put them in.
Thanks to them, I had a second chance to undo my bad move.
“...Thank you.”

At the thanks I had not managed to offer until now, Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers—as well as the men disguised as Bai warriors outside the underground prison—smiled faintly and shook their heads.
“No need to thank us.”
“That’s right. We’re only repaying a debt Nanman owes you.”
“My hyung was on Ailao Mountain. Thanks to you, I’ll get to see him again.”
People whose faces and names I didn’t know had helped me. One even called me his benefactor.
I looked at each of them, committing their faces to memory. Then I took the wooden cases from Yayul Mok and stepped into the faint moonlight.
Soft crunch.
The moment my foot landed on the damp earth—
Ding!

System Escape from the underground prison before the execution (Complete) - You have fulfilled the Quest success conditions! - You have successfully completed the Quest, Escape from Namshank! - Issuing the Quest completion Reward! - You obtained a massive amount of EXP! - Level Up! - Some injuries and Status Effects have been removed!
As the Quest notifications rang in my ears, a cool breeze that only I could feel swept through my body.
Whoooosh!

My muscles, stiff for more than a full day, loosened. The fatigue that had built up as I forced out the still woefully insufficient power of the Middle Dantian faded. Finally, the force constricting my Lower Dantian melted away.
Hoo.
Heat from the Scorching Yang Qi mingled with my long exhale.
Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers widened their eyes, as if they had sensed something from my appearance.
Of course they’re surprised. I haven’t even taken the antidote yet.
But I had neither the time nor the intention to explain every little detail.
I tossed Taishan a pill from one of the wooden cases, telling him it was a snack, then fed the other to the unconscious Sama Pyo.
Fwoosh. Sssslip.
The Scorching Yang Qi melted the pill like water. As the liquid ran down Sama Pyo’s throat, color returned to his slightly pale face.
He’s in better shape than I expected, but he shouldn’t push himself for a while.
Namho aside, losing Sama Pyo’s full strength as a fighter was a serious disadvantage. But it didn’t mean we couldn’t escape.
If anything, we were in a better position than before I’d surrendered.
We’ve got everyone except the reconnaissance squad, and I’ve gained a little insight too.
Then Yayul Mok offered one more kindness I hadn’t expected.
“Take him with you.”
Grrrr.
A familiar growl.
The White Tiger, looking at its lifelong friend and master with sad eyes, held out its back toward me.
“Muyaho is called a spiritual creature even among Nanman’s White Tigers. He’s like a brother to me. I trust you’ll take good care of him.”
As if it understood Yayul Mok’s low voice, the White Tiger licked my hand, then pressed its nose against me and sniffed.
Yayul Mok smiled faintly as he watched it, then pointed in one direction.
“Go. Run straight northeast from where we first met, and you’ll find the reconnaissance squad.”
That was when it happened.
Thud.
At the sound of a blow, Yayul Mok’s body jerked. Wonhu caught him as he collapsed, then grinned at me.
“I trust you understand without us saying it.”
“You people...”
“Please look after the Young Palace Lord.”

chapters.title: Chapter 670
paragraphs: It was a short time, and a long one.

Long enough for a moment to feel like seven days and nights. Long enough to walk through the past several decades, year by year, and watch the newborn who had cried in the arms of his mother, dead from childbirth, grow into a fine young man.
Baeksang’s deliberation was short and long, long and short.
When his tightly closed lips finally parted, he already had his answer.
“You’ll regret this.”
The Beast Miao King asked calmly, “What will I regret? Coming to find you? Or rescuing Jin Taekyung and the other Han Chinese?”
“Everything that has happened until now.”
“Like you, Baeksang?”
“It’s different.”
Baeksang’s expression hardened.
“Unlike me, you still have a chance, Palace Lord. One last chance to undo your mistake.”
“One last chance...”
“If you leave quietly now, I’ll forget everything I saw and heard here. As though none of it happened.”
“How can I cover the sky with the palm of my hand? I knew what I was risking when I told you to spare the men guarding the underground prison.”
“If I order them to keep silent, they will. The Bai people are no less loyal to me than the Seven Miao Tigers are to you.”
“Is that... the last kindness you can offer me as my sworn brother?”
Baeksang nodded without a word.
The Beast Miao King gave him a sorrowful smile.
“Then let me ask you one more time, on the strength of that last kindness. Half a shichen. Open a path for them, even if only for half a shichen.”
“Palace Lord!”
“Even if I could turn back, I wouldn’t. That’s the one difference between us, after a lifetime together.”
The corners of Baeksang’s eyes trembled.
More than anything, he wanted to tell the Beast Miao King he was wrong. That unlike him, Baeksang had seen only one path ahead and had had no choice but to walk it.
But his lips stayed shut. His hand had already found his sword hilt.
Click. Shing.
The cold scrape of metal cut through the brief silence. The Beast Miao King’s gaze deepened as he looked at Baeksang, sword lowered at his side.
“So that’s your choice?”
“I can’t help it, Palace Lord. Right now... it’s the best I can do.”
“It’s much better not to hear that awkward formal speech. It feels as though we’ve gone back to the old days.”
“You know as well as I do, Palace Lord. We can never go back to those days.”
“Do you think so?”
“Of course.”
The Beast Miao King smiled faintly at his firm answer.
Baeksang had made his decision. He did not hesitate.
Tssssss!
Dazzling light flooded the space around them. A vast concentration of qi known as Sword Force descended toward its target.
Slice!
Three tigers ran like the wind, led by the snow-white White Tiger.
Wonhu, the eldest of the Seven Miao Tigers, watched their backs disappear into the darkness and muttered,
“Damn, they’re fast.”
That was the entirety of his impression.
Those who were leaving had left. Those who remained had stayed. He and the others had chosen to stay.
“Heh heh.”
Wonhu laughed, feeling strangely relieved, and pulled a gourd from his robes.
Pop.
The scent of liquor spread the instant he pulled the stopper. The eyes of the nearby Miao warriors lit up.
“Oh-ho.”
“That smells incredible. Did you brew it yourself, Big Brother?”
“Hell, did they round up nothing but a pack of fucking mutts? Why are all your noses so sharp?”
He grumbled, but his eyes were smiling. With a look of helpless resignation, Wonhu passed the gourd to the men crowding around him.
“There isn’t much. Take turns and have a little each.”
“I swear, not a drop will make it back to your mouth, Big Brother.”
“Now this I can’t pass up.”
The Miao warriors roared with laughter and took turns tipping back the gourd.
Nanman people were famous for their love of liquor. With twenty grown men sharing it, their boast that they would leave nothing behind sounded entirely plausible.
But...
“Ahh, that’s good. Your turn, Big Brother. I left you a few drops out of courtesy.”
Wonhu took the gourd at last and let out a short laugh.
Slosh.
One light shake told him enough. It was not even half empty.
The men stood there shamelessly praising the liquor, and he couldn’t help laughing again.
“Turns out you’re not mutts. You’re just a pack of blowhards.”
“Hm? What’s that supposed to mean?”
“Has senility caught up with you already? You’re only in your fifties.”
“Enough nonsense. Drink.”
At their urging, Wonhu tipped the gourd—not toward his mouth, but toward the weed-covered ground.
Trickle.
“Don’t begrudge a single drop. If we survive, we’ll sit together and drink all night. If we fall here, we can get drunk after we’re dead.”
The men watched him with solemn faces. Then their mouths curled into smiles.
“Yeah. I like that.”
“Big Brother knows what he’s talking about.”
“You’ve always been crazier about liquor than martial arts, haven’t you?”
Wonhu laughed. So did the Seven Miao Tigers, who had spent their lives alongside him, and the Miao warriors who had volunteered for this dangerous mission.
Regrets? Not one.
Even if every one of them died here, their only hope would make it out of danger alive.
That was why Wonhu could laugh. He thought of the man who had always led from the front, who had sent even his only heir here to set an example.
I’ll gladly accept punishment for disobeying your order... in the afterlife, my lord.
Neither the Beast Miao King nor Yayul Mok feared death. They never put their subordinates in front of them as shields, and they never backed away in terror.
The Beast Miao King loved the only child he had had late in life more than anything. But if he knew what Wonhu had done, he would scold him. No life was worth more than another.
That’s enough of a reason to give mine.

Wonhu shook the now-empty gourd, trying to get out the last drops. He watched the liquor fall like the tears of an ant, smacked his lips, and suddenly spoke toward somewhere in the darkness that had settled all around them.
“Hey, got any liquor?”
A low voice answered.
“I thought you were on duty.”
“We both know better. Go peel yourself a tiger’s dick and eat it.”
Wonhu grinned.
Their scheduled shift change was long past, and the waves of energy reaching him from the darkness were strong enough to raise goose bumps.
“So? Are you going to share or not?”
“I’ve heard there’s a monkey among the Miao people who likes liquor. Catch.”
Whoosh.
Wonhu snatched the object out of the air. The moment he saw the rough, familiar gourd, a groan escaped him.
“This...”
There was no mistaking it. His lord, the Beast Miao King, had made this gourd himself and always carried it.
“Recognize it?”
The voice reached his ears again. Wonhu slowly raised his head, and a man came into view.
His white robes were stained with blood and filth from unknown owners. His skin was so starkly white that pallid was the only word for it.
“...Baeksang.”
Baeksang answered in a dry voice.
“How dare a mere warrior casually speak the name of the Great Chieftain?”
“What happened to my lord?”
“You’ll find out soon enough.”
Swish. Papapat!
Baeksang flicked his blood-soaked sleeve. In an instant, more than a hundred Bai warriors emerged from the darkness and surrounded them.
Damn it.
Wonhu cursed inwardly and drew the broad-bladed saber tucked into his waist.
He glanced up. Clouds covered the moon tonight, of all nights. It was a poor night to die, but the darkness was a blessing in one respect.
The fugitives would have the advantage if anyone gave chase.
Please be alive. Both of you.
There was only one thing left to do.
Wonhu—or rather, all of them—raised their weapons and charged toward the enemy without hesitation.
Their roar was too great for fear to find a place among them.
Whoooooosh!
Cold wind swept over me as the landscape raced past. No people. None of the houses with their unusual shapes. Only thickets.
We had left the Outer Palace behind.
But we’re still in the Nanman Beast Palace’s territory. We can’t slow down.

We might have to run without stopping until we rescued the Fire Dragon Pavilion members in the reconnaissance squad. The Nanman Beast Palace’s reach covered this entire unfamiliar land of forests, plains, jungles, and swamps.
“Sorry, but I need you to keep going a little longer.”
Grrr.
Yayul Mok was right: the White Tiger really was a spiritual creature. It seemed to understand me even over the rushing wind. With a low growl, it picked up speed.
Papapapat!
Its master, tied to its back, was probably another reason it listened to me so well.
I watched Yayul Mok sway gently with each bound and sighed.
Yayul Mok.
We had made it out of the Outer Palace, but I hadn’t woken him. More accurately, I hadn’t been able to bring myself to try.
If he wakes up, he’ll find some way to go back.
If he did, everything would be for nothing. Abandoning the one escape route they had risked their lives to open would mean nothing but pointless deaths.
Given his position, they probably wouldn’t try to execute him on the spot the way they intended to execute me... but if he wanted to go back, I would stop him.
For Yayul Mok. For the Miao warriors fighting for him. And for the Fire Dragon Pavilion members.
They could call me selfish. They could curse me and point fingers, say I cared only about my own life.
But as fucked up as it was, this was the best choice I had.
Damn it.
I bit down hard on my lip.
Within a day at most—perhaps half a day—a net over heaven and earth would be cast across Nanman. We had to get as far away as we could and find the reconnaissance squad before then.
The two tribal chieftains leading the squad are effectively loyal to the Beast Miao King. We might be able to rescue the three of them without much of a fight.
That was the best outcome I could imagine.

With Dark Heaven’s intervention and Baeksang’s betrayal now certain, and with me having become the star of a massacre that had never been in the cards for me, no one could predict what variables might arise.
First, get every Fire Dragon Pavilion member out. After that...
My thoughts broke off.
Rustle.
The White Tiger stopped dead. It had been running at the front without a moment’s hesitation, but now it would not take another step.
“What? What’s wrong?”
Grrr.
“Your master said to keep going northwest, so...”
Grrrr. Sniff, sniff.
What?
It looked in two directions, one after the other. Then it buried its nose in my hand and sniffed, just as it had before we set out.
Wait. Could it be?
At that moment—
Ding!
System A Sudden Quest, Yohi’s Tracking Scent, has been generated!
As the Quest notification rang in my ears, I remembered the scent pouch I had found at Yohi’s Western Yao Estate.

Long enough to walk through the past several decades, year by year, and watch the newborn who had cried in the arms of his mother, dead from childbirth, grow into a fine young man.

When his tightly closed lips finally parted, he already had his answer.
“You’ll regret this.”
The Beast Miao King asked calmly, “What will I regret?

Or rescuing Jin Taekyung and the other Han Chinese?”
“Everything that has happened until now.”

“It’s different.”
Baeksang’s expression hardened.
“Unlike me, you still have a chance, Palace Lord.
One last chance to undo your mistake.”
“One last chance...”
“If you leave quietly now, I’ll forget everything I saw and heard here.
As though none of it happened.”
“How can I cover the sky with the palm of my hand?
I knew what I was risking when I told you to spare the men guarding the underground prison.”
“If I order them to keep silent, they will.
The Bai people are no less loyal to me than the Seven Miao Tigers are to you.”
“Is that... the last kindness you can offer me as my sworn brother?”
Baeksang nodded without a word.
The Beast Miao King gave him a sorrowful smile.
“Then let me ask you one more time, on the strength of that last kindness.
Half a shichen.
Open a path for them, even if only for half a shichen.”
“Palace Lord!”
“Even if I could turn back, I wouldn’t.
That’s the one difference between us, after a lifetime together.”
The corners of Baeksang’s eyes trembled.
More than anything, he wanted to tell the Beast Miao King he was wrong.
That unlike him, Baeksang had seen only one path ahead and had had no choice but to walk it.

Click.
Shing.
The cold scrape of metal cut through the brief silence.
The Beast Miao King’s gaze deepened as he looked at Baeksang, sword lowered at his side.
“So that’s your choice?”
“I can’t help it, Palace Lord.
Right now... it’s the best I can do.”
“It’s much better not to hear that awkward formal speech.
It feels as though we’ve gone back to the old days.”
“You know as well as I do, Palace Lord.
We can never go back to those days.”
“Do you think so?”
“Of course.”
The Beast Miao King smiled faintly at his firm answer.
Baeksang had made his decision.
He did not hesitate.
Tssssss!
Dazzling light flooded the space around them.
A vast concentration of qi known as Sword Force descended toward its target.
Slice!
Three tigers ran like the wind, led by the snow-white White Tiger.
Wonhu, the eldest of the Seven Miao Tigers, watched their backs disappear into the darkness and muttered,
“Damn, they’re fast.”
That was the entirety of his impression.
Those who were leaving had left.
Those who remained had stayed.
He and the others had chosen to stay.
“Heh heh.”
Wonhu laughed, feeling strangely relieved, and pulled a gourd from his robes.
Pop.
The scent of liquor spread the instant he pulled the stopper.
The eyes of the nearby Miao warriors lit up.
“Oh-ho.”
“That smells incredible.
Did you brew it yourself, Big Brother?”
“Hell, did they round up nothing but a pack of fucking mutts?
Why are all your noses so sharp?”
He grumbled, but his eyes were smiling.
With a look of helpless resignation, Wonhu passed the gourd to the men crowding around him.
“There isn’t much.
Take turns and have a little each.”
“I swear, not a drop will make it back to your mouth, Big Brother.”
“Now this I can’t pass up.”
The Miao warriors roared with laughter and took turns tipping back the gourd.
Nanman people were famous for their love of liquor.
With twenty grown men sharing it, their boast that they would leave nothing behind sounded entirely plausible.
But...
“Ahh, that’s good.
Your turn, Big Brother.
I left you a few drops out of courtesy.”
Wonhu took the gourd at last and let out a short laugh.
Slosh.
One light shake told him enough.
It was not even half empty.
The men stood there shamelessly praising the liquor, and he couldn’t help laughing again.

You’re just a pack of blowhards.”
“Hm?
What’s that supposed to mean?”
“Has senility caught up with you already?
You’re only in your fifties.”
“Enough nonsense.
Drink.”

Trickle.

chapters.title: Chapter 671
paragraphs: The place where I currently found myself—the Murim—had neither the dazzling scientific civilization nor the mechanical engineering of the modern world. Nor did it have magic.
But extraordinary things were woven into this world—things no less remarkable than magic.

Murim people accumulated internal energy and wielded power beyond that of Hunters. There were countless martial arts unknown to the modern world, along with mysterious, bizarre spiritual creatures and elixirs.
And... tracking scent was one of those things.
Ding.
System A Sudden Quest, Yohi’s Tracking Scent, has been generated! Would you like to open the Quest window and check its contents? Y / N
The System notification caught me off guard. Almost entranced, I nodded.
Ding.

System Quest Yohi’s Tracking Scent A new path has appeared before you as you flee from pursuit. Now you must choose once again. You cannot know what awaits at the end of either path. There will only be the consequences of your choice—and the responsibility that comes with it. Grade: Supreme Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: Choose a direction to travel (Incomplete) Reward: Linked Quest ??? Failure: ???
Goddamn it. What is this now?
A holographic window filled the air before me. At the same time, a memory from barely a day ago flashed through my mind.
“Looks like they really went at it.”
“By the time I received the report, everything was already over. All that remained at the Western Yao Estate was blood and corpses. And... those things.”
I remembered everything from that day clearly. It was the only clue left behind by Heugung and Yohi, the two Great Chieftains who had vanished without a trace.
Heugung left a severed wrist, and Yohi...
That was right. She had left a scent pouch.

But I had only just arrived at the Western Yao Estate, and I’d focused on Heugung’s wrist instead. The marks on the severed end might tell me something about his opponent’s martial arts and how skilled they were.
Yohi’s scent pouch didn’t seem nearly as important.
It wasn’t even intact. The silk had a long tear in it, and the scent seemed to have escaped, leaving the pouch almost odorless.
I hadn’t known. With everything that happened afterward, none of us had time to give it another thought.
It was the most important clue at the Western Yao Estate: tracking scent Yohi had left so someone could find her.
The scent hadn’t escaped. It was like that from the start.
As far as I knew, tracking scent was an unusual object made for following someone’s trail, just as its name suggested.
It wasn’t something you came across often, but that didn’t mean no one used it. Among the orthodox faction, there were the Lower District Sect and the Beggars’ Sect, for example.

And the fact that I had spent quite a lot of time with the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect—a man from an organization of truly enormous scale—and exchanged all kinds of stories with him had been an unexpected stroke of luck.
“Tracking scent, huh? It works, but it’s incredibly rare. The method of making it is a closely guarded secret, and only a handful of people in Murim can produce it.”
“Like the Ten-Thousand-Li Tracking Scent?”
“The Ten-Thousand-Li Tracking Scent? Hm. I suppose even you’ve picked up a thing or two.”
“About five of your teeth are going to fall out in a minute. Want me to pick those up for you, too?”
“Ah. Well...”
“Go on. Run your mouth some more.”
“Ahem. The truth is, I’ve never seen the Ten-Thousand-Li Tracking Scent myself. Ten thousand li sounds impressive, but would any scent really last over a journey that long?”
“What? So it was a scam after all?”
“Not necessarily. The Ten-Thousand-Li Tracking Scent you’ve heard rumors about aside, Murim uses quite a few kinds of tracking scent. The finest is commonly called the Thousand-Li Tracking Scent.”
“The Thousand-Li Tracking Scent?”

“It has several distinguishing features. First, the manufacturing process is disgustingly difficult. Second, the manufacturing cost is disgustingly high. Third, acquiring the Thousand-Li Tracking Scent made that way requires a disgustingly large amount of gold.”
“No mistaking you for a fucking beggar. You can’t get through a sentence without working ‘filthy’ in somewhere.”

“However filthy I am, your character is... Sorry. That was out of line. Anyway, tracking scent of that quality is worth dozens of times its weight in gold. Of course, it works just as well as you’d expect.”
“For example?”

“Unlike the unverified Ten-Thousand-Li Tracking Scent, its scent really does last for about a thousand li. And it’s almost odorless—so faint that even some beasts with extraordinarily keen noses can’t detect it. Humans certainly can’t.”
“Then couldn’t you just put tracking scent on someone and call it a day?”

“The trade-off is that tracking scent lasts for seven days and nights at most. If the target burns their clothes or fully immerses themselves in water, for example, the duration will be shortened even if the scent doesn’t disappear entirely.”
“Even so, you’d have to know you’d been marked with tracking scent before you could try any of that. You said that even most beasts can’t smell it properly.”
“True. But spiritual creatures are different.”
“Ah.”
“So there are only two ways to follow a target marked with tracking scent. You need either someone trained in advanced tracking arts or a spiritual creature with a nose keen enough to smell it.”
Remembering that conversation with Gung Gibang, I had to admit he’d been right about all of it.
Grrr. Sniff, sniff.
A damp nose pressed against my palm, twitching with every sniff. I looked down at the White Tiger licking my fingers. Its rough tongue stung a little.
“...Right. You’re here.”
A spiritual creature capable of smelling tracking scent. Just as Gung Gibang had said.
This White Tiger—Muyaho—was even a spiritual creature intelligent enough to understand and communicate with humans from a young age.
The intelligence of a spiritual creature, and senses sharper than any ordinary beast’s.

Looking back, the nearly odorless scent pouch had probably contained Thousand-Li Tracking Scent: the finest kind, said to last seven days and nights as long as the target stayed within a thousand li, barring unusual circumstances.
The two other tigers, standing there waiting blankly while Muyaho sniffed my hand, made the difference plain enough.
Grrr. Grrr.
Muyaho gave a low growl, as if asking me which way to go. His great snow-white head kept turning between two directions.
One was northwest, where the reconnaissance squad had gone.
The other—
...Southeast.
Crack.
I’d clenched my fist without realizing it. It trembled. Taishan watched me, blinking his huge eyes.
“Pavilion Master. What’s wrong?”
It’s nothing. Nothing’s wrong, so let’s just keep going.
My lips parted, but no words came out.
Fuck.
The curse I couldn’t bring myself to say hung in my mouth.

There was no reason to hesitate. Our route was already set, and the beasts were faster than I’d expected. Even if the net over heaven and earth went up right after dawn, in my current condition I thought I could find a way out of Nanman.
So why was I hesitating?
What happens if I leave Nanman with them now? What comes after that?
I already knew the answer. Maybe I’d known since the moment I climbed onto the White Tiger’s back.
Even if I come back... I’ll be too late.
Shaking off our pursuers and breaking through Baeksang’s net over heaven and earth would take days, even if we went as fast as we could. Add the journey back, and it would be seven days and nights.
Would the people who had set out to rescue us still be alive by then?
No. If this incident had even put the Beast Miao King in danger, would Dark Heaven have any reason to hesitate before carrying out its sinister scheme?
They’ll die. Dozens. Hundreds. Maybe even thousands of people.
I blinked slowly. Eyes closed or open, the world was still dark. There was no sign of dawn.
Fuck. It was like this when I first got to boot camp.
The sudden thought made me let out a hollow laugh.
Thinking back, boot camp might have been the easiest time of all. Back then, I could fuck up as badly as I liked and still be forgiven. Things had changed.

I’d come close to death more times than I could count. I’d survived after leaving dying comrades behind. I’d shut myself in my room for days and bawled like an idiot, swearing I’d never lose my people again.
Then one day, I gained the System. When I came to my senses and looked around, I found myself with a great deal to be responsible for.
Everything happening in the world felt like it was my fault, and I pitied the innocent people losing their lives in the process.
Each time, I thought the same thing.
What if I’d been there?
Now all I could do was laugh at myself. Those thoughts felt like a sham—like I’d been playing dress-up, trying to look like a hero.
That was right.
I wasn’t a heroic martial artist. I wasn’t the hero of some superhero movie.
But today, the people who had watched me flee until the very end were true heroic martial artists—true heroes.
“No need to thank us.”
Of course. Nanman was only repaying the debt it owed you.
“My hyung was on Ailao Mountain. Thanks to you, I’ll get to see him again.”
“Please look after the Young Palace Lord.”
Dozens of faces brushed through the darkness. Some belonged to young men, others to graying middle-aged men.
How skilled were they? If I set my mind to it, I could bring every one of them down within moments.
That only made what they’d done more remarkable. They hadn’t stayed to win. They’d stayed to die.
Even if it was an egg striking a stone, they wouldn’t retreat. They would hurl their bodies against the solid rock, even if they were ultimately smashed to pieces.
Maybe that’s happening right now.
And I... had left them behind. I’d sensed what awaited them, yet I’d gone anyway, clinging to an empty promise that I would return.
Haa.
The air had been muggy a moment ago. Now a deep breath sent a white cloud from my mouth.
Nanman really was a fucking awful place. Just like my mood.
System Select a Quest mission.
I stared silently at the holographic window. Then I spoke.
“Taishan.”
“Hm?”
“From now on...”
At what I said next, Taishan’s eyes widened.
The old man opened his eyes without warning.
How long had he been unconscious? His joints ached, and he was tied to the back of a huge beast that bounced beneath him without pause.
A tiger?
His gaze darted around. Namho realized Yayul Mok’s plan had succeeded. Then he noticed something strange.
“...Why? Why isn’t that bastard here?”
At the old man’s voice, filled with confusion, Taishan turned his head.
“Namho. You awake?”
Namho didn’t answer. A terrible feeling pressed against his chest.
“Where is he?”
“...Namho.”
“Where is he? Where’s Jin Taekyung, that bastard?”
The eastern sky was beginning to brighten, but Taishan’s expression darkened.
Namho knew then that his fear hadn’t been unfounded.
