As far as I knew, tracking scent was an unusual object made for following someone’s trail, just as its name suggested.
It wasn’t something you came across often, but that didn’t mean no one used it.
Among the orthodox faction, there were the Lower District Sect and the Beggars’ Sect, for example.

And the fact that I had spent quite a lot of time with the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect—a man from an organization of truly enormous scale—and exchanged all kinds of stories with him had been an unexpected stroke of luck.
“Tracking scent, huh?
It works, but it’s incredibly rare.
The method of making it is a closely guarded secret, and only a handful of people in Murim can produce it.”
“Like the Ten-Thousand-Li Tracking Scent?”
“The Ten-Thousand-Li Tracking Scent?
Hm.
I suppose even you’ve picked up a thing or two.”
“About five of your teeth are going to fall out in a minute.
Want me to pick those up for you, too?”
“Ah.
Well...”
“Go on.
Run your mouth some more.”
“Ahem.
The truth is, I’ve never seen the Ten-Thousand-Li Tracking Scent myself.
Ten thousand li sounds impressive, but would any scent really last over a journey that long?”
“What?
So it was a scam after all?”
“Not necessarily.
The Ten-Thousand-Li Tracking Scent you’ve heard rumors about aside, Murim uses quite a few kinds of tracking scent.
The finest is commonly called the Thousand-Li Tracking Scent.”
“The Thousand-Li Tracking Scent?”
“It has several distinguishing features.
First, the manufacturing process is disgustingly difficult.
Second, the manufacturing cost is disgustingly high.
Third, acquiring the Thousand-Li Tracking Scent made that way requires a disgustingly large amount of gold.”
“No mistaking you for a fucking beggar.
You can’t get through a sentence without working ‘filthy’ in somewhere.”
“However filthy I am, your character is...
Sorry.
That was out of line.
Anyway, tracking scent of that quality is worth dozens of times its weight in gold.
Of course, it works just as well as you’d expect.”
“For example?”
“Unlike the unverified Ten-Thousand-Li Tracking Scent, its scent really does last for about a thousand li.
And it’s almost odorless—so faint that even some beasts with extraordinarily keen noses can’t detect it.
Humans certainly can’t.”
“Then couldn’t you just put tracking scent on someone and call it a day?”
“The trade-off is that tracking scent lasts for seven days and nights at most.
If the target burns their clothes or fully immerses themselves in water, for example, the duration will be shortened even if the scent doesn’t disappear entirely.”
“Even so, you’d have to know you’d been marked with tracking scent before you could try any of that.
You said that even most beasts can’t smell it properly.”
“True.
But spiritual creatures are different.”
“Ah.”
“So there are only two ways to follow a target marked with tracking scent.
You need either someone trained in advanced tracking arts or a spiritual creature with a nose keen enough to smell it.”
Remembering that conversation with Gung Gibang, I had to admit he’d been right about all of it.
Grrr.
Sniff, sniff.
A damp nose pressed against my palm, twitching with every sniff.
I looked down at the White Tiger licking my fingers.
Its rough tongue stung a little.
“...Right.
You’re here.”
A spiritual creature capable of smelling tracking scent.
Just as Gung Gibang had said.
This White Tiger—Muyaho—was even a spiritual creature intelligent enough to understand and communicate with humans from a young age.
The intelligence of a spiritual creature, and senses sharper than any ordinary beast’s.

Looking back, the nearly odorless scent pouch had probably contained Thousand-Li Tracking Scent: the finest kind, said to last seven days and nights as long as the target stayed within a thousand li, barring unusual circumstances.
The two other tigers, standing there waiting blankly while Muyaho sniffed my hand, made the difference plain enough.
Grrr.
Grrr.
Muyaho gave a low growl, as if asking me which way to go.
His great snow-white head kept turning between two directions.
One was northwest, where the reconnaissance squad had gone.
The other—
...Southeast.
Crack.
I’d clenched my fist without realizing it.
It trembled.
Taishan watched me, blinking his huge eyes.
“Pavilion Master.
What’s wrong?”
It’s nothing.
Nothing’s wrong, so let’s just keep going.
My lips parted, but no words came out.
Fuck.
The curse I couldn’t bring myself to say hung in my mouth.
There was no reason to hesitate.
Our route was already set, and the beasts were faster than I’d expected.
Even if the net over heaven and earth went up right after dawn, in my current condition I thought I could find a way out of Nanman.
So why was I hesitating?
What happens if I leave Nanman with them now?
What comes after that?
I already knew the answer.
Maybe I’d known since the moment I climbed onto the White Tiger’s back.
Even if I come back...
I’ll be too late.
Shaking off our pursuers and breaking through Baeksang’s net over heaven and earth would take days, even if we went as fast as we could.
Add the journey back, and it would be seven days and nights.
Would the people who had set out to rescue us still be alive by then?
No.
If this incident had even put the Beast Miao King in danger, would Dark Heaven have any reason to hesitate before carrying out its sinister scheme?
They’ll die.
Dozens.
Hundreds.
Maybe even thousands of people.
I blinked slowly.
Eyes closed or open, the world was still dark.
There was no sign of dawn.
Fuck.
It was like this when I first got to boot camp.
The sudden thought made me let out a hollow laugh.
Thinking back, boot camp might have been the easiest time of all.
Back then, I could fuck up as badly as I liked and still be forgiven.
Things had changed.
I’d come close to death more times than I could count.
I’d survived after leaving dying comrades behind.
I’d shut myself in my room for days and bawled like an idiot, swearing I’d never lose my people again.
Then one day, I gained the System.
When I came to my senses and looked around, I found myself with a great deal to be responsible for.
Everything happening in the world felt like it was my fault, and I pitied the innocent people losing their lives in the process.
Each time, I thought the same thing.
What if I’d been there?
Now all I could do was laugh at myself.
Those thoughts felt like a sham—like I’d been playing dress-up, trying to look like a hero.
That was right.
I wasn’t a heroic martial artist.
I wasn’t the hero of some superhero movie.
But today, the people who had watched me flee until the very end were true heroic martial artists—true heroes.
“No need to thank us.”
Of course.
Nanman was only repaying the debt it owed you.
“My hyung was on Ailao Mountain.
Thanks to you, I’ll get to see him again.”
“Please look after the Young Palace Lord.”
Dozens of faces brushed through the darkness.
Some belonged to young men, others to graying middle-aged men.
How skilled were they?
If I set my mind to it, I could bring every one of them down within moments.
That only made what they’d done more remarkable.
They hadn’t stayed to win.
They’d stayed to die.
Even if it was an egg striking a stone, they wouldn’t retreat.
They would hurl their bodies against the solid rock, even if they were ultimately smashed to pieces.
Maybe that’s happening right now.
And I... had left them behind.
I’d sensed what awaited them, yet I’d gone anyway, clinging to an empty promise that I would return.
Haa.
The air had been muggy a moment ago.
Now a deep breath sent a white cloud from my mouth.
Nanman really was a fucking awful place.
Just like my mood.
System Select a Quest mission.
I stared silently at the holographic window.
Then I spoke.
“Taishan.”
“Hm?”
“From now on...”
At what I said next, Taishan’s eyes widened.
The old man opened his eyes without warning.
How long had he been unconscious?
His joints ached, and he was tied to the back of a huge beast that bounced beneath him without pause.
A tiger?
His gaze darted around.
Namho realized Yayul Mok’s plan had succeeded.
Then he noticed something strange.
Why isn’t that bastard here?”
At the old man’s voice, filled with confusion, Taishan turned his head.
“Namho.
You awake?”
Namho didn’t answer.
A terrible feeling pressed against his chest.
“Where is he?”
“...Namho.”
“Where is he?
Where’s Jin Taekyung, that bastard?”
The eastern sky was beginning to brighten, but Taishan’s expression darkened.
Namho knew then that his fear hadn’t been unfounded.

chapters.title: Chapter 672
paragraphs: Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!
The fierce wind rippled the White Tiger’s snowy fur. Gripping Muyaho by the scruff of his neck, I watched the scenery race past.

Thick undergrowth filled the forest, and trees towered over it like giants. A snake hiding between moss-covered rocks glared at us with bright yellow eyes, while a leopard lying flat in the grass and searching for prey spotted the White Tiger and slowly began backing away.
Above it all, the sky was growing brighter.
Already?
I muttered to myself, then realized how much time had passed. We’d escaped the underground prison just after midnight. By my rough calculation, we’d been running nonstop for at least three shichen.
Grrr.
Perhaps that was why the breathing of the White Tiger carrying me—Muyaho—was much rougher than before, and fatigue could be felt in every step he took.
Can’t blame him.

After all my time in Murim, I could say this with confidence: even a Peak Master who knew a movement technique would get varicose veins from running full speed through this godforsaken place for three shichen.

And Muyaho was enormous, even for a tiger. Crossing terrain so rugged that Kim Jeong-ho would have given up on mapmaking must have drained his stamina and worn down his muscles. On top of that, he had me to carry, and I was hardly small.
I wasn’t a veterinarian, but I could tell what condition he was in with my eyes closed.
Only a spiritual creature like him could have lasted this long.
His physical abilities were exceptional, even by the standards of Nanman’s renowned spiritual creatures. But if we kept going like this, he wouldn’t have any strength left when it mattered.
I stroked his neck and whispered, “Let’s stop and rest somewhere nearby.”
—Grrr.
He understood and gave a small nod.
As luck would have it, I could hear running water not far away. We slowed down and soon found a small stream, along with a few animals that had come out early to drink.
Squeal?
Wild boars. Excellent.
I acted on the thought the moment it occurred to me.
Open Inventory. Summon.
I’d stuffed so many things into my Inventory while trying to survive that I was practically a walking armory. I pulled out a cheap iron spear I couldn’t even remember storing and hurled it.
Two large boars dropped before they could make a sound.
Whoosh—thunk!
Squeeeeeal!
They must have been the piglets’ parents. Watching the little ones flee, squealing as they ran, made my heart sink.
“Hoo.”
—Grrr.
Muyaho nodded solemnly. I went on, looking mournful.
“The young ones have more tender meat. I should’ve caught them first.”
What, you little punk?
Ignoring the look he gave me, as if he couldn’t believe I was human, I skinned the boars and skewered them on the spear.
Fwoosh. Crackle.
I used Scorching Yang Qi to start a campfire. As smoke curled upward and the meat began to cook, a short laugh escaped me.
There was no particular reason. Even I had to admit that what I was doing was absurd.
I’ve made an enemy of all Nanman, and here I am throwing a barbecue party.
I knew it was insane. Turning back along the southeastern route toward the heart of Nanman had been insane to begin with.

But every time I thought it through, I came to the same conclusion. Once I’d decided to follow Yohi’s tracking scent, this was the best thing I could do. It was why I’d gone so far as to light a fire barely a hundred li from the Outer Palace.
The more attention I draw here, the better the others’ chances of surviving.

Before leaving, I’d urged Taishan again and again: run without looking back. Persuade the chieftains of the reconnaissance squad’s tribes through Yayul Mok, then use the swift ships of the Water Dragon Stronghold to escape Nanman.
Unlike his usual self, Taishan had fallen silent for a long while. Then he’d spoken.
“Pavilion Master.”
“What?”
“Taishan will go too. Taishan can’t let Pavilion Master go alone.”
Maybe it was because it had been dawn, or maybe because his words had been so unexpected. For that moment, at least, I think I had been rather sentimental too.
But moved as I was, I knew the truth: if even one of them came with me, neither group would be safe.
“Wait with the others. I’ll be back soon.”
“When? How many nights does Taishan have to wait?”
“Who knows? Ten nights or so?”
“Taishan doesn’t like that. Ten nights is too long.”
“Then five.”
“Good. Promise?”
“Yeah. Promise.”
And I’d left them with a promise I wasn’t sure I could keep.
Five nights.
Could I make it back by then? No—could I make it back at all? I honestly didn’t know.
The Logout function was still blocked, even after my escape from the underground prison. By now, countless Nanman people who had become my enemies were probably closing in from every direction.
Maybe...
Rustle.
Yes. Even now.
—Grrr.
Muyaho had been drooling over the browning meat, but now a low growl rose from his throat. I calmed him as he bristled at the intruders and sharpened my senses.
New information flowed in through my heightened five senses.
About fifty. I can’t tell which tribe they’re from yet, but they’re all warriors... and they have no beasts with them. Did they leave the beasts behind so they wouldn’t be spotted?
A truckload of beasts wouldn’t have changed the outcome, but their absence did make things easier.
Once I had the lay of things, I slowly turned the spear over the fire.
Sizzle.
Beyond the appetizing sound of roasting meat, the intruders’ hushed conversation reached my ears.
“That’s him. He has the White Tiger Yayul Mok prized so much. It has to be.”
“I’m not sure. I can only see his back from here. Shouldn’t we turn around and ask for reinforcements?”
“Pathetic. Heaven has handed us an opportunity, and you want to give the glory to another tribe? We’ve come this far, and you’re still talking like a coward?”
“B-but, hyung. Even if that man really is the Han Chinese we know about, how are we supposed to deal with a monster like him?”

“Even so, he’s still just a human made of flesh and blood. Judging by the fact that he’s cooking meat here dressed like a beggar, he must have been separated from the others and lost his mind. If we capture him here, we’ll gain not only ten thousand gold, but our father might even become the new Great Chieftain.”
Hm. So that’s it.
I listened a moment longer, brushed off my backside, and stood. As I turned, I asked, “Really? Do I look that bad?”
Even from more than thirty zhang away, I could feel it: the trembling air and the many emotions wrapping around the enemies who had been approaching as stealthily as possible.
Shock. Astonishment. And...
“Attack!”
A rash decision born of stupidity and a vain thirst for glory.
They didn’t know that my clothes were the only thing worse for wear. My body was in peak condition, and I was already hurtling toward them.
Whoooosh!
My body surged forward like a streak of light. Wind whipped up like a gale, and the thick grass burst apart.
Through the leaves shattering and scattering in every direction, I saw eyes filled with terror.
“What’s everyone doing? Aren’t you going to finish drawing your weapons?”
Despite my helpful advice, their hands froze around weapons that weren’t even halfway out. The man in front of them was no different.
“Y-you...”
I feel like I’ve seen this face somewhere.
It didn’t matter right now.
“Why aren’t you attacking?”
“W-what?”
“You said to attack. You came all the way here, and you’re not going to?”
“Th-that’s...”
“You won’t? Then I will.”
I tossed out a single, quiet word.
“Attack.”
A huge shadow fell across the ground.
—Raaaaar!
With a roar, Muyaho leaped over my head and crashed down on the man.
Crack. Craaack!
Someone once said force and oppression were no way to communicate. If you wanted someone to open their mouth, you needed a gentle expression and a kind tone.
They weren’t entirely wrong. Ordinary force and oppression wouldn’t do it. You needed fucking merciless force and oppression.
And, as I was reminded yet again, I had a real talent for that.
“What’s going on inside the Nanman Beast Palace?”
“You bastard! Just kill me!”
“Fine. Muyaho?”
Crunch!
“Gyaaaah!”
“Good boy. Now spit it out.”
Ptooey.
“Urgh. Hic... hiiic.”
“Why are you bawling so pathetically? You’re a grown-ass man.”
“Hic.”
“That was your leg this time, but if you keep crying, I’ll go for your balls next. Do you understand, you fucking bastard?”
“Ghk. Gnnng...!”
“Good. I’ll ask again. What’s going on inside the Nanman Beast Palace?”
The interrogation went quickly and smoothly. Of course, my preparations for it had been thorough.
I broke both arms of the men who came at me late, and the legs of those who tried to run away.
After crippling about twenty of them, I gave Muyaho his one-bite chance. They all became as docile as golden retrievers.
Is that about it?
They might have lied about some things, but what they’d told me had enough supporting detail to treat it as true for now. Besides, people tended to get honest when death was staring them in the face.
Especially when their balls were at stake.
Once the questioning was done, I glanced at the man Muyaho had pounced on first. His body was crushed, and he was barely breathing. When he caught me looking at him, he groaned.
So that’s where I’d seen him.

He was the spitting image of his father, the tribal chieftain. Not that his father was particularly important to me. On the first day of the Tribal Grand Council and on the day of the tragedy at the Western Yao Estate, he’d been nothing more than a sycophant desperate to get behind Baeksang.
But that was also why I was letting him and the others live.
“Go back and tell them.”
At my quiet words, the man’s lips moved. His eyes were full of fear.
“T-tell them what?”
“That I’m here. That I’m watching you from somewhere nearby.”
“Remember everything you heard today. I will.”
The man—and the other Nanman people nearby, who had been watching my every move with all their senses alert—shuddered.

They would probably remember this day for the rest of their lives. My expression, my tone, my voice, my actions—and the warning I’d given them during the interrogation, when I learned that the Miao warriors who’d attacked the underground prison the previous night were still alive.
If you touch them, I’ll kill every one of you. Maybe not today, but tomorrow. Or next year. Perhaps at the very moment you think everything is over and finally let your guard down.
A threat frightened people when they believed it might come true. And in their eyes, I was more than capable of carrying mine out.
The inheritor of the Fire Gate Clan’s legacy. The successor of Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King. An unprecedented monster who had shaken the entire world at only around twenty years of age.
That was enough.
Today I’d carved a fear into their bones that they would never forget. Now it would spread among the Nanman people on Baeksang’s side.
Quickly. Farther and farther.
Until no tribe dared harm the Miao warriors.
With Baeksang still there, I couldn’t guarantee their safety. But this was the best I could do for them right now.
“Leave at once. Unless you want to die here.”

A little later, from the branch of a giant tree, I watched some fifty pale-faced figures leave the forest. They fled in a panic, as though they’d seen a ghost. I watched until the last of them was gone, then slowly drew up three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi.
Fwoosh.
Flames gathered in both my hands.
It was time to light a beacon that would draw the net over heaven and earth toward me. A bright beacon with an entire forest for kindling.
Fwoosh. Whooom!
As I watched the horrifying heat and flames spread in every direction and devour the forest, a thought suddenly occurred to me.
Old Master would curse me out if he saw this.
I let out a quiet laugh and turned away from the blazing forest.
Ahead of me, Muyaho was already running energetically with a half-charred piece of wild boar meat clenched in his mouth.

Of course, my preparations for it had been thorough.
I broke both arms of the men who came at me late, and the legs of those who tried to run away.
After crippling about twenty of them, I gave Muyaho his one-bite chance.
They all became as docile as golden retrievers.
Is that about it?
They might have lied about some things, but what they’d told me had enough supporting detail to treat it as true for now.
Besides, people tended to get honest when death was staring them in the face.
Especially when their balls were at stake.
Once the questioning was done, I glanced at the man Muyaho had pounced on first.
His body was crushed, and he was barely breathing.
When he caught me looking at him, he groaned.
So that’s where I’d seen him.
He was the spitting image of his father, the tribal chieftain.
Not that his father was particularly important to me.
On the first day of the Tribal Grand Council and on the day of the tragedy at the Western Yao Estate, he’d been nothing more than a sycophant desperate to get behind Baeksang.
But that was also why I was letting him and the others live.
“Go back and tell them.”
At my quiet words, the man’s lips moved.
His eyes were full of fear.
“T-tell them what?”
“That I’m here.
That I’m watching you from somewhere nearby.”
“Remember everything you heard today.
I will.”
The man—and the other Nanman people nearby, who had been watching my every move with all their senses alert—shuddered.
They would probably remember this day for the rest of their lives.

My expression, my tone, my voice, my actions—and the warning I’d given them during the interrogation, when I learned that the Miao warriors who’d attacked the underground prison the previous night were still alive.
If you touch them, I’ll kill every one of you.
Maybe not today, but tomorrow.
Or next year.
Perhaps at the very moment you think everything is over and finally let your guard down.
A threat frightened people when they believed it might come true.
And in their eyes, I was more than capable of carrying mine out.
The inheritor of the Fire Gate Clan’s legacy.
The successor of Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King.
An unprecedented monster who had shaken the entire world at only around twenty years of age.
That was enough.
Today I’d carved a fear into their bones that they would never forget.
Now it would spread among the Nanman people on Baeksang’s side.
Quickly.
Farther and farther.
Until no tribe dared harm the Miao warriors.
With Baeksang still there, I couldn’t guarantee their safety.
But this was the best I could do for them right now.
“Leave at once.
Unless you want to die here.”
A little later, from the branch of a giant tree, I watched some fifty pale-faced figures leave the forest.
They fled in a panic, as though they’d seen a ghost.
I watched until the last of them was gone, then slowly drew up three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi.
Fwoosh.
Flames gathered in both my hands.
It was time to light a beacon that would draw the net over heaven and earth toward me.
A bright beacon with an entire forest for kindling.
Fwoosh.
Whooom!
As I watched the horrifying heat and flames spread in every direction and devour the forest, a thought suddenly occurred to me.
Old Master would curse me out if he saw this.
I let out a quiet laugh and turned away from the blazing forest.
Ahead of me, Muyaho was already running energetically with a half-charred piece of wild boar meat clenched in his mouth.

chapters.title: Chapter 673
paragraphs: For the first time since the Great Faction War, the world had entered a period of upheaval.
It reached the Central Plains, the so-called center of the world, and distant Nanman, thousands of li away.
“Gasp, pant... Did everyone hear the news?”
“Catch your breath first. What happened this time?”
New rumors spread every day, and the people of Nanman no longer reacted with the shock they had at first.
Or rather, they thought nothing could surprise them anymore.
They had reason to think so. In the past month or so, they had endured one shock after another—more than every incident in Nanman since the end of the Great Faction War combined.
A Miao village massacred by Han Chinese.
The sudden attack of a Thousand-Year Spider from Ailao Mountain, which had been quiet for decades.

And a young Han Chinese man who had not only entered the Inner Palace—a first in the history of the Nanman Beast Palace—but had attended the Tribal Grand Council, where only thirty-two tribal chieftains were permitted to sit.
If it had ended there, perhaps things would have been bearable.

But just three days ago, more than a hundred Yao warriors had been brutally killed at the Western Yao Estate, and two Great Chieftains of immense symbolic importance had gone missing. After that, events began to move with the force of a torrent.
The culprit! The culprit behind the Western Yao Estate incident has been revealed! It was that young Han Chinese man! Jin Taekyung!
Wait. Have you forgotten that Jin Taekyung saved the warriors at Ailao Mountain the day before? Nothing’s been proven yet. We shouldn’t rush to judgment...
Too soon? Ever since those Han Chinese bastards came here, nothing but bad things have happened. There’s no reason to wait any longer!
He’s right!
Only reason could overcome anger, but the voices of those few people were helplessly buried beneath the shouts of many Nanman people whose reason had already gone numb.
Drag the Han Chinese into the street and tear them limb from limb!
Great Chieftain Baeksang! Make sure those bastards are punished!
The music and laughter that filled the streets whenever the Tribal Grand Council convened were gone.
Angry shouts rang out on every side, and two names came up again and again.
Jin Taekyung. And Baeksang.
Their standing differed as much as their origins, ages, and names. To the people of Nanman, that was only natural.

One was an outsider from the distant Central Plains—a criminal who had committed a tragedy that could never be forgiven. The other was the Great Chieftain who led the Bai people, the strongest tribe in this land after the Miao people.

The Nanman people still respected and loved their Palace Lord. His martial prowess was renowned throughout the world, and he was an unpretentious man. But after what had happened at the Western Yao Estate, their trust in him could not help but falter.
After all, it was none other than the Palace Lord, Yayul Cheok, who had brought the Han Chinese responsible for every recent misfortune into the Inner Palace.
Yet even those who had cheered for Great Chieftain Baeksang could not help but become flustered when they heard the new rumors that emerged at daybreak.
“W-What did you say?”
“Did I... Did I hear that wrong?”
Their pupils trembled, and their faces were filled with bewilderment.
Everyone who heard the news could only keep repeating the unbelievable story in their minds, wearing the same expression and the same look in their eyes.
The Palace Lord... tried to harm Great Chieftain Baeksang last night, failed, and then fled?
At first, they all thought it was a ridiculous false rumor. The Palace Lord they knew—the Great Chieftain of the Miao people, Yayul Cheok—was not that kind of person.
Before he was a fine Palace Lord, he was a good man, born in this land and more devoted to Nanman than anyone.
But the news that followed was enough to plunge the beliefs and questions of the Nanman people into an abyss.
“Baeksang is taking over as temporary Palace Lord? What does that mean?”
“I-I don’t know. But the Inner Palace put up a notice. It says just what we heard.”
“That’s absurd! How could it be true?”

“That’s not all. Apparently, the Palace Lord even mobilized the Young Palace Lord and dozens of elite warriors under his command to raid the underground prison and release the culprit, Jin Taekyung, along with the other Han Chinese.”

“I can hardly believe it either, but the circumstances are remarkably clear. It’s an undeniable fact that the Palace Lord has been friendly toward the Han Chinese for a long time. And the whereabouts of Jin Taekyung, the Young Palace Lord, and the other Han Chinese are unknown. The Tribal Grand Council was convened last night, and they apparently declared this a betrayal against all of Nanman and issued a general mobilization order.”
“What? A general mobilization order?”

“That’s right. I heard it was decided along with the matter of the temporary Palace Lord. They must intend to hunt down and execute the rebels who have thrown Nanman into chaos. Naturally, the highest-priority targets are the Han Chinese Jin Taekyung and the Palace Lord. No—the former Palace Lord.”
“Former Palace Lord? What are you saying?”
“I don’t know. I’m still trying to make sense of it. But how would ordinary tribespeople like us know what really happened? All we can do is follow the Tribal Grand Council’s decision.”
The notice, bearing the unmistakable seal of the Inner Palace, spread through Nanman in no time. Its people split into three groups.
Those who believed the Beast Miao King had betrayed them. Those who refused to believe it.
And those who made no effort to question it or seek the truth, accepting the new reality as it was presented to them.
Amid the confusion, some fifty warriors returned through the West Gate to the Outer Palace. Every one of them was injured, some worse than others.
They trembled like aspens, terror etched into their faces. In their unsteady eyes lingered the image of the enormous fire they had seen from ten li away.
“Mon... monster...”
The voice that escaped someone’s lips sounded frozen despite the fierce sunlight pouring down overhead.
It was around noon.
Baeksang studied his reflection in a large mirror.

He was handsome and youthful, with a balanced build that belied his more than seventy years. His clothes were made of pure white fox fur. A stranger might have admired his bearing and taken him for the ruler of a kingdom.
But Baeksang’s gaze remained fixed on his own coldly hardened face.
Have I looked like this all along? For so many years?
He searched the past several decades and could not remember the last time he had laughed from the heart.
All he could do was draw out a memory long covered in dust and look at it once more.
Yes. That was the last time.
The chill in his eyes softened as a particular day came back to him.
They had won a hard-fought battle and been given a few precious days of rest.

The bold boy who had set out after his father, determined to defeat the Demonic Cult, had already grown into a handsome young man. And the girl who had been lively since childhood—and therefore always covered in scrapes and bruises—had grown into a beautiful woman.
The young man was Hwi. The woman was Hyang.

The two of them were as radiant and fragrant as their names. They were a pair of flowers that had bloomed amid a battlefield overflowing with blood and death. Though they called each other dog-and-monkey enemies despite having grown up together, they would sometimes walk together while avoiding the eyes of others.
They probably never knew that someone had been watching on the night they quietly left the others, who were drunk on victory and wine, to walk together along a hill under faint moonlight.
...You’re here again?
...Why are you here again, hyung?
Why do you think? I’m keeping an eye on Hwi. That wolf might try something with my delicate, beautiful Hyang.
I have to ask—do you honestly believe that?
Of course I’m serious.
Then you know Little Tide Demon died in the battle three days ago.
Little Tide Demon? That bastard who could slap the Heavenly Demon across the face if lust were martial arts?
That’s the one.
As a father with a daughter, I’d been meaning to deal with him myself someday. Good riddance. But why bring him up?
That bastard. Hyang killed him.
Hwi was fighting him and took a sword wound. Hyang came out of nowhere with a pair of axes—heaven knows where she found them—and split Little Tide Demon’s head open.

And apparently, that still didn’t satisfy her. She crushed the dead bastard’s balls, hurled every curse imaginable at him, and hacked his corpse to pieces. In Hwi’s words, it looked like an imperial palace chef mincing meat with uncanny skill.
...You’re lying. My Hyang would never do that.
Five people saw it besides Hwi. Three of them still can’t speak from the shock.
Good. Tell them to keep their mouths shut. Otherwise, I might have to shut them myself... Oh. No.
You sound like a fiend... Gasp.
That day, the sworn brothers crouching far away in the darkness had unintentionally witnessed it.
The sight of the two children they cherished more dearly than their own lives slowly tilting their heads toward each other.
Turn your head. Quick!
Lower your voice, hyung! I’ve already turned!
Oh, heavens. What did I just see?
What else? Did you leave your eyes in Nanman? They were kissing—mmph. Mmph!
Baeksang, you conniving bastard. You put that wolf of a son up to this, didn’t you? Do you want to be Palace Lord that badly?
Mmph! Hah! Me, Palace Lord? What kind of insane nonsense is that? Maybe after you or I die, but not now.
Ah, I see. You’ll fulfill your dream through your son. Hyang could be the next Palace Lord, so you’ll snatch her up and make her do nothing but housework. Is that it?
You’re driving me mad.
Last chance. Admit it.
No! I said no!
Really? Swear to the heavens.
I swear to the heavens!
Fine. I believe you. Then prepare for them to hold their wedding this year.
How many times must I tell you I don’t— What? What did you just say?
“Don’t ‘what’ me. Just get ready to marry off those two love-struck youngsters.”
Why are you just staring at me with that blank expression? You had already figured it out too. Unless you dislike it?
O-Of course I don’t. You’re right, I’d guessed. But... how do I put it? Huh.

“Then that settles it. No need for a long discussion. If the Western Front stabilizes before winter, let’s have them marry and send them back to Nanman. And although the thought makes me feel strange... if they have a child, those two will give up their stubbornness and return willingly, won’t they?”
A child. Ha... Haha. Has that much time passed already?
You’re younger than I am. Stop acting like an old man. Promise me one thing.
What is it?
That girl Hyang. To me, she is more precious and pitiful than anyone. Because of her worthless father, she lost two older brothers and suffered terribly.
Hyung...
Damn it. What I mean is... Shit.
You can stop. I know what you mean. She’s precious to you, and you want us to treat her that way.
You have nothing to worry about. Hwi will certainly do that. He’ll grow old with her not merely as a woman, but as a companion—and sometimes as a friend.
I suppose I can trust Hwi.
And if you can’t trust Hwi, trust Hyang.
What?
You know her temper. If Hwi disappoints her in the slightest, he’ll end up like Little Tide Demon. I’d bet—!
Baeksang, you bastard! How dare you think of my Hyang as—!
That last shout had been a mistake.
Hwi and Hyang broke apart in the middle of their shy first kiss, and the two sworn brothers fled as fast as their legs could carry them.
Then, when they reached a quiet stream and were about to hurl a word at each other...
Yes. We laughed. Loud enough to shake the world.
Baeksang could no longer remember what had made them laugh so hard. It could not have been only the sight of each other’s panic-stricken faces.

Perhaps they had been happy that the two children who had grown up together would be joined at last—and that they, sworn brothers who had spent their lives side by side, would finally become one family.
Hyang... If she hadn’t gone like that. If only...
Everything might have been different.
But Baeksang knew that the thought was nothing more than a futile wish.
That winter, as they waited for a wedding all Nanman would have celebrated, the Western Front failed to stabilize. Ten thousand Demonic Cult troops swept in with the cold wind.
And then... the flower withered.
After Yayul Hyang—the woman who had been as beautiful as a flower and as strong as steel—withered on the battlefield, the light vanished from Baekhwi’s face.
That must have been why, during the final battle at the Great Snow Mountain, he had cut down enemy after enemy as though possessed, stepping into ever greater danger.
In the years that followed, Baeksang sometimes wondered whether the boy had seen a single flower blooming somewhere in that narrow ravine.
Was that really what happened?
As always, there was no answer.
Baeksang looked at the mirror, now blurred before him.
No. The whole world looked that way.
Drip. Drip.
Not a cloud marked the clear sky. Yet raindrops fell from somewhere.
And then, in the next moment, someone’s voice pierced Baeksang’s ears.
“Oh my. Should I come back later?”
Baeksang turned slowly. In his bloodshot eyes, he saw a woman who had appeared like a ghost.
“...Southern Heaven Demon Empress.”
At Baeksang’s words, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress smiled broadly. It was a smile as radiant as a flower and as wicked as a viper.

chapters.title: Chapter 674
paragraphs: Things happened in this world that defied common sense.
The woman reflected in Baeksang’s bloodshot eyes at this very moment was one of them.
“...Southern Heaven Demon Empress.”
His voice rang softly through the room. They were alone.
The woman—the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—smiled broadly.
“It’s been a while, Great Chieftain Baeksang.”
Her smile was impossibly beautiful—and more bewitching still. Baeksang’s heart sank.
How?
Getting past the tight security was no great surprise. But he had reached the Supreme Peak realm, and he hadn’t sensed her approach at all.

He had first learned of the Southern Heaven Demon Empress more than thirty years ago. Much had changed since the days when grief over his child’s death had driven him half-mad. Yet the gulf between him and that demoness had not narrowed in the slightest. The realization weighed on him.
“...What brings you here?”
At his stiff question, she put on a sulky face.
“Why? Aren’t you happy to see me?”
There was plenty of mischief in her voice, but Baeksang could not afford to lower his guard around her for an instant. He forced himself to remain calm.
“I simply didn’t expect you to come in person. Normally, you would have sent a messenger or left me a secret message.”

The Southern Heaven Demon Empress—or rather, Dark Heaven—had always done things that way. Baeksang was used to meeting black-clad figures whose names and faces were concealed, or finding messages they had left in unexpected places.
And he had never been able to refuse them.
“We agreed to meet again in four days. I would have come to you then. There was no need for you to make the trip.”

He had followed that arrangement for decades. On the first day of every month, he exchanged missives with Dark Heaven between Insi and the hour of the Rabbit. Once every three months, he went to them alone, without telling anyone.
“Three days from now? Oh my, has it been that long already?”
She widened her eyes as if she had completely forgotten. Baeksang felt his fist clench.
“I’m joking. You’re getting worked up? That’s not like you. Our Great Chieftain has a surprisingly cute side.”
“I came for a few reasons. So much has happened lately, and now that you’re finally the ruler of Nanman, I wanted to congratulate you in person. But...”
She covered her mouth and laughed.
“Who would have thought I’d see the cold, calculating Great Chieftain Baeksang in tears? Or should I say, the new Palace Lord?”
The corners of her mouth were lifted, but her gaze had sunk deep. Baeksang felt a chill in his heart before he spoke.
“It was nothing. The mirror brought back an old memory, that’s all.”
“Oh, because you thought of the son who looked exactly like you in the mirror?”
“...I’d rather leave that subject alone. What matters now is the future, not the past.”
“Well, if that’s what our Palace Lord wants. A good attitude.”
She smiled and went on.
“Though I am a little disappointed. I thought my gift had moved you to tears.”
“I’m grateful for the mirror,” Baeksang said stiffly. “I’ve been putting it to good use.”
“Never mind. I went to some trouble to find it as a gift for your appointment as Palace Lord, and now you’re thanking me only because I brought it up.”
She shot him a sidelong glance, then walked slowly to the window. From the Palace Lord’s Hall atop the highest hill in the Inner Palace, she could see countless pavilions and houses below.
“Wow. What a view. I suppose the Palace Lord’s residence ought to be special. You’ll get to see this every day now, won’t you?”
“I’m only the temporary Palace Lord.”
“Temporary... You don’t really believe that, do you?”
“My dear Palace Lord. Why pretend when you know perfectly well?”
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress gave the silent Baeksang a smile with her eyes before turning her gaze toward the view outside.
Sunlight streamed down. A cool breeze blew in from somewhere, and not a cloud marred the blue sky. The first fine day she had seen in some time lifted her spirits.
How could it not? Soon she could stain that clear sky with a darkness that would leave not a single ray of light.
Whoooosh.
Wind poured through the open window, setting her silky hair rippling. She closed her eyes and smiled. Moments later, she spoke.
“You know the great undertaking is entering its final stage, don’t you?”
Her quiet voice made Baeksang’s eyelids tremble. Decades of memories flashed before him, along with one person’s face.
“Of course... I do.”
“Everything is going smoothly. Apart from a few minor problems.”
Baeksang could guess what she meant. The two names she spoke next confirmed it.
“The Beast Miao King. And Jin Taekyung.”
Resting her chin on one hand, she watched the Nanman warriors filing in below.
“Honestly, they’re more than minor problems. One is a Supreme Peak master powerful enough to stand among the Ten Kings. And the other is—yes—that Jin Taekyung.”
Baeksang watched her back. What he had dreaded was finally here. It was probably why she had shown herself after staying out of sight for so long.
“I’m sorry.”
“Sorry? For what?”
“How could I not be? It was clearly my mistake.”
“Hmm.”
She hummed softly, then said, “Yes. But it was our mistake too. I never expected the Beast Miao King to make a move like that. And...”
She glanced over her shoulder at Baeksang’s left arm. Beneath his robe of snow-white fox fur, the sleeve was empty now. It had not been the night before.
“I know our new Palace Lord did make an effort.”
The bleeding had stopped, but the pain from where Force had severed his arm would not fade so quickly. Baeksang bore a fresh throb of it as he answered.
“I couldn’t defeat him. I brought in every soldier waiting nearby, but he broke through the encirclement.”
“He may be the least of the Ten Kings, but he’s still one of them. Then again, perhaps what saved him was... that last bit of affection you still feel for your sworn brother.”
“That...”
“Wasn’t it? Can you deny it outright?”
Baeksang was silent for a moment.
“Perhaps. Yes, perhaps it was. At the very least, I might have been able to buy enough time to pursue him.”
“Do you understand what you’re admitting?”
“Of course. But I can say one thing with certainty: it will never happen again.”
She studied his dark eyes, then let out a light sigh.
“Phew. What a relief.”
“What is?”
“That you told me the truth. If you’d refused to admit it, I was going to tear you limb from limb and kill you before long.”
“I truly am relieved. We haven’t seen each other often, but I’ve grown rather fond of you, Palace Lord.”
She gave him a shy smile, like a young girl.
“You know how, when you see a little ant fall into the water and struggle to stay alive, you find yourself rooting for it? Oh, I don’t mean that you’re an ant. I’m just not very good with words.”
Baeksang felt the blood in his body turn cold. The fear pressing down on him swallowed even his shame and humiliation.
It reminded him how dangerous this woman truly was. To Dark Heaven, he was an easily controlled puppet, an animal on a leash—or something less.
But...
This is the path I chose.
That was the cold truth. Long ago, he had taken the hand the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—Dark Heaven—offered him. In return, he had received hope.
That hope had lifted him from the grief of losing his child and given him a reason to go on living. He could not bring this path to an end himself.
He had climbed onto a tiger’s back. All he could do was ride it onward with all his strength.
Thud.

No one in Nanman would have believed the sight, but it was happening in the Palace Lord’s Hall. The new Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, ruler of all that vast land, had dropped to one knee before a woman who seemed more beautiful than anything in the world.
“Please give me your orders, Demon Empress.”
She looked down at him and smiled languidly in the sunlight from the window.
“This is why I like you.”
She reached toward the open window, as though she meant to seize the Nanman warriors still pouring in under the new Palace Lord’s general mobilization order—and the blue sky above them.
“Three days. Find the Beast Miao King and eliminate him within three days. As for Jin Taekyung...”
Or perhaps she meant to turn it all to darkness at a stroke.
“We’ll deal with him.”

With the great undertaking already nearing its end, she had no doubt: the path opened through Nanman would become a bridgehead into the Central Plains. And at the end of that path awaited the return of the omnipotent Lord of Heaven, ruler of all creation.
I’ll stake Hyuk Mujin’s balls on it.
That was probably a signal fire unlike any in Nanman’s history. Maybe even Murim’s.
Fwoosh. WHOOOM!
Two days had passed since I left the others in Taishan’s care and headed south. I was setting my seventh mountain on fire.
Oh, the pasture too, of course.
“Wait. Is this the seventh or the eighth?”
Grrrr.
“Right. That’s not important.”
I ignored the White Tiger’s annoyed look. Blood and soot had dirtied its once-white fur.
The blood wasn’t its own. After we’d driven off pursuit squads half a dozen times, a little mess was unavoidable.
Soon, though, I wouldn’t hear Muyaho complaining anymore. No—neither of us would have the attention to spare for anything like that.
Step.
The White Tiger planted a huge forepaw in the mud. It had been running like the wind until now, so when it stared into the black forest and let out a low cry, that could mean only one thing.
Yes.
“It’s here.”
I muttered while gazing at the mountain shrouded in darkness.

chapters.title: Chapter 675
paragraphs: I’d thought of this place from the beginning, but I still hadn’t believed it would be here. Nanman was vast, and I was a Korean who didn’t even know the geography of the Central Plains properly.
In fact, of all the martial artists in the world, there probably wasn’t another hybrid quite like me.
An outsider in the Central Plains, for all intents and purposes. And undeniably an outsider in Nanman.
How was someone like me supposed to know exactly where we were headed, or where we would stop?
Besides, Muyaho was a spiritual creature that understood human speech, not one that could speak it.
So when the White Tiger’s pace finally slowed, I realized where we were.
Looks like “no way” really is going to get someone killed. Fuck.
The mountain looked ominous even from a distance.
Ailao Mountain was just as it had been when I left it a few days ago: dark and chilly, with a smell of blood that seemed to drift from beyond the thick fog.
In short, it was the kind of place that made me feel fucking awful every time I came here.
As far as Ailao Mountain was concerned, they ought to invent a character for “dick” and write its name with that instead of the character for “mountain.”
“...Is it really here?”
- Grrr.
“You know I’ll chop your leg off if you’re lying, right?”
- Grrrr!
“Ah. Okay.”
Damn. Guess it really was.
I gently scratched between the White Tiger’s brows to soothe its irritation and looked around.
A wolf howled now and then. Each time, mountain birds took flight with a flutter. Those were the only sounds I heard.
Yeah. At least as far as sound goes.
I checked the Quest window.
The linked Quest that had begun automatically when Muyaho and I split off from the group was short and simple for a Quest with a Grade as high as Supreme Peak.

System Quest I Can See Your Tracking Scent You chose to follow the tracking scent. At the end of the road you are traveling now, may you find what you seek. Grade: Supreme Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: Find Yohi (Incomplete) Reward: ??? Failure: ???
Find Yohi, huh? Of course I had to succeed.
Honestly, though, it didn’t matter to me whether I found Yohi or Heugung.
Quest or no Quest, I had to do this. Those two were among my best chances of thwarting the Southern Heaven Demon Empress and Baeksang’s plans.

From what I’ve learned, no one knows where the Beast Miao King is, and the friendly forces inside the Nanman Beast Palace have effectively lost their power. With so little time left, the best move is to rescue the two Great Chieftains and take them to the Inner Palace.
Did you think I’d made Muyaho run like hell while I sat comfortably on its back enjoying the scenery? I’d thought this through on the way here.
After what happened at the Western Yao Estate, the Nanman Beast Palace considered me the greatest fucking bastard under heaven. If I charged in alone, all that awaited me were spears and blades.
But what if Heugung and Yohi—the very people who’d been abducted—came back alive with me?
That would turn the whole board around. No question.
Words carried different weight depending on who spoke them.
If Great Chieftains from the four tribes came forward to prove my innocence and reveal the truth behind the tragedy, everything happening in Nanman would take a new turn.
That was why I had to complete this Quest, one way or another. It was a brilliant move that could overturn the situation in a single stroke.
Of course...
“Can’t make a brilliant move without a Go stone to play. And getting one won’t be easy.”

I muttered the words like a sigh. Then, sensing people closing in around me from every direction, I added, “So I think I’ll catch a few of you instead of Go stones to start with... Who wants to die first?”
As expected, no one answered. I launched myself forward without hesitation.
Whoosh. Fwoooosh!
Flamefire Path.
Flames rose with my footsteps and became a meteor’s tail, cleaving the darkness.
There were more enemies here than I’d encountered at any point since I began following the tracking scent.
I could see roughly three hundred of them, and there were probably just as many—or more—lying in wait behind the dense grass.
But...
That’s all?
I stood among the predators at the top of Murim’s vast food chain. The enemies surrounding me were nothing more than a helpless flock of sheep.
I could subdue them without sinking my teeth into their necks.
Whoosh, fwoooosh!
I shot forward amid flames that devoured the darkness. Screams erupted from the enemies who realized what was happening half a beat too late.
“H-He’s spotted us!”
“Stop him! He’s com—!”
Kwaaaang!
The shout vanished beneath a thunderous blast.
The ground overturned, and enormous trees tore free by their roots. Dozens of enemies flew in every direction at once, as if they’d agreed to do it together.
“Guh!”
“Aaargh!”
Their tightly packed formation had collapsed. Screams filled the gaps.
As I walked out, brushing dirt from my shoulder, someone shouted, “Put the beasts in front! Attack him from the rear!”
“Oh, you animal-abusing bastard.”
That aside, it wasn’t a bad choice.

Nanman’s way of fighting with beasts had earned its reputation. It was one reason Nanman warriors, despite being individually less skilled than martial artists from the Central Plains, had distinguished themselves in the Great Faction War.
Of course, that only worked when the situation called for it.
Grrrrrrr!
The moment a creature far larger than an ordinary brown bear charged at me with a roar—
Shh-shh-shhik!
A pale blur accompanied by a sharp whistle of displaced air flashed past my side and struck the alpha brown bear in the mouth.
Crack! Crunch!
Drops of blood scattered through the air, and the bear toppled forward.
With a single kitty-paw punch, Muyaho had subdued a beast that might have ranked among the three strongest here. Its eyes gleamed.
Whooosh!
I couldn’t see it, but I could feel it: a chill spreading in every direction.
This is...
Fear.

The White Tiger had been born beyond the bounds of an ordinary beast. As its overwhelming presence bore down on the area, the beasts’ growls vanished, and their bristling tails drooped toward the ground.
Another strange gleam passed through Muyaho’s moonlit blue-white eyes.
- GRAAAAAAWR!
The explosive roar made the air tremble.
The wind surged. Grass and flowers bent low. Pupils dilating, the beasts huddled down and backed away.
And they weren’t the only ones affected.
“Gasp.”
“M-My body...”
Muyaho’s aura fell short of the Water God Dragon’s, or that of some of the monsters I’d encountered. But it was enough to freeze some of the less accomplished martial artists among our enemies.
Which meant, of course, that others could still move.
“You idiots! What are you doing?!”
I heard panic and fury in the shout.
I spotted a middle-aged man wearing a leopard hide well behind the others and shot toward him like a spear.
Shaaak! Crack!
“Aaargh!”
“M-Monster!”
That was right. Here and now, I was the only monster.
Someone they couldn’t stop. Someone they’d imagined in their heads but never once thought they would have to face as an enemy.
Even if every person here stood in my way, I had the strength to keep going.
“Protect the Chieftain!”
“Stop him by any means necessary—guh!”
I tapped an opponent’s chest with my palm.
Scorching Yang Qi seeped into his body and disrupted the flow of his qi. Blood burst from his mouth like a fountain, and he crumpled.
“You bastard! How dare—!”
Whoosh! Tap.
Was the man I’d just taken down a friend of his?
He had plenty of momentum, but not enough skill.
I caught his sword between two fingers, putting Empty-Hand Seizes the Blade into practice, then shrugged at the face beyond its trembling blade.
“He’s not dead. He’ll spend about a month in bed shitting blood, though.”
“Since you’re at it, you can shit beside him.”
Boom!
His body shot backward, sweeping more than a dozen people along with it.
I walked down the path that had opened before me and spread both hands. The fire dragon coiled in my lower dantian surged through my acupoints and settled in my hands.
Whoosh. Ssssss.
Terrible heat spread in every direction.
Water evaporated from the mud before my feet could touch it. Blue-white flames shone in the eyes of the elite warriors about to charge me.
“W-Wait...!”
I answered with both palms.
Like the former Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan who had once destroyed the Five Poisons Sect, I unleashed Flame Divine Palm in every direction.
Kwaaaang!
Rumble!
Flames shot through the air, swept over the undergrowth, and set the densely packed trees ablaze.
Beneath that enormous blaze, hundreds of enemies fled screaming through the darkness.
Among them, thankfully, was a middle-aged man in a leopard hide flashy enough to recognize at a glance.
“Move! Get out of my way!”
From the way he was running, he clearly wanted to live.
But no matter how hard he and his guards tried to get out of here, there was a reason the word impossible existed.
“Yeah. I’m afraid I can’t get out of your way.”
“J-Jin Taekyung!”
“They called you a tribal chieftain, but I wasn’t sure at first. I definitely saw you at the Tribal Grand Council, though. So, how’ve you been?”
Shaaak!
This was why people called sword-carrying bastards ill-mannered. I greeted him warmly, and the first thing he did was swing a weapon at me.
Whoosh, crack!
“Aaargh!”
I dodged the sword with ease and broke his wrist, drawing a scream of pain.
Then I fired Finger Qi at the five guards charging me. Muyaho appeared like the wind a moment later, and the beasts turned tail.
Whoosh. Rumble!
Flames and ash drifted overhead. Huge trees toppled one after another like dominoes. The tribal chieftain’s face went deathly pale.
“P-Please, spare me...”
“You’re a tribal chieftain. Of course I’ll spare you—if you answer my questions properly.”
“I-I’ll tell you anything you want to know!”
The chieftain I’d captured was my favorite kind of enemy. He valued his own life enough to spill things I hadn’t even asked about.
Some of it was useful, too.
“...A general mobilization order?”
The chieftain nodded frantically.
“G-Great Chieftain Baeksang has become temporary Palace Lord, and an army of nearly ten thousand is already stationed in the Inner Palace.”
“Go on.”
“The Miao people are under strict surveillance and couldn’t answer the call, but all of Nanman is on the move, led by the three tribes under Baeksang.”
Damn it.
I swallowed the curse.
With the Beast Miao King having fled, it had been inevitable that Baeksang would become the temporary Palace Lord.
But this wasn’t a net over heaven and earth cast to catch me. It was a general mobilization order.
No way.
Dread seized me.
Perhaps Dark Heaven’s plan was far bigger than any of us had imagined—and far closer to completion.
If I waste even a moment here...

sentences.text: I’d thought of this place from the beginning, but I still hadn’t believed it would be here.
Nanman was vast, and I was a Korean who didn’t even know the geography of the Central Plains properly.
In fact, of all the martial artists in the world, there probably wasn’t another hybrid quite like me.
An outsider in the Central Plains, for all intents and purposes.
And undeniably an outsider in Nanman.
How was someone like me supposed to know exactly where we were headed, or where we would stop?
Besides, Muyaho was a spiritual creature that understood human speech, not one that could speak it.
So when the White Tiger’s pace finally slowed, I realized where we were.
Looks like “no way” really is going to get someone killed.
Fuck.
The mountain looked ominous even from a distance.
Ailao Mountain was just as it had been when I left it a few days ago: dark and chilly, with a smell of blood that seemed to drift from beyond the thick fog.
In short, it was the kind of place that made me feel fucking awful every time I came here.
As far as Ailao Mountain was concerned, they ought to invent a character for “dick” and write its name with that instead of the character for “mountain.”
“...Is it really here?”
- Grrr.
“You know I’ll chop your leg off if you’re lying, right?”
- Grrrr!
“Ah.
Okay.”
Damn.
Guess it really was.
I gently scratched between the White Tiger’s brows to soothe its irritation and looked around.
A wolf howled now and then.
Each time, mountain birds took flight with a flutter.
Those were the only sounds I heard.
Yeah.
At least as far as sound goes.
I checked the Quest window.
The linked Quest that had begun automatically when Muyaho and I split off from the group was short and simple for a Quest with a Grade as high as Supreme Peak.
System Quest I Can See Your Tracking Scent You chose to follow the tracking scent.
At the end of the road you are traveling now, may you find what you seek.
Grade: Supreme Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: Find Yohi (Incomplete) Reward: ???
Failure: ???
Find Yohi, huh?
Of course I had to succeed.
Honestly, though, it didn’t matter to me whether I found Yohi or Heugung.
Quest or no Quest, I had to do this.
Those two were among my best chances of thwarting the Southern Heaven Demon Empress and Baeksang’s plans.
From what I’ve learned, no one knows where the Beast Miao King is, and the friendly forces inside the Nanman Beast Palace have effectively lost their power.
With so little time left, the best move is to rescue the two Great Chieftains and take them to the Inner Palace.
Did you think I’d made Muyaho run like hell while I sat comfortably on its back enjoying the scenery?
I’d thought this through on the way here.
After what happened at the Western Yao Estate, the Nanman Beast Palace considered me the greatest fucking bastard under heaven.
If I charged in alone, all that awaited me were spears and blades.
But what if Heugung and Yohi—the very people who’d been abducted—came back alive with me?
That would turn the whole board around.
No question.
Words carried different weight depending on who spoke them.
If Great Chieftains from the four tribes came forward to prove my innocence and reveal the truth behind the tragedy, everything happening in Nanman would take a new turn.
That was why I had to complete this Quest, one way or another.
It was a brilliant move that could overturn the situation in a single stroke.
Of course...
“Can’t make a brilliant move without a Go stone to play.
And getting one won’t be easy.”
I muttered the words like a sigh.
Then, sensing people closing in around me from every direction, I added, “So I think I’ll catch a few of you instead of Go stones to start with...
Who wants to die first?”
As expected, no one answered.
I launched myself forward without hesitation.
Whoosh.
Fwoooosh!
Flamefire Path.
Flames rose with my footsteps and became a meteor’s tail, cleaving the darkness.
There were more enemies here than I’d encountered at any point since I began following the tracking scent.
I could see roughly three hundred of them, and there were probably just as many—or more—lying in wait behind the dense grass.
But...
That’s all?
I stood among the predators at the top of Murim’s vast food chain.
The enemies surrounding me were nothing more than a helpless flock of sheep.
I could subdue them without sinking my teeth into their necks.
Whoosh, fwoooosh!
I shot forward amid flames that devoured the darkness.
Screams erupted from the enemies who realized what was happening half a beat too late.
“H-He’s spotted us!”
“Stop him!
He’s com—!”
Kwaaaang!
The shout vanished beneath a thunderous blast.
The ground overturned, and enormous trees tore free by their roots.
Dozens of enemies flew in every direction at once, as if they’d agreed to do it together.
“Guh!”
“Aaargh!”
Their tightly packed formation had collapsed.
Screams filled the gaps.
As I walked out, brushing dirt from my shoulder, someone shouted, “Put the beasts in front!
Attack him from the rear!”
“Oh, you animal-abusing bastard.”
That aside, it wasn’t a bad choice.
Nanman’s way of fighting with beasts had earned its reputation.
It was one reason Nanman warriors, despite being individually less skilled than martial artists from the Central Plains, had distinguished themselves in the Great Faction War.
Of course, that only worked when the situation called for it.
Grrrrrrr!
The moment a creature far larger than an ordinary brown bear charged at me with a roar—
Shh-shh-shhik!
A pale blur accompanied by a sharp whistle of displaced air flashed past my side and struck the alpha brown bear in the mouth.
Crack!
Crunch!
Drops of blood scattered through the air, and the bear toppled forward.
With a single kitty-paw punch, Muyaho had subdued a beast that might have ranked among the three strongest here.
Its eyes gleamed.
Whooosh!
I couldn’t see it, but I could feel it: a chill spreading in every direction.
This is...
Fear.
The White Tiger had been born beyond the bounds of an ordinary beast.
As its overwhelming presence bore down on the area, the beasts’ growls vanished, and their bristling tails drooped toward the ground.
Another strange gleam passed through Muyaho’s moonlit blue-white eyes.
- GRAAAAAAWR!
The explosive roar made the air tremble.
The wind surged.
Grass and flowers bent low.
Pupils dilating, the beasts huddled down and backed away.
And they weren’t the only ones affected.
“Gasp.”
“M-My body...”
Muyaho’s aura fell short of the Water God Dragon’s, or that of some of the monsters I’d encountered.
But it was enough to freeze some of the less accomplished martial artists among our enemies.
Which meant, of course, that others could still move.
“You idiots!
What are you doing?!”
I heard panic and fury in the shout.
I spotted a middle-aged man wearing a leopard hide well behind the others and shot toward him like a spear.
Shaaak!
Crack!
“Aaargh!”
“M-Monster!”
That was right.
Here and now, I was the only monster.
Someone they couldn’t stop.
Someone they’d imagined in their heads but never once thought they would have to face as an enemy.
Even if every person here stood in my way, I had the strength to keep going.
“Protect the Chieftain!”
“Stop him by any means necessary—guh!”
I tapped an opponent’s chest with my palm.
Scorching Yang Qi seeped into his body and disrupted the flow of his qi.
Blood burst from his mouth like a fountain, and he crumpled.
“You bastard!
How dare—!”
Whoosh!
Tap.
Was the man I’d just taken down a friend of his?
He had plenty of momentum, but not enough skill.
I caught his sword between two fingers, putting Empty-Hand Seizes the Blade into practice, then shrugged at the face beyond its trembling blade.
“He’s not dead.
He’ll spend about a month in bed shitting blood, though.”
“Since you’re at it, you can shit beside him.”
Boom!
His body shot backward, sweeping more than a dozen people along with it.
I walked down the path that had opened before me and spread both hands.
The fire dragon coiled in my lower dantian surged through my acupoints and settled in my hands.
Whoosh.
Ssssss.
Terrible heat spread in every direction.
Water evaporated from the mud before my feet could touch it.
Blue-white flames shone in the eyes of the elite warriors about to charge me.
“W-Wait...!”
I answered with both palms.
Like the former Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan who had once destroyed the Five Poisons Sect, I unleashed Flame Divine Palm in every direction.
Kwaaaang!
Rumble!
Flames shot through the air, swept over the undergrowth, and set the densely packed trees ablaze.
Beneath that enormous blaze, hundreds of enemies fled screaming through the darkness.
Among them, thankfully, was a middle-aged man in a leopard hide flashy enough to recognize at a glance.
“Move!
Get out of my way!”
From the way he was running, he clearly wanted to live.
But no matter how hard he and his guards tried to get out of here, there was a reason the word impossible existed.
“Yeah.
I’m afraid I can’t get out of your way.”
“J-Jin Taekyung!”
“They called you a tribal chieftain, but I wasn’t sure at first.
I definitely saw you at the Tribal Grand Council, though.
So, how’ve you been?”
Shaaak!
This was why people called sword-carrying bastards ill-mannered.
I greeted him warmly, and the first thing he did was swing a weapon at me.
Whoosh, crack!
“Aaargh!”
I dodged the sword with ease and broke his wrist, drawing a scream of pain.
Then I fired Finger Qi at the five guards charging me.
Muyaho appeared like the wind a moment later, and the beasts turned tail.
Whoosh.
Rumble!
Flames and ash drifted overhead.
Huge trees toppled one after another like dominoes.
The tribal chieftain’s face went deathly pale.
“P-Please, spare me...”
“You’re a tribal chieftain.
Of course I’ll spare you—if you answer my questions properly.”
“I-I’ll tell you anything you want to know!”
The chieftain I’d captured was my favorite kind of enemy.
He valued his own life enough to spill things I hadn’t even asked about.
Some of it was useful, too.
“...A general mobilization order?”
The chieftain nodded frantically.
“G-Great Chieftain Baeksang has become temporary Palace Lord, and an army of nearly ten thousand is already stationed in the Inner Palace.”
“Go on.”
“The Miao people are under strict surveillance and couldn’t answer the call, but all of Nanman is on the move, led by the three tribes under Baeksang.”
Damn it.
I swallowed the curse.
With the Beast Miao King having fled, it had been inevitable that Baeksang would become the temporary Palace Lord.
But this wasn’t a net over heaven and earth cast to catch me.
It was a general mobilization order.
No way.
Dread seized me.
Perhaps Dark Heaven’s plan was far bigger than any of us had imagined—and far closer to completion.
If I waste even a moment here...
I watched the flames spread rapidly across Ailao Mountain, then launched myself forward.
Into the darkness crouched over Ailao Mountain.
Into the flames.

chapters.title: Chapter 676
paragraphs: The fire I’d started with Flame Divine Palm spread from the entrance to Ailao Mountain in the blink of an eye.
Fwoosh. Roooar!
If the Scorching Hell described in Buddhism existed, I imagined it would look something like this.
Ash drifted endlessly through the air, mixing with acrid smoke. A fire demon rolled like a wave, devouring everything in its path.
Crack. Rumble!
The earth shook as massive trees toppled one after another, and mountain birds took flight all at once.

It was the sort of sight that would have made Jeok Cheongang, honorary chairman of the Forest Protection Association, roll his eyes back in horror. Fortunately, there were no beasts in sight, so it looked like the Animal Protection Association wouldn’t be getting involved too.
Wild animals must be quick on the uptake. Have they all run away already?
Not that it mattered now.
I didn’t want to take the home and lives of some poor family of muntjacs, but stopping Dark Heaven’s scheme and saving everyone else’s lives mattered more.
If that sense of dread is right...
I had no time to hesitate.
Running at full speed, I spotted a wall of flame blocking the path a little over thirty yards ahead and reached into the air.
Open Inventory. Summon.
Not taking White Flame out when I surrendered at the Western Yao Estate had been the right choice. If they’d confiscated it, I wouldn’t have had it when I needed it most.
Shing.
Cool metal filled my hand. Flames flickering all around me reflected off the spearhead, so white it looked almost transparent.
Now.
With the entire area already turning into a sea of fire, I didn’t do something stupid like send out Scorching Yang Qi.
What I needed was power and speed—and a single clean, perfect motion.
Whoosh!
The spearhead slashed diagonally down. A violent gust burst from its tip with a short whistle and tore the flames apart.
Fwoosh! Boom!
The explosion opened a path.
I flattened myself against Muyaho’s white fur and whispered into the ear of the tiger that had hesitated before the flames.
“Let’s go.”
- Grrr.
The White Tiger answered with a low growl and shot forward like a beam of light.
The flames rolled after us like waves, close on our heels, but even amid the chaos, Muyaho knew exactly where it was going.
Papat!
The scenery flashed past. Clouds hid the moon high overhead. As we raced on with the fire at our backs, something about the path struck me as familiar.
“Don’t tell me...”
A thought flashed through my mind, and I fell silent.
No. Maybe there was no don’t tell me about it. This path and the scenery around it should have been unfamiliar. If I recognized them, it could mean only one thing.
The Poisonblood Grounds.
After the Five Poisons Sect, which had once terrorized all of Nanman, was destroyed, Ailao Mountain became known as one of Nanman’s forbidden lands.
And the Poisonblood Grounds lay in its deepest, most secluded reaches.
If my guess was right, that was exactly where we were headed. To what might be the most dangerous place in Nanman.
But there should be plenty of troops guarding it by now.
The Nanman Beast Palace wasn’t some backwater sect full of riffraff.

When five Thousand-Year Spiders—venomous beasts so rare they were almost unheard of—appeared, and the Poisonblood Grounds emerged after going undiscovered for so long, the Palace had sent a sizable force to root out any surviving remnants of the Five Poisons Sect and whatever dangers remained.
Even if they were trying to hide right under the Palace’s nose, they went in there?
I didn’t have to wait long for an answer.
- Grrrr...
Muyaho gradually slowed. It bared its teeth at something I couldn’t see, and I knew at once that something had happened. Then I caught the smell seeping through the acrid smoke.
Human blood.
I see. So that’s how it is.
I looked toward the entrance to the Poisonblood Grounds. It gaped like the maw of a gigantic monster, full of the same unknown dangers I’d sensed on my first visit.
No. Perhaps it was worse now.
Well, if it were easy, it wouldn’t be a Supreme Peak-grade Quest.
I’d started to think things were going more smoothly than expected. But like Baeksang—though for a very different reason—I’d come too far to turn back.
If I avoided the danger in front of me, something worse would come rushing up behind me. Just like the flames sweeping through the forest at my back.
Rustle.
I climbed down from Muyaho’s back and gently scratched under its chin, where it liked it.
“Looks like this is where we part ways. Unlike last time, you don’t have to come back for me.”
- Grrr?
“Go back before it gets any later. You can break through the flames and escape. I know you can.”
- Grrrr...
Muyaho gave a soft growl and gazed into my eyes.
I could see conflict and fear in the intelligent White Tiger’s blue-white eyes. With instincts like its, it must have guessed already.
Getting in would be easy. Getting out would be hard.
It might never see Yayul Mok again.
Yet it couldn’t turn away as easily as it had last time. I supposed we’d grown attached to each other along the way.
“I’m not going in there to die. Don’t worry about me. Go on—your master’s waiting.”
I stroked the back of its neck. At last, Muyaho gave a slow nod and sprang forward.
- GRAAAWR!
Whoosh!
Not toward the hill the flames had yet to reach, but straight for the entrance to the Poisonblood Grounds.
“Hey! Hey, you idiot!”
I shouted in surprise, but it was already too late to catch it.
I froze at the unexpected turn of events. With a mighty roar, the White Tiger charged headlong into the pale Poison Mist—then staggered back out.
- Krrk. Cough.
“...Want a poison-warding pearl?”
Muyaho paused, avoided my eyes, and gave a furtive nod.
Muyaho adapted to the Poisonblood Grounds much faster than I’d expected.

As if biting down on the poison-warding pearl weren’t enough, it gulped the thing down whole. With nimble reflexes, it dealt with the venomous beasts surging in from every direction and cleared a swamp so wide that even Peak masters who had learned a movement technique would have hesitated to cross it in a single leap.
But the deeper we went, the more cautious its movements and breathing became.
Whooosh...

Poison Mist filled the grounds, making it hard to see. Something brushed through the grass. Water dripped somewhere out of sight. Apart from those occasional sounds, everything was quiet enough to make my skin crawl.
It wasn’t this bad even when I came here with the Beast Miao King last time.
I had sensed it from the moment I smelled blood at the entrance, but this was definitely not a good sign.
A thought crossed my mind. Perhaps... No, there was a good chance the Palace warriors sent here a few days ago were already dead.
If they are, that bastard probably did it.

A Supreme Peak master whose name, sobriquet, and face remained unknown. Someone who had drenched the Western Yao Estate in blood and abducted Heugung and Yohi in mere moments was more than capable of it.
It was also highly possible that it wasn’t just one bastard, but them.
Dark Heaven.
Even what they’d revealed of their strength so far was terrifying. They had emerged in the wake of the Demonic Cult, and I’d personally faced the Blood Lord and the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
Their martial prowess was such that even now, after growing rapidly through the System, relentless training, and countless life-or-death battles, I couldn’t count on beating them.
I haven’t fought the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, but I doubt she’s any weaker.
No wonder I was tense, heading into enemy territory alone.

When I’d encountered the Blood Lord, Sword Saint Mae Jonghak had been there. And when I’d come closer to death than ever before in my battle with the Western Heaven Demon Lord, Jeok Cheongang had helped me.
But if the Southern Heaven Demon Empress is here...
Would I live to see my companions and family again?
Drip.
A bead of cold sweat I hadn’t noticed forming slid down the back of my neck.
Lick.
Something rough enough to sting swept over my skin.
The White Tiger had licked the back of my neck. Now it was pretending nothing had happened. I let out a quiet laugh.
“Telling me not to be nervous?”
- Grrrr.
It was such a small thing, but somehow it put me at ease.
I’d faced death more times than I could count. After coming this far, what was I doing breaking into a cold sweat? If I let myself tense up, I’d be too stiff to fight properly.
Yeah, fuck it. It’s not like this is my first time.
I called to mind the no-brakes mentality essential to the successor of the Fire Gate Clan and the heir of the Fire King, then thrust a palm toward the Poison Mist.
Boom!
The sharp sound of displaced air shattered the silence.
Scorching Yang Qi was poison’s natural enemy. The fierce heat of Flame Divine Palm surged forward, breaking the thick mist apart and staining the dark Poisonblood Grounds red.
Hssssss!
Strangely shaped venomous beasts scurried away from the light and heat.
The tangled, maze-like paths finally lay exposed. I glared into them, put internal energy behind my voice, and roared.
“Come out, you fucking bastards!”
- GRAAAAAAWR!
How had this happened?
Yohi came to her senses and blinked into darkness so deep she couldn’t see an inch in front of her.
“Ah.”
Her usually alluring voice was half-hoarse. Her body ached all over, perhaps from lying still for so long.
Then fragments of memory began to return.
Her heart lurched. Her body, relaxed for a moment, went rigid as stone.
In Yohi’s trembling eyes, memories she couldn’t believe were flashing past.
Screams. Corpses. Blood.
And the face of the one person responsible for it all.
She was about to scream when a voice, carefully hushed, came from the darkness.
“Calm yourself, Yohi.”
“Gasp...!”
“Don’t be frightened. It’s me.”
Yohi barely managed to swallow her scream and calm her pounding heart.
As her eyes adjusted to the dark, a familiar figure came into view.
“Heugung? Is it really you, big brother Heugung?”
“That’s right. Don’t you remember?”
It took her a moment to piece her memories back together. She recalled Heugung resisting him to the very end.
“I forgot for a moment. But why are you speaking so differently...?”
Heugung had been waiting not far away in the darkness for her to wake. He gave her a bitter smile.
“There were various circumstances. Circumstances I couldn’t easily tell even you.”
His tone was so courteous. Yohi was used to seeing Heugung grin foolishly and call her “little sister”; this side of him felt strange. But it wasn’t what mattered now.
“Where are we? Wh-where is that man?”
“I don’t know either. I woke up here.”
Iron chains bound her body, and her internal energy wouldn’t budge.
Yohi searched the darkness around her in despair. Then came a heavy noise, and faint light poured in.
