A bead of cold sweat I hadn’t noticed forming slid down the back of my neck.
Lick.
Something rough enough to sting swept over my skin.
The White Tiger had licked the back of my neck.
Now it was pretending nothing had happened.
I let out a quiet laugh.
“Telling me not to be nervous?”
- Grrrr.
It was such a small thing, but somehow it put me at ease.
I’d faced death more times than I could count.
After coming this far, what was I doing breaking into a cold sweat?
If I let myself tense up, I’d be too stiff to fight properly.
Yeah, fuck it.
It’s not like this is my first time.
I called to mind the no-brakes mentality essential to the successor of the Fire Gate Clan and the heir of the Fire King, then thrust a palm toward the Poison Mist.
Boom!
The sharp sound of displaced air shattered the silence.
Scorching Yang Qi was poison’s natural enemy.
The fierce heat of Flame Divine Palm surged forward, breaking the thick mist apart and staining the dark Poisonblood Grounds red.
Hssssss!
Strangely shaped venomous beasts scurried away from the light and heat.
The tangled, maze-like paths finally lay exposed.
I glared into them, put internal energy behind my voice, and roared.
“Come out, you fucking bastards!”
- GRAAAAAAWR!
How had this happened?
Yohi came to her senses and blinked into darkness so deep she couldn’t see an inch in front of her.
“Ah.”
Her usually alluring voice was half-hoarse.
Her body ached all over, perhaps from lying still for so long.
Then fragments of memory began to return.
Her heart lurched.
Her body, relaxed for a moment, went rigid as stone.
In Yohi’s trembling eyes, memories she couldn’t believe were flashing past.
Screams.
Corpses.
Blood.
And the face of the one person responsible for it all.
She was about to scream when a voice, carefully hushed, came from the darkness.
“Calm yourself, Yohi.”
“Gasp...!”
“Don’t be frightened.
It’s me.”
Yohi barely managed to swallow her scream and calm her pounding heart.
As her eyes adjusted to the dark, a familiar figure came into view.
“Heugung?
Is it really you, big brother Heugung?”
“That’s right.
Don’t you remember?”
It took her a moment to piece her memories back together.
She recalled Heugung resisting him to the very end.
“I forgot for a moment.
But why are you speaking so differently...?”
Heugung had been waiting not far away in the darkness for her to wake.
He gave her a bitter smile.
“There were various circumstances.
Circumstances I couldn’t easily tell even you.”
His tone was so courteous.
Yohi was used to seeing Heugung grin foolishly and call her “little sister”; this side of him felt strange.
But it wasn’t what mattered now.
“Where are we?
Wh-where is that man?”
“I don’t know either.
I woke up here.”
Iron chains bound her body, and her internal energy wouldn’t budge.
Yohi searched the darkness around her in despair.
Then came a heavy noise, and faint light poured in.

chapters.title: Chapter 677
paragraphs: Click. Rumble.
The stone gate swung open, spilling light into the darkness.
Heugung and Yohi, whose eyes had grown accustomed to the darkness, instinctively shrank back and groaned. Then a voice bored into their ears.
“Oh-ho. Now that’s a sight worth seeing.”
“Of course. This is how the barbarians of Nanman ought to look.”
The voice slurred and swayed as though its owner were drunk. Both of them trembled.
Was it because they felt humiliated by the mockery and ridicule in his words?
No. It was because of fear. Because of terror.
That voice...
Yohi recognized it, and her blood seemed to turn cold.
How could she forget the voice of the Fiend who had appeared like a ghost, slaughtered her warriors, and left Heugung with one arm after a single move?
Her mind went blank. Beside her, Heugung whispered as quietly as he could.
“Remember this. You must never open your eyes—”
Boom!
A sharp blast of displaced air sounded, followed by a scream.
Yohi squeezed her eyes shut as he had told her. She could not see him, but it was easy enough to imagine Heugung coughing up dark-red blood from his internal injuries.
“Stop! Please, stop!”
“Cough, cough. Yohi, stay still—”
Boom! Thud.
Another blast of displaced air rang out, and Yohi could no longer endure it. She opened her eyes.
Heugung lay on the floor, his whole body bound. He had vomited what looked like a full doe of blood. The Fiend stood over him.
“I heard you were a clever woman. Seems that was just a rumor.”
The Fiend revealed yellow teeth in a grin as Yohi’s voice slipped between her trembling lips.

His white hair was nearly as disheveled as a bird’s nest, and his eyes were narrow slits. He had hidden his face behind a mask in the Western Yao Estate, but there was no doubt that the old man before her was the same Fiend.
“Why didn’t you listen to that fellow? If you hadn’t seen this old man’s face, you might have lived for another fifteen minutes.”
“Well, too late now. I’ll just have to send you both to the afterlife together.”
He shrugged and reached toward her. His arm was unnaturally long for such a small man.
His palm was covered in spots Yohi could not identify. As it drew closer, so did the smell of death.
Yohi knew this was the end. She was about to struggle when—
“That’s enough, Black Hand.”
The words came through the gap in the half-open stone gate. The old man called Black Hand withdrew his hand and sighed.
“Now I can’t even have a little fun without watching myself.”
Someone beyond the gate answered.
“Was that directed at me?”
The voice was as cold as eternal snow. Black Hand smacked his lips.
“Of course not. I was talking to myself. Just talking to myself.”
“Stop acting like a reckless brat. You haven’t forgotten the order given by Her Majesty the Demon Empress, have you?”
Black Hand’s face twisted.
“Reckless? I never thought I’d hear that at my age.”
“Then act your age. If you do anything rash with the great undertaking so close at hand, I will not forgive you.”
“I’ll take your silence as an answer.”
Yohi had sensed no one outside the gate, nor could she sense anyone leaving. But when Black Hand muttered a moment later, she knew the speaker was gone.
“Damn old monster.”
To Black Hand, it might have been a passing complaint. Yohi had to fight to keep her shock and fear off her face.
There’s someone else.
She did not know who had spoken from beyond the gate. But their exchange had told her enough.
That person possesses enough seniority and martial prowess to make even the Fiend before me obey him.
And there was something more.
The Demon Empress. He definitely said the Demon Empress.
Two words that had appeared in the middle of their short conversation.
The Demon Empress.
Yohi knew whom he meant.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
One of Dark Heaven’s core figures, said to be unnaturally beautiful and more dangerous still.
Everything concerning the Southern Heaven Demon Empress was treated as top-secret information. But Yohi was one of Nanman’s four Great Chieftains, so she was an exception.
More importantly, she had a great tree named Baeksang whom she could trust and rely on.
“Stand by my side, and I’ll give you what you want.”
He had said it when they first met, shortly after Yohi became a Great Chieftain. She had asked him:
“What do you intend to give me?”
“Vast wealth and influence. And the restoration of the Yao people.”
“Interesting. But I’ll refuse.”
“Why?”

“Even if I accept your offer, Great Chieftain Baeksang, I won’t get as much as I want. I’m more ambitious than I look. And I’m not naive enough to make Palace Lord Yayul my enemy over a promise you might not keep.”
“You inherited the Western Yao Estate when you took the position of Great Chieftain. Do you have any trustworthy subordinates there?”
“Of course. But why are you suddenly asking about that...?”
“I thought I might send a belated gift to congratulate you. Five carts of gold should be enough to start with.”
“Go home for now. If you wish to accept my offer, meet me here at this time tomorrow.”
Five carts of gold.
At first, Yohi had hardly believed him. She had never imagined a sum like that. Then she saw the gleaming piles of gold waiting for her, and doubt became impossible.
Baeksang kept his promises. If she stood by him, she might receive more than she had asked for.
Yohi spent a sleepless night and went straight to Baeksang the next day. She thought her judgment had been sound.
No. She had believed it was sound.
Until the Fiend came for her.
“Oh-ho. Look at this little bitch.”
As if his irritation had vanished, Black Hand gave her a hazy, drunken smile.
“Those eyes have gone so wide. You’re starting to understand, aren’t you?”
“I’ve heard the gist of it. They said things went smoothly for us thanks to you. I’ll give Baeksang that much—for a barbarian, he handled his part rather well.”
Yohi’s pupils shook violently.
She could not believe the situation she was in: not only had she served as a pawn of Dark Heaven, she was now in danger of dying.
“That can’t be. It can’t. I didn’t know...”
“Didn’t know? Or pretended not to?”
“I don’t even need to ask. After all, you followed that bastard Baeksang for more than ten years. A woman who had risen to become a Great Chieftain would naturally have had her doubts.”
Yohi could only stare blankly at Black Hand as he chuckled.
Everything he said was true.
It had started small. At the annual Tribal Grand Council, she supported Baeksang’s proposals. She followed a few minor instructions from him. In return, gold and influence came pouring in.
As the years passed, her doubts deepened. A few months ago, she began hearing the name Dark Heaven more and more often, and unease took hold.
But she did nothing. She pushed down her suspicions and refused to look at them.
She had gained too much to expose everything and try to put it right.
The Yao people looked up to the woman who had restored their weakening tribe. Chieftains who had once treated her like a little girl now bowed their heads first.
Even the mighty Beast Miao King and Baeksang would eventually return to the earth as a handful of soil. When that time came, she might even be able to reach for the vacant throne.
She would rise to the position of Palace Lord as a woman and rewrite the history of the Nanman Beast Palace.
That was the ambition Yohi had dwelt on every night. Now it was collapsing around her.
“Even so, you should be grateful to this old man. If the previous Great Chieftain of the Yao people hadn’t died suddenly, how could a stupid woman like you have lived in luxury until now?”
“Th-that can’t mean...”
“He was troublesome. His martial arts were pathetic, but he noticed things. A plague happened to strike the Yao people at just the right time, so he was easy to deal with.”
Black Hand grinned.

“Strange, isn’t it? The Great Chieftain was old, so his death was one thing. But then his three sons, the ones meant to succeed him, died too. The position passed all the way down to a daughter born to him by a concubine in his old age.”

“Baeksang’s expression back then was truly something to see. He dragged things out to the bitter end, insisting he would somehow persuade the old man... Still, perhaps the bastard had a strong survival instinct, because he never came charging in. What a shame.”
Yohi stared at him, hollow-eyed. She thought nothing could surprise her now. She thought she had no strength left for it.
She was wrong.
“You did rather well for a woman, though. Setting out a tracking scent with your life at stake—that caution must come from your old father.”
Tracking scent.
At the three words that slipped from Black Hand’s dark lips, Yohi’s delicate body suddenly went rigid.
Black Hand saw the last of her hope break, and his delight spilled over.
“What? Did you think this old man wouldn’t know?”
He chuckled at the despair in her trembling eyes. He had seen it countless times, but the thrill of such moments had never faded.
“Oh, you poor, green little girl. You foolish child.”
A palm mottled with black spots, true to his name, stroked her pale cheek.
“You’re truly beautiful. Beautiful enough for Her Majesty the Demon Empress to covet.”
He opened his mouth like a predator over its prey. The stench from his teeth was foul; every one of them was rotten or grotesquely twisted.
“I’d like to kill you both with one palm strike, but... I’ll restrain myself this time. I have something to do first.”
He left Yohi frozen like an insect caught in a web and stood. After a glance at Heugung, who lay unconscious on the floor, he approached the stone gate.
Then—
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
A tremendous crash shook the area. From far away came a shout.
—Come out, you fucking bastards!
GRAAAAAWR!
It was time to welcome the guest who had come such a long way.
My method of calling out enemies was simple.
I broke things, wrecked things, and smashed them to pieces.
Poison Mist? Venomous beasts? Enemies hiding somewhere, waiting for their chance?
I didn’t care. I rampaged like an eight-ton truck with a broken steering wheel, smashing everything in the Poisonblood Grounds.
They’d have no choice but to come out.
Before long, it worked.
“What a vigorous young man.”
“I expected the Beast Miao King if someone came looking for us... So you’re Jin Taekyung?”
I followed the voices and slowly turned around.
A short, squat old man swaying as though he were drugged, and a tall old man radiating such cold that I wondered if his hometown was King Sejong Station in Antarctica.
They could hardly have looked less alike. But they had two things in common.
First, they were both Supreme Peak masters.
Second, both were giving off enough killing intent to make it clear they had no intention of letting me leave alive.
I considered the two of them for a moment, then spoke sternly.
“One of you step aside. By the customs of the martial world, I’ll take you on one at a time.”
The answer came immediately.
Whoosh—KWA-BOOM!
Yeah, fuck. I knew that wouldn’t work.

chapters.title: Chapter 678
paragraphs: It was a relief that the Southern Heaven Demon Empress was nowhere in sight. But there were two Supreme Peak masters here.
Damn it. I don’t know.
Was I lucky, or was I screwed?
Whoosh—KWA-BOOM!
I dodged a black Fist Force by a hair as it shot toward me like a beam of light. I steadied myself and sighed.
“Ah, the code of the martial world lies in ruins. Whatever happened to the noble custom of yielding three forms to a junior?”
“What?”
The squat old man with disheveled hair blinked at me.
What I’d said must have struck him as so absurd that the fist he’d been about to throw after his opening attack lowered instead.
“The code of the martial world? Yielding three forms to a junior?”
I dropped my voice.
“Indeed.”
“Why are you suddenly talking like an old-fashioned gentleman and spouting nonsense? A moment ago, you told one of us bastards to stay out of it while you fought the other.”
“‘Bastards’? Did I say that?”
“Now you’re being polite again. Either talk like you did at first or stick to that formal way of speaking. I can’t keep up.”
“Forgive me. I’m a junior from a much later generation. I failed to recognize my Seniors and was terribly rude.”
I straightened up and even gave them a clasped-fist salute. Confusion filled the disheveled old man’s eyes.
“Now you’re confusing me. Aren’t you Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung, the Fire King’s heir?”
“I am.”
“Then that means you’re one of those orthodox-faction types. Hearing you go on about juniors is enough to make me sick.”

“What a hurtful thing to say. Aren’t all those who dwell in the martial world fellow martial artists and members of one family? Besides, the Fire Gate Clan has always been a faction between the orthodox and unorthodox sides. We don’t discriminate between the orthodox, demonic, or anything else. We all get along.”
“And yet you’re a pavilion master in the Murim Alliance?”
His eyes had already gone completely off the rails, but at least his brain still seemed to possess a minimum level of function.
A true master, however, kept his composure in any situation. I answered his sharp question without a change of expression.
“I’m actually a double agent.”
“A double agent?”
“Yes.”
“Bullshit.”
“Woof.”
“This is driving me insane.”
“I understand how you feel. But I swear to heaven, every word is true.”
“You little...”
“Did you call for me, Senior?”
The disheveled old man stared blankly at my polite demeanor before opening his mouth with a look of admiration.
“You put your heart into every stitch of that nonsense. In all my years, I’ve never met an orthodox-faction brat like you.”
I scratched the back of my head sheepishly.
“You fucking bastard. Then at least pretend to fall for it out of respect for the effort.”
“You deranged child. I might, if any of it were believable.”
“I’m embarrassed enough already. Shut up, you idiot.”
“...That tongue of yours got awfully rude, awfully fast. I could’ve sworn I was ‘Senior’ just a moment ago.”
“Going senile, old man? You’re a piece of demonic, heterodox trash who should’ve died in the Great Faction War. Who the hell do you think you are, asking to be called Senior?”
The disheveled old man stared at me for a moment as the insults poured out, then chuckled.
“You really are insane. A Disciple worthy of the Fire King.”
“Funny how everyone I meet says that when none of them have ever even seen the Fire King’s face.”
He paused, then let out a short laugh.
“How amusing. Truly amusing. You’ve barely passed twenty, and you dare talk about those days?”
“I don’t think I need to have lived through them to know.”
I shrugged.
“If a bastard like you had met him, you’d be dead. In other words, you were lucky enough to survive by avoiding the Fire King.”
“But I think your luck runs out today.”
Swish.
I raised White Flame and pointed it at him—no, at both of them. Heat shimmered above the pure-white spearhead, filled with Scorching Yang Qi.
“The Western Yao Estate. Was that your doing?”
Crack.
The smile vanished from the disheveled old man’s face. He clenched his fist and stepped forward.
“Yes. This old man did it.”
“I thought so. Only a lunatic would kill people that way. What about Heugung and Yohi?”
“We’ve kept them safe for now. Once Her Majesty the Demon Empress returns, though, those two won’t have long to live.”
Relief washed over me. He’d confirmed two things himself.
“Thanks for the fucking useful intel. So the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—that fucking bitch—isn’t here. And those two are still in one piece.”
Only then did he realize he’d said more than he needed to. His face stiffened.
“...That changes nothing. Even if Her Majesty the Demon Empress is absent, you will die by this old man’s hand.”
“Then why did you both come? Afraid a kid might kick your ass, so you brought your hyung?”
“You fucking brat...”
Step.
He couldn’t contain his anger and took a step forward. It wouldn’t have meant much to anyone watching, but that single step was exactly what I needed.
Now.
In the next instant, though, I had to stop the spear I’d been about to swing with all my strength.
Thud.
A long, withered hand as thin as a branch had caught the disheveled old man’s shoulder just as he stepped forward.
“It’s a provocation tactic. Don’t let that bastard’s three-inch tongue fool you.”
So he finally stepped in.
A cold voice. A cold expression.
Baeksang was about as chilly as a man could get, but the slender old man who’d remained silent until now was something else. No—their temperaments might be similar, but the depth was different.
His composure was as hard and cold as a glacier. So was the martial power within him.
I can’t see an opening.
My instincts were telling me something clear: he was at least my equal, perhaps stronger.
Though I’d been talking to the disheveled old man, my attention had been on this one from the start.
And it seemed my opponent felt the same way.
“Impressive. No, that hardly does you justice.”
The slender old man stepped forward, his admiration difficult to read.

“You unsettled your opponent with a few words, then looked for an opening to exploit. Now I understand why Her Majesty the Demon Empress warned us about you. You have martial prowess beyond your years and a calculating mind besides. You’ll become a great obstacle in time.”
“Am I taking a compliment the wrong way? Because it sounds like you’re saying you’ll kill me.”
“You understood both the compliment and my intention correctly.”
“Since you’ve already complimented me, why not let me pass? Do you really need to pull up a stone?”
“A stone lodged in the middle of the road must be removed if the path ahead is to be smooth.”
“And are the two of you really skilled enough to do that?”
“You bastard! Shut your mouth!”
The disheveled old man’s face twisted at the casual taunt. The slender one answered calmly.
“We’ll have to do our best.”
Damn it.
I suddenly had a feeling—no, the certainty—that this would be an extremely difficult fight.
When a mad dog runs wild, you can beat it down with a club. But an enemy who stays calm in any situation and doesn’t underestimate you is another matter.
Even more so if that enemy possessed martial prowess that was in no way inferior to my own.
One-on-one, in a life-and-death duel, I’d have even odds against him. But he won’t fight me one-on-one.
When the slightest difference can decide who lives and who dies, even a cat’s paw helps. And from what I could tell, the disheveled old man was stronger than Baeksang.
Can I do this? Can I?
The instinctive doubt had barely crossed my mind when—
“Grrrr...”
Muyaho bared his teeth and growled warily. He crouched low, ready to spring at any moment, without the slightest sign of backing away.
Yeah, fuck it. If an animal that can’t even talk is willing to fight, how can I back down?
Only one thing troubled me. I had a feeling I might not be able to protect him this time.
I’m sorry.
“Grrr.”
I couldn’t tell whether the clever White Tiger had read my eyes or understood that I wanted him, at least, to run far away.
But I was certain of one thing.
Either I would die here, or I would kill them.
Whatever happened, I wouldn’t back down.
Step.
“I’ve never heard your names, so go peel those dicks of yours that don’t even get hard anymore and eat them. Then spit out your sobriquets.”
With White Flame lowered at my side, I faced them. The disheveled old man smiled with killing intent.
“Black Hand Fist Demon.”
“Right, Black Hand. Never heard that one before. Guess you really are a nobody.”
“I had my reasons for staying unknown. But now the whole world will hear it—the sobriquet of the man who killed the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.”
“They’ll hear it without you doing that. Everyone who dies by my hand gets famous.”
I answered calmly, ignored Black Hand Fist Demon as he started to flare up, and turned to the other old man.
But contrary to my wishes, the slender old man met my eyes and gave a small shake of his head.
“An enemy whose sobriquet is known is easy to assess. Isn’t that right, Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung?”
“I know you, and you know nothing of me. One of us will fall here. Come when you’re ready.”
Damn it. This really won’t be easy.
But the die was cast. It was time to see how it landed.
I awakened the fire dragon curled in my lower dantian.
Rumble-rumble-rumble—!

An aura erupted from my entire body like a volcano exploding, shaking the area in every direction. Blue-white flames layered themselves over the transparent spearhead made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, completely enveloping the spear.
Fwoosh. Sizzle-sizzle-sizzle!
The terrible heat burned away poison and evaporated moisture.
As my aura surged, Black Hand Fist Demon’s drunken, unfocused gaze sharpened. A strange light flashed in the other old man’s eyes, which had been frozen like eternal snow.
“Indeed...!”
Swish.
An edged weapon slid from beneath his loose sleeve, gleaming blue. Then—
SHWAAAAAAK!
The twin wheels flew from the old man’s hand, tearing through the air.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
They ran without stopping.
Three tigers had become two, and five people had become four. Still, they ran. If anything, they had to move faster.
They had come too far to turn back. Doing so now would make his choice and sacrifice meaningless.
And perhaps thanks to him—no, thanks to Jin Taekyung—nothing stood in their way.

The tigers carried the four of them north, then farther north, before the messenger pigeon sent from the Nanman Beast Palace could arrive. The warriors of each tribe were too busy pursuing Jin Taekyung to stop them.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
They crossed the plains, climbed over mountains, and passed through swamps and rivers.
And at last, the first goal of this short yet urgent journey began to appear.
“There!”
Namho’s shout was directed below the hill.
Far ahead, several hundred Nanman warriors followed one another toward the northern border.
They had finally caught up with the reconnaissance squad. Relief hit them—and with it came the thought of one man.
Jin Taekyung.
Their Pavilion Master, though they had no idea where he was or what he might be doing now.

chapters.title: Chapter 679
paragraphs: The reconnaissance squad was made up of swift-footed elites, and it showed. More than two hundred strong, they reached the northeastern border in barely three days, even with breaks along the way.

But none of them—not even the two tribal chieftains leading the squad—had expected another group of unwelcome visitors to arrive before they encountered the mysterious monster known as the Blood Monk.
And this unexpected situation was nothing compared to the news those visitors had brought.
“What... did you just say?”
“What are you talking about?”
Chief Jang and Chief Go stared wide-eyed in disbelief.

It was shocking news none of them had expected. Had it come from anyone other than the Young Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, they would have dismissed it as nonsense. In fact, they wished they could.
But despite their desperate wish, Yayul Mok’s answer did not change.
“It is all true.”
The truth was there in his trembling eyes. The two chieftains could only sigh as they realized it had all happened.
“What in the world...”
“Why would the Palace Lord make that choice? Why?”
Yayul Mok clenched his fists so tightly that blood ran from his palms before opening his mouth.
“My father had already guessed that he would be unable to resist the tide of events once so many chieftains had joined hands with Uncle Baek—no, with Baeksang.”
“Even so, did he bring this danger upon himself just to save a few Han Chinese?”
“He did not bring it upon himself.”
“What?”

“My father said this when he sent me and the others to the underground prison. He said that repaying a righteous act with righteousness was keeping faith, and that turning away from someone who had helped us was injustice. So today, I intend to stake my fate on keeping faith. On those two people—Jin Taekyung and Baeksang.”
The two chieftains closed their eyes with low groans.
Having served at the Beast Miao King’s side for a long time, they had vaguely guessed what kind of person he was and what choices he would make.
But...
“This time, the Palace Lord was wrong. He should have gathered all the strength of the tribes that followed him and the Miao people, then executed the traitors in the Inner Palace.”

“Even if we give Jin Taekyung every benefit of the doubt, trusting him may have been the right choice. If the Young Palace Lord’s story is true, Jin Taekyung ultimately left alone in order to keep faith. But Baeksang is different.”
As the two chieftains spoke with such certainty, Yayul Mok, who had been looking at them with a trace of hope, opened his mouth.
“It is too early to judge. If Baeksang granted my father’s request...”
“Young Palace Lord.”
Chief Jang cut him off, his voice hollow.
“‘Subdue the Han Chinese in the reconnaissance squad and escort them to the Inner Palace.’ That is the first and last missive we received. Do you understand what it means?”
Yayul Mok faltered. Behind him, Namho, who had been watching quietly, suddenly understood. He spoke almost in a groan.
“He kept them in the dark on purpose.”
“Elder Namho, you mean...”

“There is no need to say more. The two chieftains here and the warriors in the reconnaissance squad are all people who follow the Palace Lord. If they were told about the trouble in the Inner Palace, they would surely interfere somehow. He probably intended to call them back after everything was finished. Or...”
Namho’s gaze darkened.
“Or... the Blood Monk. He may have planned to let that old monster deal with them.”

“A borrowed knife to kill others. Baeksang and Dark Heaven chose a useful blade. No, in this situation, it isn’t even someone else’s blade. There is a strong possibility that the Blood Monk is in league with them as well.”
A cold silence settled over the group. Namho saw their shaken faces and felt his heart sink.
This is bad. The worst.
Behind them lay the Nanman Beast Palace, likely in Baeksang and Dark Heaven’s hands by now. Ahead stood a mysterious Supreme Peak master they could not face alone.
And Jin Taekyung, the one person they could count on most, was not here.
What are we supposed to do?
Even after a lifetime in the Hidden Shadow Pavilion, Namho had no easy answer. But he had to decide before it was too late.
Amid the suffocating feeling that invisible chains were wrapped around his entire body, Namho finally forced his lips apart.
“Where are the others?”
Chief Jang understood.
“If you mean the Han Chinese, we detained them as a precaution. We did them no harm—only struck their Sleep Acupoints.”
“You intend to send them back to the Central Plains?”
The question caught Namho squarely off guard. After a brief silence, Namho nodded heavily.
“I’m sorry. But for now, this is the best option. If they cross the Yangtze and report what is happening in Nanman, the Murim Alliance will never stand by and do nothing.”
“...The Murim Alliance.”

“I was born in Nanman and spent half my life in the Central Plains. Though I am nothing more than a powerless old man, I am someone who understands the circumstances of both Nanman and the Central Plains better than anyone. If it is the Murim Alliance I know, they will find a way to help Nanman.”
His voice was calm, but his resolve was unmistakable.
Beyond the dense grass where they were lying in ambush, the two chieftains gazed at the broad, endless waters of the Yangtze before opening their mouths with sighs.
“Damn it.”
“What should we do?”
Namho had already made up his mind.
“There are two ways. First, release the Han Chinese, leave this place at once, avoid Baeksang’s eyes, and wait for the right moment. Second, head to the Central Plains together with the Han Chinese.”
“Head to the Central Plains together? There is no ship of sufficient size anywhere around here. How are we supposed to—”
“There is. A ship that can take everyone.”
They turned toward the sudden voice. Sama Pyo was staggering to his feet, supported by Taishan.
“Is that true?” Chief Jang asked.
At Chief Jang’s question, Sama Pyo answered with a pale face.
“How do you think we got all the way to Nanman?”
“Do you mean...”
“The swift ship of the Yangtze River Channel League is not far from here. It’s half a day to the west. If we travel for even half that time, we might be able to rendezvous with it.”
Hope lit the two chieftains’ faces.

If they followed a tributary of the Yangtze as far as Sichuan, they would be within the reach of the Central Plains Murim. Even if Baeksang and Dark Heaven held the Nanman Beast Palace, reinforcements from the Murim Alliance—with the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families at their head—could turn the situation around.
There are already three prestigious great sects in Sichuan alone. Even if the Murim Alliance’s official reinforcements are delayed, those three will be different.
Namho calmly considered their prospects.
The Emei Sect. The Qingcheng Sect. The Sichuan Tang Clan.
Even though they had shed much blood and weakened during the Sichuan Bloodbath, their roots ran deep and firm enough that even Dark Heaven could not tear them out in a single stroke.
Moreover, all three sects considered Jin Taekyung their Benefactor. If they answered the call, gathered the strength of Sichuan Murim, and headed for Nanman...
Seven days and nights to return, if we’re fast. Ten days at most.
Namho was neither a hot-blooded youth nor a martial artist who trusted in his own martial arts. That was why his judgment was colder and more accurate than anyone else’s in this place.
Lead them back the way we came, and we’ll surely die. Bring the Central Plains to our aid, and we have a real chance. Until then, Jin Taekyung and the Beast Miao King will have to...
He could only trust that they would hold out. That they would still be alive when the others returned.
Even Namho himself could not quite believe in that hope. Then, as he held on to it—
Boom. Boom. Booooom!
Namho heard it. No—everyone hidden in the forest above the endless river could see and hear it.
A low drumbeat. A sleek hull approaching on the currents of the Yangtze.
“What is that...?”
“The Yangtze River Channel League! It’s their swift ship!”
But the next moment, the two chieftains, who had been celebrating with brightened faces, sensed something strange and fell silent.
The swift ship should have been at least half a day to the west. Why was it here?
They saw the rigid expressions on Namho’s and Sama Pyo’s faces, and their puzzlement turned to dread. Namho spoke through a groan.
“Prepare for battle.”
Fear swept through the group. Namho thought of the one person who was not at his side—the one he needed now more than ever.
Damn it. I’m sorry.
They might die before they could save him.
Crash. Boom.
The hull cut through the water without slowing and drove hard onto the sandy shore.
And then...
Step.
Where a wave had swept over the sand, one person’s footstep was etched into it.
Whoosh!
Two streaks of light cut through the air.
Despite their strange movements, the twin wheels came at me like flashes of light. I swung White Flame diagonally downward to meet them.
KWA-BOOM! Rumble-rumble!
A tremendous roar erupted as a shockwave tore through the area and shook the air. But it was not over yet.
My five senses, sharp as blades, caught every movement of the twin wheels behind me.
They’re coming again.
As Muyaho slid backward, I caught him by the nape and twisted my body.
Whoosh—shhk!
A blue flash skimmed past me. I heard a sharp slicing sound and saw the White Tiger’s snow-white fur scatter through the air.
In my tilted field of vision, another sight came into view: a wild-haired freak charging at me like a mad bison.
“You bastard—!”
The Black Hand Fist Demon.
Black Force layered itself over his dark fist, and then he shot it straight toward my chest.
Whoom!
I felt the air ripple. Felt the terrifying power behind that punch. But...
That won’t be enough.
With a brief mutter, I straightened the body I had twisted as far as it would go. By then, the black Force had already reached point-blank range and was giving off an ominous light.
Beyond it, the Black Hand Fist Demon’s eyes gleamed with madness. They seemed to say, You’re dead now.
I had seen that certainty in the eyes of many enemies before.
From Third Rate swordsmen to Supreme Peak masters. Regardless of their level of martial arts, they had always worn that expression.
And when everything was over, I was always the one still standing on two feet.
Swish.
In the slowed-down world, the cool feel of the spear shaft slipped away from my hand.
The Black Hand Fist Demon had closed in so deftly that my spear had lost its advantage. Without a moment’s hesitation, I let go and struck with my palm.
KWA-BOOM!
Two differently colored Forces collided with a roar. Everything within a radius of ten-odd jang melted beneath the horrific heat, and the Black Hand Fist Demon’s eyes flew wide open.
One clash was enough for each of us to measure the other’s strength.
Even though the twin wheels had made me react half a beat late, I had easily blocked the Black Hand Fist Demon’s punch. Looking into his wavering eyes, I spoke calmly.
“A nobody. Right?”
He knew something had gone wrong. Too late.
I clenched my other, empty hand.
Fwoosh.
Blue-white flames surged around my fist.
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
KWA-AAANG!

sentences.text: The reconnaissance squad was made up of swift-footed elites, and it showed.
More than two hundred strong, they reached the northeastern border in barely three days, even with breaks along the way.

But none of them—not even the two tribal chieftains leading the squad—had expected another group of unwelcome visitors to arrive before they encountered the mysterious monster known as the Blood Monk.
And this unexpected situation was nothing compared to the news those visitors had brought.
“What... did you just say?”
“What are you talking about?”
Chief Jang and Chief Go stared wide-eyed in disbelief.
It was shocking news none of them had expected.
Had it come from anyone other than the Young Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, they would have dismissed it as nonsense.
In fact, they wished they could.
But despite their desperate wish, Yayul Mok’s answer did not change.
“It is all true.”
The truth was there in his trembling eyes.
The two chieftains could only sigh as they realized it had all happened.
“What in the world...”
“Why would the Palace Lord make that choice?
Why?”
Yayul Mok clenched his fists so tightly that blood ran from his palms before opening his mouth.
“My father had already guessed that he would be unable to resist the tide of events once so many chieftains had joined hands with Uncle Baek—no, with Baeksang.”
“Even so, did he bring this danger upon himself just to save a few Han Chinese?”
“He did not bring it upon himself.”
“What?”
“My father said this when he sent me and the others to the underground prison.
He said that repaying a righteous act with righteousness was keeping faith, and that turning away from someone who had helped us was injustice.
So today, I intend to stake my fate on keeping faith.
On those two people—Jin Taekyung and Baeksang.”
The two chieftains closed their eyes with low groans.
Having served at the Beast Miao King’s side for a long time, they had vaguely guessed what kind of person he was and what choices he would make.
But...
“This time, the Palace Lord was wrong.
He should have gathered all the strength of the tribes that followed him and the Miao people, then executed the traitors in the Inner Palace.”
“Even if we give Jin Taekyung every benefit of the doubt, trusting him may have been the right choice.
If the Young Palace Lord’s story is true, Jin Taekyung ultimately left alone in order to keep faith.
But Baeksang is different.”
As the two chieftains spoke with such certainty, Yayul Mok, who had been looking at them with a trace of hope, opened his mouth.
“It is too early to judge.
If Baeksang granted my father’s request...”
“Young Palace Lord.”
Chief Jang cut him off, his voice hollow.
“‘Subdue the Han Chinese in the reconnaissance squad and escort them to the Inner Palace.’ That is the first and last missive we received.
Do you understand what it means?”
Yayul Mok faltered.
Behind him, Namho, who had been watching quietly, suddenly understood.
He spoke almost in a groan.
“He kept them in the dark on purpose.”
“Elder Namho, you mean...”
“There is no need to say more.
The two chieftains here and the warriors in the reconnaissance squad are all people who follow the Palace Lord.
If they were told about the trouble in the Inner Palace, they would surely interfere somehow.
He probably intended to call them back after everything was finished.
Namho’s gaze darkened.
“Or... the Blood Monk.
He may have planned to let that old monster deal with them.”
“A borrowed knife to kill others.
Baeksang and Dark Heaven chose a useful blade.
No, in this situation, it isn’t even someone else’s blade.
There is a strong possibility that the Blood Monk is in league with them as well.”
A cold silence settled over the group.
Namho saw their shaken faces and felt his heart sink.
This is bad.
The worst.
Behind them lay the Nanman Beast Palace, likely in Baeksang and Dark Heaven’s hands by now.
Ahead stood a mysterious Supreme Peak master they could not face alone.
And Jin Taekyung, the one person they could count on most, was not here.
What are we supposed to do?
Even after a lifetime in the Hidden Shadow Pavilion, Namho had no easy answer.
But he had to decide before it was too late.
Amid the suffocating feeling that invisible chains were wrapped around his entire body, Namho finally forced his lips apart.
“Where are the others?”
Chief Jang understood.
“If you mean the Han Chinese, we detained them as a precaution.
We did them no harm—only struck their Sleep Acupoints.”
“You intend to send them back to the Central Plains?”
The question caught Namho squarely off guard.
After a brief silence, Namho nodded heavily.
“I’m sorry.
But for now, this is the best option.
If they cross the Yangtze and report what is happening in Nanman, the Murim Alliance will never stand by and do nothing.”
“...The Murim Alliance.”
“I was born in Nanman and spent half my life in the Central Plains.
Though I am nothing more than a powerless old man, I am someone who understands the circumstances of both Nanman and the Central Plains better than anyone.
If it is the Murim Alliance I know, they will find a way to help Nanman.”
His voice was calm, but his resolve was unmistakable.
Beyond the dense grass where they were lying in ambush, the two chieftains gazed at the broad, endless waters of the Yangtze before opening their mouths with sighs.
“Damn it.”
“What should we do?”
Namho had already made up his mind.
“There are two ways.
First, release the Han Chinese, leave this place at once, avoid Baeksang’s eyes, and wait for the right moment.
Second, head to the Central Plains together with the Han Chinese.”
“Head to the Central Plains together?
There is no ship of sufficient size anywhere around here.
How are we supposed to—”
“There is.
A ship that can take everyone.”
They turned toward the sudden voice.
Sama Pyo was staggering to his feet, supported by Taishan.
“Is that true?” Chief Jang asked.
At Chief Jang’s question, Sama Pyo answered with a pale face.
“How do you think we got all the way to Nanman?”
“Do you mean...”
“The swift ship of the Yangtze River Channel League is not far from here.
It’s half a day to the west.
If we travel for even half that time, we might be able to rendezvous with it.”
Hope lit the two chieftains’ faces.
If they followed a tributary of the Yangtze as far as Sichuan, they would be within the reach of the Central Plains Murim.

Even if Baeksang and Dark Heaven held the Nanman Beast Palace, reinforcements from the Murim Alliance—with the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families at their head—could turn the situation around.
There are already three prestigious great sects in Sichuan alone.
Even if the Murim Alliance’s official reinforcements are delayed, those three will be different.
Namho calmly considered their prospects.
The Emei Sect.
The Qingcheng Sect.
The Sichuan Tang Clan.
Even though they had shed much blood and weakened during the Sichuan Bloodbath, their roots ran deep and firm enough that even Dark Heaven could not tear them out in a single stroke.
Moreover, all three sects considered Jin Taekyung their Benefactor.
If they answered the call, gathered the strength of Sichuan Murim, and headed for Nanman...
Seven days and nights to return, if we’re fast.
Ten days at most.
Namho was neither a hot-blooded youth nor a martial artist who trusted in his own martial arts.
That was why his judgment was colder and more accurate than anyone else’s in this place.
Lead them back the way we came, and we’ll surely die.
Bring the Central Plains to our aid, and we have a real chance.
Until then, Jin Taekyung and the Beast Miao King will have to...
He could only trust that they would hold out.
That they would still be alive when the others returned.
Even Namho himself could not quite believe in that hope.
Then, as he held on to it—
Boom.
Boom.
Booooom!
Namho heard it.
No—everyone hidden in the forest above the endless river could see and hear it.
A low drumbeat.
A sleek hull approaching on the currents of the Yangtze.
“What is that...?”
“The Yangtze River Channel League!
It’s their swift ship!”
But the next moment, the two chieftains, who had been celebrating with brightened faces, sensed something strange and fell silent.
The swift ship should have been at least half a day to the west.
Why was it here?
They saw the rigid expressions on Namho’s and Sama Pyo’s faces, and their puzzlement turned to dread.
Namho spoke through a groan.
“Prepare for battle.”
Fear swept through the group.
Namho thought of the one person who was not at his side—the one he needed now more than ever.
Damn it.
I’m sorry.
They might die before they could save him.
Crash.
Boom.
The hull cut through the water without slowing and drove hard onto the sandy shore.
And then...
Step.
Where a wave had swept over the sand, one person’s footstep was etched into it.
Whoosh!
Two streaks of light cut through the air.
Despite their strange movements, the twin wheels came at me like flashes of light.
I swung White Flame diagonally downward to meet them.
KWA-BOOM!
Rumble-rumble!
A tremendous roar erupted as a shockwave tore through the area and shook the air.
But it was not over yet.
My five senses, sharp as blades, caught every movement of the twin wheels behind me.
They’re coming again.
As Muyaho slid backward, I caught him by the nape and twisted my body.
Whoosh—shhk!
A blue flash skimmed past me.
I heard a sharp slicing sound and saw the White Tiger’s snow-white fur scatter through the air.
In my tilted field of vision, another sight came into view: a wild-haired freak charging at me like a mad bison.
“You bastard—!”
The Black Hand Fist Demon.
Black Force layered itself over his dark fist, and then he shot it straight toward my chest.
Whoom!
I felt the air ripple.
Felt the terrifying power behind that punch.
But...
That won’t be enough.
With a brief mutter, I straightened the body I had twisted as far as it would go.
By then, the black Force had already reached point-blank range and was giving off an ominous light.
Beyond it, the Black Hand Fist Demon’s eyes gleamed with madness.
They seemed to say, You’re dead now.
I had seen that certainty in the eyes of many enemies before.
From Third Rate swordsmen to Supreme Peak masters.
Regardless of their level of martial arts, they had always worn that expression.
And when everything was over, I was always the one still standing on two feet.
Swish.
In the slowed-down world, the cool feel of the spear shaft slipped away from my hand.
The Black Hand Fist Demon had closed in so deftly that my spear had lost its advantage.
Without a moment’s hesitation, I let go and struck with my palm.
KWA-BOOM!
Two differently colored Forces collided with a roar.
Everything within a radius of ten-odd jang melted beneath the horrific heat, and the Black Hand Fist Demon’s eyes flew wide open.
One clash was enough for each of us to measure the other’s strength.
Even though the twin wheels had made me react half a beat late, I had easily blocked the Black Hand Fist Demon’s punch.
Looking into his wavering eyes, I spoke calmly.
“A nobody.
Right?”
He knew something had gone wrong.
Too late.
I clenched my other, empty hand.
Fwoosh.
Blue-white flames surged around my fist.
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
KWA-AAANG!

chapters.title: Chapter 680
paragraphs: The world crept by.
Blue-white flames surged around my fist, feeding on every sight that flashed past in that fraction of a second.
The punch I drove like a cannonball toward the Black Hand Fist Demon’s heart.
His bulging eyes and the hand he thrust out in haste.
The black Force giving way despite his efforts, and his Body-Protecting Qi shattering the instant it touched the flames.
Even the dazzling flash that came slicing through the space beyond them.
KWA-AAANG!
A tremendous roar. A violent tremor.
Everything happened in an instant, and ended just as quickly. Then a blast of hot air swept across the place.
No—the blast swept across everything within several dozen jang.
Mist born from the heat and steam of Scorching Yang Qi spread everywhere, blocking my view.
Whoosh...
I stood still, staring into the pale mist, until a voice drifted out of it.
“Truly astonishing. More than I expected.”
There was a faint note of genuine admiration in his voice. I drew White Flame back with Seizing an Object Through Empty Space and answered calmly.
“I’m pretty good for my age. I doubt even the Heavenly Demon or Martial God was this good.”
“How arrogant. Still, I’ll grant you that. You’ve earned the right to say it.”
“Listen to you talking about what I’ve earned. You got scared and interfered, and now you’re saying that?”
My voice sounded calm, but I was bitter inside.
Damn it.

That flash I’d seen at the last moment. If it hadn’t been for the twin wheels the slender old man had thrown, the Black Hand Fist Demon might have suffered a severe internal injury—or died on the spot.
I expected him to interfere, but his timing was too damn good.
I’d had only two choices: finish off the Black Hand Fist Demon and let the twin wheels take my head, making me a Dullahan candidate, or let him go and save my own life.
Naturally, I’d chosen the latter.
I changed the direction of my punch in midair and struck the twin wheels aside. The Black Hand Fist Demon did not even dare try to take advantage of the opening. He hurriedly pulled back.
The clash had started and ended in the blink of an eye. It might have looked like a draw, but I’d lost far more.

Having learned what I could do to him, the Black Hand Fist Demon would fight me with a caution he’d never shown before. An opponent’s carelessness was a weakness greater than any other, but you only got one chance to exploit it.
At this rate...
This wouldn’t be easy. No, it had become an incredibly difficult fight.
I searched for the figure hidden beyond the mist and called out.
“Black Hand? My dear Black Hand, who’s had fifty more years than me to learn martial arts and apparently learned them through his asshole instead. Where are you hiding?”
I thought he might ignore me. But the Black Hand Fist Demon was considerate enough to give my question his full attention.
“...Shut your damn mouth.”
“Is it just me, or are you talking a lot quieter than before? Did a taste of fire shrink your balls too?”
“...You bastard. You caught me off guard once, and now you’re full of yourself. Do you think you’ll get another chance?”
I let out a short laugh.
Given his martial prowess, he wasn’t entirely wrong to say I’d caught him off guard. But that was the kind of excuse a young prodigy made, not an old monster who’d lived as long as he had.
“You sound like a fucking idiot, and you know it. Right?”
“You—tearing you apart wouldn’t be enough...!”
“Enough.”
A cold voice cut off the Black Hand Fist Demon’s shout. A slender figure emerged from the mist still blanketing the area.
Step.
Mud baked hard by the terrible heat crumbled like sand beneath the old man’s foot.
He held a wheel in each hand, blades jutting from them like the teeth of gears. He gave his sleeves a light shake.
Whoosh...
A cold wind settled over the heat and swept away the mist, revealing what had become of the poisonous marshland around us.
It looked like a desert.
“So this is the Fire Gate Divine Technique I’ve heard so much about. Impressive. What stage have you reached?”
His admiration sounded genuine. I lowered my spearhead and answered.
“Three thousand twenty-five.”
“Is it just me, or is that a ridiculous number?”
“The realm of martial arts has no end.”
“A foolish question met with a wise answer. The Fire King raised his Disciple well.”
“He did, didn’t he? So why did your parents raise their kid like this?”
A parent insult, thrown hard and tight on the inside. The old man didn’t flinch.
“I suppose I’ll ask them if I ever find myself in the afterlife.”
Step.
He walked forward as if out for a stroll. I measured the distance between us.
“Since you brought it up, why not visit them today?”
“Unfortunately, I don’t expect to go anywhere near there for some time.”
“You shouldn’t put that off. Think how angry your parents must be in the Nine Springs. They worked their asses off raising you, and you won’t even visit.”
“You’ve guessed wrong this time. I’m an orphan, with no family in this world. No one cared for me growing up, so I can hardly be accused of being an unfilial son.”
Step.
His third step.

Muyaho had gone from a majestic White Tiger to Poppy after a disastrous grooming job with the twin wheels. He gave a low growl. I watched the wheels begin to turn slowly in the old man’s hands and muttered,
“Then you won’t be able to ask why they raised you this way when you get to the Nine Springs. You don’t know what they look like.”
“Now that you mention it, you’re right. Thank you for the advice.”
“What about the idiot creeping along behind you?”
The Black Hand Fist Demon spat out a brief curse. The old man answered calmly.
“Black Hand? He’s in a similar position.”
“I’m genuinely curious. Is that a requirement for joining Dark Heaven, or is it just a trend?”
The old man took another step instead of answering.
Step.
The sound rang unusually clear in my ears. At that moment, I saw blue light blaze from the twin wheels in his hands.
Hiss! Whoosh!

Two streaks of light flew toward me with faint sounds of splitting air. The twin wheels twisted through the air like living snakes. Beneath them, the Black Hand Fist Demon charged, madness gleaming in his eyes.
SHWAAAAAAK!
An attack from two directions. No—from three at once.
“GRAAAH!”
As the White Tiger roared behind me, I brought White Flame’s spearhead down with all my strength.
KWAANG!
The impact sent a violent jolt through my arms. I knocked one wheel aside, felt wind from my blind spot, and turned my head.
Whoosh—shhk!
It missed by a hair. Strands of hair severed by Force scattered through the air as the Black Hand Fist Demon closed to within three jang of me and snapped his tattered sleeves.
“Youuu!”
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
Palm Force burst from his outstretched hands, shaking the space around us. I eased my spearhead into the black Force rolling toward me like a wave.
Fire Dragon Divine Spear. First form.
Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.
Fwoosh—shaaaa!
Blue-white flames surged. The fire dragon’s tail split the black Palm Force and shot straight toward him. The Black Hand Fist Demon cried out in alarm and twisted aside.
Shhk!
A sharp cutting sound.
Unlike me, he hadn’t escaped with a few lost hairs. Blood dripped from the blunt end of his nose, whose tip had been sliced off before he knew it.
“You—you dare...”
I knew it now. Even if we fought ten more times, the Black Hand Fist Demon could never defeat me.
That old monster’s towering pride and the anger buried in his heart clouded his judgment. The smallest crack in it was an opening for me.
Now.
Flash!
One step.
The several jang between us vanished. More than a dozen possible moves flashed through my mind, and choosing one was easy.
Whoosh!
From sky to earth, my spearhead came down with a faint hiss. Blue-white flames rose along its edge.
Fire Dragon Divine Spear. Second form.
Heavenly Strike.
Fwoosh—KWA-AAANG!
A snowball grows as it rolls. A current swells into a wave when more water joins it.
The Black Hand Fist Demon looked up at the streak of flame crossing the air. His eyes flew wide.
With a startled cry, he thrust up both palms. The Palm Force he hastily summoned met the flames and faded away. In that brief instant, blue flashes came from my left and right.
SHWIIIIING!
My neck. My chest.
I couldn’t dodge both by moving. I made my decision in a split second and twisted the spearhead away from the Black Hand Fist Demon, swinging it at the wheels.
KWAANG!
Even someone like me couldn’t overcome the verdict contained in those four characters: force majeure.
SHRAAAK!
The tremendous rebound threw me off balance and sent me sliding helplessly backward. A pale figure rushed in like a ghost.
Shrik!
Not a word. Not even a breath.
Until now, the old man had stayed back and thrown his twin wheels. Now he entered the fight himself—calm and cold, each movement timed and placed with precision.
Just as he did now.
SHWAAK! THUD!
Hot and cold.
Though I twisted aside at the last moment, it made little difference.
Finger Qi erupted from the tips of fingers long and withered as tree branches and pierced my shoulder. White Flame’s spearhead, which had been driving toward the old man, wavered off course.
Dodging the weakened spearhead was easy for him.
Whoosh!
My spearhead cut uselessly through empty air. Gritting my teeth, I steadied myself and opened my free hand. Flames roiled around it as I drove my palm toward the old man’s chest.
Fwoosh—whoooom!
The Flame Divine Palm surged forward, burning everything in its path. I saw its flames reflected in his eyes, their heat beyond description, burning without pause.
Yet his eyes remained cold. A chill I couldn’t explain ran through me.
This is...
And the ominous instinct that seized my entire body soon revealed itself as reality.
Sss...
In a moment divided into fractions of a fraction, the old man slowly extended his hand.
No. He wasn’t the only one moving slowly.
My palm advanced toward his chest just as slowly. Behind each of us, the Black Hand Fist Demon and the White Tiger were charging toward the other.
Then cold flowed from the old man’s wrinkled hand, and time began moving again.
KRAK! SHHHHTZZZ!
Our palms met at last. Blue-white flames collided and mingled with pure-white cold.
KRRRUMBLE!
Everything was hot and cold at once.
Two lights of different colors flashed without cease before my eyes. Unprecedented internal energy shattered and shook everything around us.
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
A roar like heaven and earth splitting apart.
And I saw it. At the same time, I heard it.
“I’m late introducing myself.”
Powerful Yin-Cold Qi pressed down on the flames as they slowly died away.
“I am called the Great Snow Fiend.”
The cold voice drifted through a cloud of pure-white breath.
KRAAASH!

Blue-white flames rose along its edge.
Fire Dragon Divine Spear.
Second form.
Heavenly Strike.
Fwoosh—KWA-AAANG!
A snowball grows as it rolls.
A current swells into a wave when more water joins it.
The Black Hand Fist Demon looked up at the streak of flame crossing the air.
His eyes flew wide.
With a startled cry, he thrust up both palms.
The Palm Force he hastily summoned met the flames and faded away.
In that brief instant, blue flashes came from my left and right.
SHWIIIIING!
My neck.
My chest.
I couldn’t dodge both by moving.
I made my decision in a split second and twisted the spearhead away from the Black Hand Fist Demon, swinging it at the wheels.
KWAANG!
Even someone like me couldn’t overcome the verdict contained in those four characters: force majeure.
SHRAAAK!
The tremendous rebound threw me off balance and sent me sliding helplessly backward.
A pale figure rushed in like a ghost.
Shrik!
Not a word.
Not even a breath.
Until now, the old man had stayed back and thrown his twin wheels.
Now he entered the fight himself—calm and cold, each movement timed and placed with precision.
Just as he did now.
SHWAAK!
THUD!
Hot and cold.
Though I twisted aside at the last moment, it made little difference.
Finger Qi erupted from the tips of fingers long and withered as tree branches and pierced my shoulder.
White Flame’s spearhead, which had been driving toward the old man, wavered off course.
Dodging the weakened spearhead was easy for him.
Whoosh!
My spearhead cut uselessly through empty air.
Gritting my teeth, I steadied myself and opened my free hand.
Flames roiled around it as I drove my palm toward the old man’s chest.
Fwoosh—whoooom!
The Flame Divine Palm surged forward, burning everything in its path.
I saw its flames reflected in his eyes, their heat beyond description, burning without pause.
Yet his eyes remained cold.
A chill I couldn’t explain ran through me.
This is...
And the ominous instinct that seized my entire body soon revealed itself as reality.
Sss...
In a moment divided into fractions of a fraction, the old man slowly extended his hand.
No.
He wasn’t the only one moving slowly.
My palm advanced toward his chest just as slowly.
Behind each of us, the Black Hand Fist Demon and the White Tiger were charging toward the other.
Then cold flowed from the old man’s wrinkled hand, and time began moving again.
KRAK!
SHHHHTZZZ!
Our palms met at last.
Blue-white flames collided and mingled with pure-white cold.
KRRRUMBLE!
Everything was hot and cold at once.
Two lights of different colors flashed without cease before my eyes.
Unprecedented internal energy shattered and shook everything around us.
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
A roar like heaven and earth splitting apart.
And I saw it.
At the same time, I heard it.
“I’m late introducing myself.”
Powerful Yin-Cold Qi pressed down on the flames as they slowly died away.
“I am called the Great Snow Fiend.”
The cold voice drifted through a cloud of pure-white breath.
KRAAASH!

chapters.title: Chapter 681
paragraphs: For an instant, I wondered.
What if the Black Hand Fist Demon hadn’t been there? What if I’d dodged the Finger Qi?
What if the pain hadn’t risen from the shoulder pierced by the Finger Qi at the exact moment our palms met?
What if I had known that my opponent’s martial arts were based on Yin-Cold Qi?
If—if any of that had been different...
Who would be standing now?
But I had no time to find the answer.
KRAK!
The frozen flames died away. The Yin-Cold Qi that had swallowed even the fire swelled as though it might burst.
Beyond the unprecedented internal energy that shook the surrounding space, someone’s hand, engulfed in pure-white light, pressed against my chest.
Tap.
One thought filled my mind.
Cold.
KRAAANG!
A storm of cold swept out in every direction.
At its center, a fierce wind battered my entire body. The world flashed past, and an immense force slammed through my back.
KRRRUNCH!
Trees. Rocks. Grass. Even unknown creatures unlucky enough to be caught in my path.
Alive or dead, it made no difference.
Everything I struck as I flew backward like a misfired shell bent, shattered, or burst apart.
The thick stone wall standing across my path—a path I had no control over—was both a curse and a blessing.
KWAANG! RRRUMBLE!
Even through the haze, I could feel the excruciating pain.
The scenery finally stopped whipping past. So did I, after flying several dozen jang and burying myself deep in the stone wall.
Goddamn it.
I strained to speak, but no sound made it past my lips.
The world was red and blurry. A constant ringing filled my ears.
BEEP! BEEP! BEEP!
That was a little unusual, even for ringing ears.
“...Fuck.”
I raised my head with a hollow mutter.
More than a dozen holographic windows floated in the air. Instead of their usual clear chimes, they came with warning beeps.
That got me good.

I let out a bitter laugh. Pain rose without pause from injury after injury. The Yin-Cold Qi that had invaded my body left my hands and feet trembling, making a mockery of my Unaffected by Cold and Heat realm.
I have to get up. I have to fight again...
But my body wouldn’t listen. It felt as though every screw in it had come loose.
I was cold and tired.
If I closed my eyes, I felt like I could get a good night’s sleep for the first time in ages.
Yes. No dreams, no one waking me. I’d sleep until my back hurt, and everything would be better.

When I woke, the pain wracking my body would be gone. This goddamn body would work again. I’d curl up under a warm microfiber blanket and look at my smartphone, and Mom’s voice would come through the crack in the door.
“Jin Taekyung, Jin Hayeon. I’ve got dinner ready, so hurry up and come out.”

Then I’d shuffle into the kitchen and, despite what she’d just said, find the table empty. I’d set out the spoons and side dishes while Mom stood with her back to me, the savory smell of soybean-paste stew wafting over her shoulder.
Ah. This is nice.
Just thinking about it put me at ease.
The corners of my mouth rose, and my eyelids sank lower.
Sss...
Something rough and damp brushed across my face.
I slowly opened my eyes. The first things I saw were sharp teeth and clear blue-white eyes.
—Whine.
The White Tiger whined like a puppy as soon as our eyes met. I gave a quiet laugh.
“...Was that you?”
—Whine. Whiiine.
I couldn’t understand him, but I could tell what his cries meant. What he wanted to say.
“Phew.”
Breathing hurt.
It felt as though I’d woken from a long dream. So many thoughts had passed through my mind, but only a short time had gone by.
Crumbled stone rained down on my body, still lodged deep in a wall so thick I couldn’t judge its depth.
Only a few seconds had passed since I’d taken the blow. There was still time.
Thud.
I braced a hand trembling from the cold against the ground and muttered, “Stop crying. I’m not dead yet.”
I was answering him, but I was telling myself, too.
That was right. I was not dead yet, and even if my flame had briefly gone cold, it could flare up again and again.
Just like now.
Fwoooosh.
Internal energy surged from my lower dantian, heating hundreds of acupoints before spreading through my limbs and bones.
As I temporarily sealed the damage inside me, fiery pain swept through my body. Something surged up my throat.
Cough!
Dark red blood spilled from my lips. I paid it no mind. It was dead blood.
And the substance that had been gnawing away at my body and interfering with the flow of my internal energy was covered in pure-white frost the instant it touched the ground.
Fsssh.
Yin-Cold Qi. An extreme form of it unlike anything I had ever seen.
During the Shaolin Bloodshed, the Yin Freak—one of the Yin-Yang Twin Freaks who had led Dark Heaven’s martial artists in a surprise attack on Shaolin Temple—had not possessed anything like this.
“...So that’s how it is.”
After muttering under my breath, I rose without hesitation.
Tududuk.

Leaves and stone dust fell from my body at the sudden movement. A dull ache followed, but fresh warmth now filled me from within. My hand had stopped trembling, and my vision cleared enough to make out the two figures drawing near.
Step.
Footsteps slowly crossed the Poisonblood Grounds, which had changed from a swamp into a desert, and from a desert into frost-covered land.
The Black Hand Fist Demon followed several paces behind with a triumphant look on his face. I had eyes only for the man ahead of him.
That damn old man.
He walked at his leisure, as though admiring a landscape he had painted himself. I raised White Flame at an angle and watched him.
“Unexpected,” he said. “I was certain you wouldn’t be able to move after that.”
I knew his sobriquet now. Or perhaps it was more accurate to say I’d remembered it.
“That might be true for old men like you, Great Snow Fiend.”
“Youth is a fine thing. Yet you fail to understand that, in a situation like this, it will only bring you more pain.”
As he had until now, the Great Snow Fiend answered without the slightest wavering and continued.
“The fight is over. Surrender now, and I will spare your life. This is my first and last offer.”
“Senior! What are you saying?”
That wasn’t me. The Black Hand Fist Demon’s face twisted as he protested, but the Great Snow Fiend shook his head.

“The Demon Empress gave me the order herself. She said that letting him live would invite great trouble in the future, but that I was to capture him alive if possible. And we already have the upper hand.”
“Even so...!”
“Shut your mouth.”
“I know how you feel, but this is Heaven’s business. Question me again, and I will not forgive you.”
His tone and aura were icy. Even the half-mad Black Hand Fist Demon knew better than to keep arguing.
“This fucking...”
The Great Snow Fiend ignored the mutter slipping through the other man’s clenched teeth and held out a hand to me.
“It is foolish to continue a fight whose outcome is clear. Surrender and live to fight another day. Do that, and the Fire Gate Clan and the Jin Family of Taiyuan may preserve their lineages.”
I stared at him and answered.
Not with words, but with action.
Whoosh!
A sharp sound of air splitting rang through the air.
The Great Snow Fiend moved exactly half a step to avoid my spear strike.
“I believe I made myself clear. My first and last offer.”
“So?”
“I thought you were fairly clever, but you’ve chosen the foolish path after all. Can you not feel which way the battle has turned?”
“Which way it’s turned.”
I muttered the words and continued.
“Honestly, I do want to live. But I’m not the kind of bastard who surrenders or runs just because things have tilted a little. Unlike some people.”
The Great Snow Fiend paused. Then, as though he’d realized something, he gave a small nod.
“You know me.”
“I’ve heard of a sobriquet or two. White Rice Cake, Great Snow Fiend, something like that.”
“A child like you would hardly have heard that name... Fire King Jeok Cheongang. Did your master tell you?”
“Then do you think the fucking Heavenly Demon told me?”
I shrugged.

“He said if I ever met a son of a bitch who used twin wheels and Yin-Cold Qi, it would be the Great Snow Fiend or his successor. He said he wished he’d killed you himself, but after you killed the former Sect Leader of the Zhongnan Sect, you disappeared without a trace.”
“I feel the same regret. If this old man had met your master during the Great Faction War, I could have killed the Fire King and made my name resound throughout the world.”
“At best, you’d have been the Ice God instead of the Great Snow Fiend, you fucking idiot.”
For the first time, he reacted. It was slight, but his brow furrowed. I gave a quiet laugh.
“So you do have some pride. Then again, you ran away back then. Maybe you don’t.”
“I merely withdrew to fight another day. This old man is not foolish enough to stake his life on a fight when outnumbered.”

In truth, from what I’d heard, his decision had been cold and sound. He’d killed the former Sect Leader of the Zhongnan Sect, thrown their chain of command into chaos, then slipped away from Great Snow Mountain and vanished.
But...
“So what?”
“What?”
“You were scared, so you ran. You didn’t want to die. You were afraid of dying. That’s why you stayed hidden for so long.”
“You bastard...”

“It’s not like I’m criticizing you. I don’t want to die either. But once you’ve lived that many years, you should be honest every now and then—even about the things you don’t want to admit. Don’t you think?”
Deep lines creased the Great Snow Fiend’s brow. Powerful Yin-Cold Qi rose around him and pressed down on everything nearby.
“I heard you. When I next meet your master, I shall pass on your last words.”
Last words.
Maybe that’s how it will be.
I took a deep breath. This was no ordinary opponent. Facing two Supreme Peak masters while suffering from internal injuries was all but suicide.
Was I afraid of dying? Of course.
I’d feared death ever since I became a Hunter. Coming to Murim hadn’t changed that.
Now that I had taken one step toward accepting the word death in my heart, I was different from before.
I can do anything. Anything.
This wasn’t a fight to survive. It was a fight to kill.
And that meant I could charge in without holding my life back.
SHWAAAAAK!

chapters.title: Chapter 682
paragraphs: SHWAAAAK!
As Jin Taekyung charged straight toward him, the Great Snow Fiend thought, Yes. Come.

The boy’s sharp tongue had unsettled him for the first time in years, but it changed nothing. He had long since put aside the fact that his opponent was barely twenty, still a boy by any ordinary measure.
How could he afford to think of him that way? By the Great Snow Fiend’s reckoning, Jin Taekyung was a monster almost without precedent in history.
Even the Three Saints and Ten Kings—giants who had left their mark on Murim history—had not reached Supreme Peak until they were at least thirty. Jin Taekyung had done it at an absurdly young age.
Terrifying talent. And an absurdly young age.
Alongside Cheongpung of Huashan, the other genius who had inherited Sword Saint Mae Jonghak’s teachings, he was certain to become one of their most dangerous obstacles.
At the very least, within the next fifty years, he will grow into a monster capable of matching the Martial God and Heavenly Demon. He must be dealt with now.
The Great Snow Fiend did not know exactly why his direct superior, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, had ordered Jin Taekyung captured alive. At this moment, though, he trusted his own judgment.
Demon Empress, you are wrong this time. He... must never be allowed to live.
As he addressed her in thoughts she would never hear, the twin wheels within his sleeves let out a harsh howl.
WOOOOONG!
His martial arts and identity had already been exposed. There was nothing to gain by holding back.
The Great Snow Fiend focused every sense on Jin Taekyung’s rapidly approaching figure. His eyes flashed.
Now!
SHWING!
The rapidly spinning twin wheels left his wrinkled hand.
SHWAAAAK!

Filled with extreme Yin-Cold Qi, the twin wheels froze the space around them as they shot forward. The two blades traced grotesque paths according to the Great Snow Fiend’s will. At the point where they descended, Jin Taekyung had already closed to within three jang.
KWAANG!
Blue and white flashes mingled with a tremendous roar. Fire met ice.
With a single swing, Jin Taekyung knocked the twin wheels away, then burst through the mistlike steam that had settled over the ground.
SHWAAK!
He looked as swift as ever, but the Great Snow Fiend’s sharp eyes caught the difference.
He’s suppressing it for now. His internal injuries are still affecting him.
It was slight, but unmistakable. His movements had lost some of their precision, and his momentum had grown rougher.
To the Great Snow Fiend, Jin Taekyung looked like a wounded beast: claws still sharp, but tiring fast.
And the Great Snow Fiend was a seasoned hunter who knew better than anyone how to hunt such a beast.
At this rate, bringing him down is only a matter of time.
He even had a hunting dog beside him—the Black Hand Fist Demon. Not strong enough to sink its teeth into the beast’s neck, perhaps, but savage enough to charge in on the hunter’s behalf.
PAT-PAT!
“Black Hand!”
The hunter moved back. The hunting dog moved forward.
The Great Snow Fiend sprang back exactly as far as Jin Taekyung had advanced. At his shout, the Black Hand Fist Demon charged.
“Youuu!”
With a furious roar, he unleashed dozens of palm strikes packed with powerful internal energy.
KRAAAAA!
Black Force surged toward Jin Taekyung like a wave. At the same moment, the spear in his hand blurred.
SHWAAAAK!
Supreme Peak—a realm only the chosen could enter.
The young monster who had reached it at barely twenty thrust out his spear without hesitation. Blue-white flames coiled around the spearhead as it drove into the center of the black wave.
BOOM!
One strike, aimed precisely at one point.
Jin Taekyung split the wave of Force and burst through it. The Great Snow Fiend swept both hands downward, and the wheels Jin Taekyung had knocked away plunged from where they circled overhead.
SHWIIIIING!
They moved like living creatures.
Some might have called it Seizing an Object Through Empty Space, or Snake Sword, a technique performed with cords or threads. Both would have been wrong.
The Great Snow Fiend’s will alone moved the wheels. Powered solely by his Middle Dantian, they carried a single purpose.
Die.
Killing intent as cold as ice, directed at one man.
The two wheels bent in different directions and descended like flashes of light. At the same time, the Black Hand Fist Demon’s figure shot forward, trailing a savage momentum.
SHWING! SHWAAAAK!
Three flashes converged from three directions.
The Great Snow Fiend looked at Jin Taekyung, standing at the intersection of death, and felt certain.
If he clashes with Black Hand now, he won’t come away unharmed. He’ll retreat, and I’ll use that opening to...
Jin Taekyung rendered the rest of the plan useless.
PAT!
He advanced. Not an inch of retreat, not a moment of hesitation.
His spear flashed toward the wheels above his head. Then he drove out a fist like the forepaw of a tiger charging from the edge of a cliff.
KWAANG! KRRRUNCH!
The Great Snow Fiend saw it clearly.
THOOM!
Within the tremendous roar that sounded as if the sky were splitting apart and the flash of light that followed, a spear rose over Jin Taekyung’s shoulder.
SHWIIIIK! SHRAK!
He had lost his grip on his treasured weapon. As he clashed with the Black Hand Fist Demon, the twin wheels slashed across his shoulder like lightning.
SHRAK! FWOOSH!
Bright-red blood sprayed like a fountain. Jin Taekyung staggered.
At this wholly unexpected development that had unfolded in an instant, even the normally cold Great Snow Fiend faltered. He could not retrieve the twin wheels buried deep in the stone wall.
Why would he choose that?
He could not understand it. In Jin Taekyung’s place, he would have dodged without a second thought.
But his thoughts could go no further.
RRRRUMBLE!
A shock wave burst from Jin Taekyung and the Black Hand Fist Demon, shaking the space around them. Their fists had met in midair and now trembled, neither advancing nor giving way.
An even match.
The thought flashed through the Great Snow Fiend’s mind, and his figure blurred.
SHWIK!

Jin Taekyung was exhausted from his successive injuries. The fact that the Black Hand Fist Demon—despite being a Supreme Peak master like him, clearly a level below—had managed to match him for even a brief moment was proof.
The chance had come sooner than expected. The Great Snow Fiend was too practiced a hunter to miss it.
Now is the perfect time.
Even if it was wounded and bleeding, a beast was still a beast. The hunting dog called the Black Hand Fist Demon could never handle that young beast on its own.
Unless the hunter—the only one capable of tearing out the beast’s throat—stepped forward.
I must kill him. Right now.
His decision took an instant. His body shot forward like lightning.
FSSSH. At every step, Yin-Cold Qi flowed from him and froze the air.
In three steps, he crossed more than twenty jang. Over the Black Hand Fist Demon’s shoulder, he caught sight of his prey.
Jin Taekyung.
He could see him. Sense him.
Haa. Hah.
Ragged breaths. A pale face. The upper body the wheels had grazed was soaked in bright-red blood. As Jin Taekyung spotted the hunter bearing down on him, his eyes began to tremble.
I was right.
Certainty settled into the Great Snow Fiend’s cold gaze.
Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung. Heir to the Fire Gate Clan and successor to the Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
The Divine Dragon of the Central Plains, who would one day become a new Martial God and look down upon the world, would die before he ever rose above the clouds.
Today. Here.
The time for the hunt had finally arrived.
Ssssss.
Wind blew across the ground, bringing cold to air and earth that had briefly grown hot. It would cover mountains, rivers, trees, and grasses with frost.
For one man, that snow wind brought despair. For another, hope.
He’s here. He came!
The Black Hand Fist Demon barely held back a cheer.

The Great Snow Fiend always spoke to him as though he were a servant and looked at him as though he were far beneath him. If his martial arts had been strong enough, he might have killed the man long ago without alerting the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
But right now, the Great Snow Fiend was worth an army.
Watching Jin Taekyung hurriedly try to pull away, the Black Hand Fist Demon smiled with mad delight.
You bastard disciple of the Fire Gate Clan. Even tearing you apart limb by limb wouldn’t be enough. You will never escape.
KRRUNCH!

ZZZT. Heat like lava seared his hands, threatening to set them alight, but he did not care.
