Or so it should have.
The former Sect Leader of the Zhongnan Sect had worn that look when they met long ago on Great Snow Mountain. So had the Black Hand Fist Demon in the instant before his death.

His eyes slowly lowered.

KRRRUNCH!

As Jin Taekyung charged straight toward him, the Great Snow Fiend thought, Yes.
Come.
The boy’s sharp tongue had unsettled him for the first time in years, but it changed nothing.
He had long since put aside the fact that his opponent was barely twenty, still a boy by any ordinary measure.
How could he afford to think of him that way?

Terrifying talent.

Alongside Cheongpung of Huashan, the other genius who had inherited Sword Saint Mae Jonghak’s teachings, he was certain to become one of their most dangerous obstacles.

He must be dealt with now.

Demon Empress, you are wrong this time.

WOOOOONG!

Fire met ice.

He looked as swift as ever, but the Great Snow Fiend’s sharp eyes caught the difference.
He’s suppressing it for now.
His internal injuries are still affecting him.
It was slight, but unmistakable.
His movements had lost some of their precision, and his momentum had grown rougher.
To the Great Snow Fiend, Jin Taekyung looked like a wounded beast: claws still sharp, but tiring fast.
And the Great Snow Fiend was a seasoned hunter who knew better than anyone how to hunt such a beast.
At this rate, bringing him down is only a matter of time.
He even had a hunting dog beside him—the Black Hand Fist Demon.
Not strong enough to sink its teeth into the beast’s neck, perhaps, but savage enough to charge in on the hunter’s behalf.

The hunting dog moved forward.
The Great Snow Fiend sprang back exactly as far as Jin Taekyung had advanced.

KRAAAAA!
Black Force surged toward Jin Taekyung like a wave.

SHWAAAAK!
Supreme Peak—a realm only the chosen could enter.
The young monster who had reached it at barely twenty thrust out his spear without hesitation.
Blue-white flames coiled around the spearhead as it drove into the center of the black wave.
BOOM!
One strike, aimed precisely at one point.
Jin Taekyung split the wave of Force and burst through it.
The Great Snow Fiend swept both hands downward, and the wheels Jin Taekyung had knocked away plunged from where they circled overhead.
SHWIIIIING!
They moved like living creatures.
Some might have called it Seizing an Object Through Empty Space, or Snake Sword, a technique performed with cords or threads.
Both would have been wrong.
The Great Snow Fiend’s will alone moved the wheels.
Powered solely by his Middle Dantian, they carried a single purpose.
Die.
Killing intent as cold as ice, directed at one man.
The two wheels bent in different directions and descended like flashes of light.
At the same time, the Black Hand Fist Demon’s figure shot forward, trailing a savage momentum.
SHWING!
SHWAAAAK!
Three flashes converged from three directions.

THOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 683
paragraphs: BOOM!
Scorching heat tore through the Great Snow Fiend’s chest.
KRRRUNCH!
An immense impact swept through his entire body like a wave.
He coughed, and dark-red blood burst between his parted lips. His vision, clear a moment ago, grew hazy. It had been a long time since he had felt pain like this.
But as he crashed through a massive ten-thousand-geun boulder, what tormented him most was neither the pain nor his internal injuries.
He saw through my move? That brat?
He had defeated countless powerful enemies to reach this point. Now a young man barely twenty had outmaneuvered him. The thought made his head spin.
My judgment should have been correct.
He muttered the words blankly inside his mind, then shook his head.
No. It had been correct.
His formidable martial arts were not the only reason he had survived this insane Murim and its countless brushes with death.
Hide yourself. Know your opponent.
If his Supreme Peak martial arts were a sharp sword, his unwavering composure and cold judgment were both shield and hidden weapon.
But this was a first.
An opponent who did not fall to his sword, could not be stopped by his shield, and was untouched even by his hidden weapon. Someone who defied every judgment he had made.
How?
The Great Snow Fiend lifted his trembling eyelids and looked ahead.
FWOOSH.
The fierce snow wind subsided. Frost melted from the ground, and bitter heat mingled with the white breath spilling into the air.
At the center of it all stood one man.
Step.
Footsteps sounded in the silence. A figure emerged through the hazy steam, and the Great Snow Fiend saw a young man drenched in blood from head to toe.
In stark contrast, his eyes were clear and bright.

As the young man approached, the Great Snow Fiend pushed himself upright. Stone fragments pattered from his body, each one bringing a fresh stab of pain. He clenched his teeth, suppressed his internal injuries, and spat out a name.
“...Jin Taekyung.”
His voice was as cold as his thoughts were muddled. Jin Taekyung’s reply was perfectly calm.
“I’m surprised. I thought you wouldn’t be able to move after that.”
“What?”
“You’ve still got plenty of energy for an old man. But that’s no good in a situation like this. It’ll only make things more painful.”
The Great Snow Fiend’s eyebrow twitched as he realized something.

“Oh, I don’t mean anything by it. I think someone said something like that to me earlier, so I repeated it. Couldn’t have been more than... fifteen minutes ago. Can’t remember which fucking idiot was running his mouth, though.”
“Early-onset dementia?” Jin muttered. He glanced over his shoulder and sighed. “Ah, this is going to keep me up tonight. That old man lying over there might know. Mind if I go ask him?”
“I’ll be right back, okay?”
It was utter nonsense. There was no asking a corpse with a crushed heart a question, much less getting an answer.
Blatant mockery, not worth listening to.
Yet the Great Snow Fiend bit his lip before he knew it. Normally, such drivel would not have drawn the slightest reaction from him. Now he could not help being shaken.
“Just what... are you?”
He genuinely wanted to know. How was Jin Taekyung still standing on his own two feet? Why had he not fallen with the Black Hand Fist Demon?
“I saw it with my own eyes. It was no illusion, no clumsy act. How... how did you do it?”
Every word was true.

Powerful Yin-Cold Qi had thrown Jin Taekyung’s qi and blood into chaos, and the Force-wreathed twin wheels had cut him. That was why the Great Snow Fiend had remained certain until the final moment that his ice sword would kill both the wounded beast and the hunting dog.
Even his decision to kill the Black Hand Fist Demon had come from an experienced hunter’s caution. There was no telling what a beast driven to the edge of a cliff might do.
But he had been wrong. No—everything had been turned upside down.
The hunter had failed to kill the beast. The beast had sunk its teeth into the hunting dog’s neck and clawed the hunter’s chest.
Something that could not happen, should not happen, had happened.
Jin Taekyung watched the Great Snow Fiend’s uncomprehending face and murmured as if to himself.
“Yeah. Maybe it was.”
The Great Snow Fiend could not know what he meant. It was a gamble only one person in this world could have made.
Level Up.
One move that could overturn an overwhelmingly unfavorable battle.
Jin Taekyung had staked everything on it. He had willingly offered up his flesh to make his enemies lower their guard, and at last he had taken their bones.
If the EXP from the Black Hand Fist Demon hadn’t leveled me up... I’d be the one lying there.
But his gamble had paid off.
On the way to Ailao Mountain, he had fought more than ten battles. Breaking through the Poisonblood Grounds, he had killed hundreds of venomous beasts. Little by little, the EXP had accumulated.
Then he had added the Black Hand Fist Demon to it.
And I still had the ten points I got escaping the underground prison, plus the Fire Dragon Armor.
The Great Snow Fiend’s unexpected move had left him with internal injuries first, but that had meant he could bring those advantages out at the moment they mattered most.
It had been close. The result was what counted.

The punch Jin Taekyung had thrown with every ounce of his strength had taken the Black Hand Fist Demon’s life faster than the ice sword could, while the Great Snow Fiend’s ice sword had failed to pierce the Fire Dragon Armor completely.
Jin Taekyung suddenly remembered something he had heard long ago from a man who loved Go. Every time the man lost a game, he would shout, “Japs out! Chinks out!”
“Son, there’s a saying in Go: a large group doesn’t die easily.”
“Dad. Is that Buddhist?”
“No, no. A large group—a big formation of stones—is hard to kill.”
“Oh, I see. But Dad, why did you lose this game?”
“Because the large group died... Honey! Please take Taekyung away! Honey!”
A quiet laugh escaped him.
His father had been right. A large group did not die easily.
After a run of bad moves, one brilliant move could make it larger than any other stone and give it command of the board.
Just like now.
“Black Hand’s already gone ahead. Time for our Santa Claus to go see his parents, too. Just so you know, I don’t offer people a chance to surrender.”
SHING.
In his blood-soaked hand, White Flame’s spearhead leveled at the Great Snow Fiend.
The old man stared back through bloodshot eyes.
“Do not spout nonsense. You have gained a slight advantage, nothing more. This is not over.”
Jin Taekyung did not bother arguing. At least the damned old man was right about one thing: it was not over.
Sacrifice flesh to break bone.
The flesh he had given up had served its purpose, but a single level-up had not been enough to heal his earlier internal injuries and the wounds left by the twin wheels.
And just as he had risen again after taking the first attack, the Great Snow Fiend still had plenty of strength left.
“You will die, and this old man will live. That is the natural order, the mandate granted by Heaven.”
FSSSSSH.
Cold spread around them with his icy voice.
Even a full-strength blow from the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist had not put the old monster down. Jin Taekyung roused the fire dragon filling his lower dantian once more.
“Well, I can understand an old man becoming senile...”
FWOOSH.
Blue-white flames spread over the transparent spearhead, driving back the cold. Fire rose in his faintly warm eyes.
“But if some bastard from Dark Heaven starts talking about Heaven’s mandate, you won’t even get to see your parents after you die.”
At that moment—
POP!
The space between them vanished. Flame and cold collided.
KWAANG!
The world shook. The fire spear and ice sword met with a tremendous roar.
A shock wave that seemed to shake earth and sky swept outward. The explosion hurled both figures back, but neither yielded an inch before stepping toward the other again.
SHWIK!
One step. That was all the Great Snow Fiend needed. He shot forward in an instant and flicked his blood-soaked sleeve.
BOOM!
Cold fierce enough to freeze the air swept over a thousand-geun boulder embedded deep in the ground.
A rock?
The Great Snow Fiend looked up the moment he understood.
Half a beat ahead of him, Jin Taekyung had stepped on empty air as though climbing an invisible stair. Now he was falling, body and spear as one.
Fire Dragon Divine Spear.
Second Form.
Heavenly Strike.
KRAAAAA!
There was no time to think. The Great Snow Fiend swung his ice sword upward on instinct.
A streak of flame descended like a meteor and struck the blade.
KWAANG!
Fifteen minutes earlier, he could have blocked it without difficulty. Not now.
With his internal energy fully restored, Jin Taekyung’s attack was heavier and sharper than before. The Great Snow Fiend’s own internal injuries were no small matter, either.
Hngh.
Blood surged into his mouth. He swallowed it with a groan and turned his ice sword, sending the flames sliding into the ground, where they exploded.
The deafening blast flung him backward. Through his spinning vision, he sent the ice sword shooting toward the figure ahead of him as though he had thrown it.
SHWAAK! KWAANG!
Jin Taekyung knocked aside the ice sword hurtling at him faster than sound. Without hesitating, he drove his foot against the rock frozen by Yin-Cold Qi.
FSSSH. KRRRUNCH.
The ice melted. Web-like cracks spread across the hard stone.
Then a streak of flame rose.
KRAAAAA!
Flamefire Path.
Wrapped in blue-white fire, Jin Taekyung charged at the Great Snow Fiend—the old monster who dared defy the natural order while invoking Heaven’s mandate.
I can do this.
It was neither certainty nor complacency. He simply trusted himself.
Holding his breath, he cut through the space between them, took the spear shaft in a reverse grip, and sent it forward.
SHWAAAAAAK!
The flame-wreathed spearhead grazed past in an instant. It split the wind. It burned the air.
And at the end of its path stood a man.
“Ha!”
Too fast.
With a roar, the Great Snow Fiend gathered Yin-Cold Qi in both hands. White Force that seemed capable of freezing the world itself shot toward the spearhead.
No. It should have.
SHWIK! SLASH!
Pain struck his back.
Something trailing white fur and leaving a burning sting flashed across his vision. It raced onward without slowing, while the old monster’s judgment faltered.
Damn it. Baek...
The Great Snow Fiend swallowed the curse rising in his throat and thrust both palms with all his strength toward the blue-white hellfire filling his vision.
KWAAAAANG!
RRRRUMBLE!
A roar like the sky splitting apart shook the world.

Powerful Yin-Cold Qi had thrown Jin Taekyung’s qi and blood into chaos, and the Force-wreathed twin wheels had cut him.
That was why the Great Snow Fiend had remained certain until the final moment that his ice sword would kill both the wounded beast and the hunting dog.
Even his decision to kill the Black Hand Fist Demon had come from an experienced hunter’s caution.
There was no telling what a beast driven to the edge of a cliff might do.
But he had been wrong.
No—everything had been turned upside down.
The hunter had failed to kill the beast.
The beast had sunk its teeth into the hunting dog’s neck and clawed the hunter’s chest.
Something that could not happen, should not happen, had happened.
Jin Taekyung watched the Great Snow Fiend’s uncomprehending face and murmured as if to himself.
“Yeah.
Maybe it was.”
The Great Snow Fiend could not know what he meant.
It was a gamble only one person in this world could have made.
Level Up.
One move that could overturn an overwhelmingly unfavorable battle.
Jin Taekyung had staked everything on it.
He had willingly offered up his flesh to make his enemies lower their guard, and at last he had taken their bones.
If the EXP from the Black Hand Fist Demon hadn’t leveled me up...
I’d be the one lying there.
But his gamble had paid off.
On the way to Ailao Mountain, he had fought more than ten battles.
Breaking through the Poisonblood Grounds, he had killed hundreds of venomous beasts.
Little by little, the EXP had accumulated.
Then he had added the Black Hand Fist Demon to it.
And I still had the ten points I got escaping the underground prison, plus the Fire Dragon Armor.
The Great Snow Fiend’s unexpected move had left him with internal injuries first, but that had meant he could bring those advantages out at the moment they mattered most.
It had been close.
The result was what counted.

The punch Jin Taekyung had thrown with every ounce of his strength had taken the Black Hand Fist Demon’s life faster than the ice sword could, while the Great Snow Fiend’s ice sword had failed to pierce the Fire Dragon Armor completely.
Jin Taekyung suddenly remembered something he had heard long ago from a man who loved Go.
Every time the man lost a game, he would shout, “Japs out!
Chinks out!”
“Son, there’s a saying in Go: a large group doesn’t die easily.”
“Dad.
Is that Buddhist?”
“No, no.
A large group—a big formation of stones—is hard to kill.”
“Oh, I see.
But Dad, why did you lose this game?”
“Because the large group died...
Honey!
Please take Taekyung away!
Honey!”
A quiet laugh escaped him.
His father had been right.
A large group did not die easily.
After a run of bad moves, one brilliant move could make it larger than any other stone and give it command of the board.
Just like now.
“Black Hand’s already gone ahead.
Time for our Santa Claus to go see his parents, too.
Just so you know, I don’t offer people a chance to surrender.”
SHING.
In his blood-soaked hand, White Flame’s spearhead leveled at the Great Snow Fiend.
The old man stared back through bloodshot eyes.
“Do not spout nonsense.
You have gained a slight advantage, nothing more.
This is not over.”
Jin Taekyung did not bother arguing.
At least the damned old man was right about one thing: it was not over.
Sacrifice flesh to break bone.
The flesh he had given up had served its purpose, but a single level-up had not been enough to heal his earlier internal injuries and the wounds left by the twin wheels.
And just as he had risen again after taking the first attack, the Great Snow Fiend still had plenty of strength left.
“You will die, and this old man will live.
That is the natural order, the mandate granted by Heaven.”
FSSSSSH.
Cold spread around them with his icy voice.
Even a full-strength blow from the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist had not put the old monster down.
Jin Taekyung roused the fire dragon filling his lower dantian once more.
“Well, I can understand an old man becoming senile...”
FWOOSH.
Blue-white flames spread over the transparent spearhead, driving back the cold.
Fire rose in his faintly warm eyes.
“But if some bastard from Dark Heaven starts talking about Heaven’s mandate, you won’t even get to see your parents after you die.”
At that moment—
POP!
The space between them vanished.
Flame and cold collided.
KWAANG!
The world shook.
The fire spear and ice sword met with a tremendous roar.
A shock wave that seemed to shake earth and sky swept outward.
The explosion hurled both figures back, but neither yielded an inch before stepping toward the other again.
SHWIK!
One step.
That was all the Great Snow Fiend needed.
He shot forward in an instant and flicked his blood-soaked sleeve.
BOOM!
Cold fierce enough to freeze the air swept over a thousand-geun boulder embedded deep in the ground.
A rock?
The Great Snow Fiend looked up the moment he understood.
Half a beat ahead of him, Jin Taekyung had stepped on empty air as though climbing an invisible stair.
Now he was falling, body and spear as one.
Fire Dragon Divine Spear.
Second Form.
Heavenly Strike.
KRAAAAA!
There was no time to think.
The Great Snow Fiend swung his ice sword upward on instinct.
A streak of flame descended like a meteor and struck the blade.
KWAANG!
Fifteen minutes earlier, he could have blocked it without difficulty.
Not now.
With his internal energy fully restored, Jin Taekyung’s attack was heavier and sharper than before.
The Great Snow Fiend’s own internal injuries were no small matter, either.
Hngh.
Blood surged into his mouth.
He swallowed it with a groan and turned his ice sword, sending the flames sliding into the ground, where they exploded.
The deafening blast flung him backward.
Through his spinning vision, he sent the ice sword shooting toward the figure ahead of him as though he had thrown it.
SHWAAK!
KWAANG!
Jin Taekyung knocked aside the ice sword hurtling at him faster than sound.
Without hesitating, he drove his foot against the rock frozen by Yin-Cold Qi.
FSSSH.
KRRRUNCH.
The ice melted.
Web-like cracks spread across the hard stone.
Then a streak of flame rose.
KRAAAAA!
Flamefire Path.
Wrapped in blue-white fire, Jin Taekyung charged at the Great Snow Fiend—the old monster who dared defy the natural order while invoking Heaven’s mandate.
I can do this.
It was neither certainty nor complacency.
He simply trusted himself.
Holding his breath, he cut through the space between them, took the spear shaft in a reverse grip, and sent it forward.
SHWAAAAAAK!
The flame-wreathed spearhead grazed past in an instant.
It split the wind.
It burned the air.
And at the end of its path stood a man.
“Ha!”
Too fast.
With a roar, the Great Snow Fiend gathered Yin-Cold Qi in both hands.
White Force that seemed capable of freezing the world itself shot toward the spearhead.
No.
It should have.
SHWIK!
SLASH!
Pain struck his back.
Something trailing white fur and leaving a burning sting flashed across his vision.
It raced onward without slowing, while the old monster’s judgment faltered.
Damn it.
Baek...
The Great Snow Fiend swallowed the curse rising in his throat and thrust both palms with all his strength toward the blue-white hellfire filling his vision.
KWAAAAANG!
RRRRUMBLE!
A roar like the sky splitting apart shook the world.

chapters.title: Chapter 684
paragraphs: RRRUMBLE!
The earth shook with a thunderous roar.

Ancient trees whose roots had held for longer than anyone could guess. Boulders weighing ten thousand geun. Even the strange creatures of the Poisonblood Grounds that had been hiding somewhere, watching the battle with bated breath.
All were buried as the earth heaved and overturned like a wave.
KRRRUNCH!
It was hot.

At the center of the shock wave, I felt a scorching wind whip around me. There was not a trace of coolness in the muggy air, and the thick dust cloud covering dozens of jang left me unable to see a thing.

But I remembered clearly how the old man had driven both palms, packed with immense Yin-Cold Qi, toward the spearhead bearing down on him. I remembered the red blood gushing from his body, too, and the White Tiger’s figure disappearing into the distance in a flurry of white fur.
That bastard...

Muyaho’s sudden ambush on the Great Snow Fiend had not been planned. I had told him the opposite: stay out of the fight and find Yohi, who was probably being held captive somewhere in the Poisonblood Grounds.

Even if I died here today, I wanted that clever beast to get out alive. If he went to the Nanman Beast Palace with the two Great Chieftains, there would still be hope of preventing the disaster to come.
But Muyaho had ignored me, and his reckless, dangerous ambush had worked.
It was a tiny difference, but it was there. The unexpected attack slowed the Great Snow Fiend’s reaction.
Sending White Flame flying—practically an extension of myself—had been worth it.
A wounded hunter who had lost his composure was no longer a hunter. He was prey.
Where are you?
POP!
I muttered the question and shot forward.
Thick dust swirled around me. Soil and stones rained down on every side. They blocked my sight and masked every presence, so I drove a fist through them.
BOOM!
I did not even need to put internal energy into it. My fist broke the sound barrier, and compressed air burst outward under the force of the blow.
The enormous dust cloud split in two, revealing what lay beyond.
FWOOSH!
Hot wind swept past me. The instant I glimpsed someone’s blood-soaked clothes through the dust, I reached out without hesitation.
I had fought hard for this opening. Now that the balance was beginning to tip my way, I could not let it slip—even if it meant revealing abilities I had yet to show the Great Snow Fiend.
Inventory Open. Summon.
With the command in my mind, I hurled the spear that appeared in my hand with all my strength.
SHWAAAAK! BOOM!
It split the air and struck with a thunderous roar. Before the sounds had faded, another spear was in my hand.
SHWIK!
Again.
KWAANG!
And again.
More. More. More, more.
My body moved as fast as I could think. I twisted my waist, drew back my shoulder, and put my full weight behind each throw. The spears devastated everything around me like a bombardment.
RRRUMBLE!
I ignored the dust cloud as it began to rise again after briefly scattering.
I was pouring out attacks even more powerful than that.
Every spear was cheap iron, nothing compared to White Flame. But once I sent one flashing from my hand, no one it struck would come away unharmed.
Even a Supreme Peak master. No...
Not even the Great Snow Fiend.
BOOM! KWAANG! KRAAA-BOOM!
Explosions roared without pause. In a matter of moments, I drove more than ten spears into the earth like bolts of lightning.
Then I saw it.
KRRK! SPLAAASH!
Beyond the thick dust, bright-red blood scattered into the air to the grisly sound of torn flesh.
There you are.
Certain now, I stepped forward. The tip of my foot, bearing the weight of a thousand geun, dug deeply into the overturned earth.
KRRRUNCH. BOOM!
An explosion occurred at the same time as I compressed my internal energy. I surged forward, erasing more than ten jang of space in an instant, and plunged into the dust cloud.
The noise and falling debris had made it nearly impossible to tell front from back. But I did not hesitate.
I’ve already seen him.
My sharp senses detected the metallic scent of blood, and my keen eyesight once again found someone’s back through the dust cloud.
The Great Snow Fiend had been injured blocking White Flame. He could not be faster than me now.
I summoned a spear from my Inventory and slashed it down diagonally.
SHIIING.
With a low sound of splitting air, blue-white flames rose around the spearhead and slowly cut through the wind.
But the spearhead was not the only thing that had slowed. Extreme concentration paralyzed my brain and brought the world to a standstill.
In that frozen moment, the flames parted the dust and touched the edge of the man’s clothes. Certainty flashed through me.
It’s over—!
Then why did I feel this inexplicable chill? This strange sense of déjà vu?
One more chi would end everything. Why was my body trying to retreat against my mind’s command?
I understood at once. It was reason, but it was instinct too—instinct that had acted before reason could.
The Great Snow Fiend.
An old monster who had crawled out of the depths of a distant past. But what made him dangerous was not that he was a Supreme Peak master who had opened his Middle Dantian.
He possessed something the overwhelmingly powerful Blood Lord and Western Heaven Demon Lord had lacked—or had never felt any need for.
Caution. Thoroughness. Those were the old monster’s sharpest weapons.
The Great Snow Fiend, this easy?
No. Not the Great Snow Fiend I had fought.
In a fraction of an instant, I twisted with all my strength. My body stopped short, and the internal energy surging through me like a raging sea reversed course.
Hot blood welled up in my throat. My spearhead veered in midair and sliced through the clothes.
Then I saw it clearly.
SHNK.

In the slow-moving world, flesh and bone parted beneath the spearhead like tofu. Blood drifted upward as though weightless. Beyond it, disheveled hair fluttered, and over the shoulder of a corpse already dead, a pair of cold eyes gleamed.
I’ll return it to you. Exactly the way you did.
I felt those words from a voice I could not hear.
Then a bitterly cold flash erupted from the gaping hole in the Black Hand Fist Demon’s chest.
SHWAAASH!
I knew at once. I could not dodge this attack.
But I could avoid a fatal wound. Covering my upper body was Fire Dragon Armor, the extraordinary divine weapon I had gained by killing the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
But...
KRRUNCH! THUD!
Cold—and hot at the same time.
The Yin-Cold Qi seeping into my body. And the spearhead of another divine weapon, White Flame, which had broken through Fire Dragon Armor and lodged in my chest.
BEEP. BEEP. BEEEEP!

System Part of Fire Dragon Armor has been destroyed by powerful energy! - Time remaining until Fire Dragon Armor is automatically repaired: 3 days Yin-Cold Qi is violently shaking your insides! - Status abnormality: Bleeding Status abnormality: Massive Internal Injury There is a risk of qi deviation! Calm your energy as soon as possible! - Your body has suffered severe internal and external damage!
My vision grew hazy from the horrible pain. As warning sounds continued to pierce my ears without pause, I thought:
This was truly turning out to be one hell of a day.
Jin Taekyung was not the only one who felt the world stop in that instant.

Hidden in the dust, waiting for his final chance, the Great Snow Fiend felt it too. After the longest, hardest wait of his nearly century-long life, he could finally let out the breath he had been holding.
KRRUNCH. THUD!
A spearhead buried in a man’s chest. A body trembling. Eyes filled with pain and despair.
“Gueeek!”
SPLASH!
Dark-red blood mixed with bits of organs splattered across the Great Snow Fiend’s face.
The foul, bloody stench filled his nose, but it did not bother him. No, what stunned him was the sight of that young bastard still alive.
What a lunatic.
The Great Snow Fiend’s plan would have been perfect if Jin Taekyung had not twisted away at the last moment. The spearhead meant for his heart had struck his chest instead.
And if this old man hadn’t adjusted the thrust to follow him... it would only have caught his side.
A chill ran down the Great Snow Fiend’s spine.
He had revised his assessment of Jin Taekyung long ago.
Not fifty years. Thirty. No—perhaps in twenty, he’ll rival the Martial God and the Heavenly Demon.
A monstrous talent. A determination fiercer than fire.
It went beyond martial arts. It was strength that came from the man himself, an aura that inspired not merely wariness but fear.

In the Great Snow Fiend’s eyes, Jin Taekyung was already strong enough to stand beside the leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families. Even beside the Ten Kings, he would not fall short.
But this is as far as you go.
GRIND.
The Great Snow Fiend gritted his teeth and tightened his grip on the spear shaft.

His right sleeve hung empty, as though something had torn the arm from it. He had lost it to the White Tiger’s ambush and the spear that had come crashing down immediately afterward. He had no regrets.
An arm was nearly as precious as his life, but Dark Heaven’s uncanny sorcerers would surely find a solution without much difficulty.
What mattered now was that he could finish Jin Taekyung—that terrifyingly tenacious monster.
Did I not tell you? You will die, and this old man will live. That is the natural order. Heaven’s mandate.
Fear and joy mingled on the Great Snow Fiend’s face as he gathered the little strength he had left.
The cool shaft of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron drove deeper into Jin Taekyung’s chest.
KRRUNCH!
The spearhead, wreathed in cold instead of flame, dug into its owner’s chest. Flesh split, bone cracked, and Jin Taekyung’s body jerked.
PFFT. SPLAAASH!
Blood spurted like a fountain. His eyes slowly dimmed.
The Great Snow Fiend had watched countless people die. He had never been more certain.
No one can save him now. Not the Divine Physician. Not even the Great Firmament Immortal.
But he had forgotten something.
The young man dying right before his eyes was an existence akin to supernatural powers—something that could not be predicted by his judgment.
GRAB. THRUST!
He had neither time nor strength to respond.
In his eyes, coldness gave way to shock. Reflected there was Jin Taekyung, gripping the spear shaft with all his strength and pushing himself forward, driving it deeper into his own chest.
And in his blood-soaked hand, the last flame burned.
Blue-white light-flames spread across the Great Snow Fiend’s widened eyes.
FWOOSH—KWAANG!

chapters.title: Chapter 685
paragraphs: FWOOSH. KWAANG!
Blue-white light-flames filled the Great Snow Fiend’s vision.
An explosion sounded as though announcing the end of everything. His aged body flew through the air in an arc and slammed into a massive boulder, shattering it.
KRRRUNCH.
His blood-red vision grew hazy. The sounds reaching his ears seemed to come from hundreds of li away.
And yet his mind remained startlingly clear.
Like a candle burning brightest just before it went out.
A final rally.
The four characters flashed through the Great Snow Fiend’s mind. At the same time, something hot rose in his throat.
COUGH.
Dark-red blood soaked his lower body. Bits of organs were mixed in with it. He stared blankly at the mess, then realized something.
No. He was certain.
This time, there could be no mistake.
It’s over. All of it.
Strange as it was, pain was how people knew they were alive.
Yet even with the meridians throughout his body torn apart by Scorching Yang Qi, his flesh and bones crushed, the Great Snow Fiend felt no pain.
Only fear.
Fear of the death finally looming before him, and of the figure approaching through his blood-red vision.
“Jin... Taekyung.”
The name escaped his trembling lips in something like a moan.
No answer came to the dying old man.
No—Jin Taekyung could not answer.
DRIP. DRIP.
Blood fell with every step he took. He staggered as though he might collapse, his eyes unfocused.
But he was alive.
With his beloved spear lodged near his ribs, Jin Taekyung was coming toward the Great Snow Fiend, fighting off even the death closing in on him.
How can this be...?
It was not just death or the cold that made the Great Snow Fiend tremble.
He was afraid. And he wanted to know.
They were made of the same flesh and blood. How was that young monster still standing? What had brought the two of them to this?
Where did it begin? What went wrong?
Nearly half a century had passed since he had left his family, subordinates, and friends behind and departed his homeland alone.
To overcome his limits, he had created new martial arts. He had risked death countless times and devoted his life to perfecting them.
The righteous path? He had never cared for that shallow phrase hypocrites liked to spout.
He had to survive, whatever it took. And if he was ever to return home, he had to become strong enough that no one could ignore him.
Without that single-minded purpose, he would never have taken the hand Dark Heaven offered him decades ago.
The day the Lord of Heaven descends upon this land, everything you desire will come true.
Everything...?
Yes. If that is what you want.

The Great Snow Fiend had believed those words. He had pledged himself to Dark Heaven. At the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s command, he had even taken on a successor—something he had never imagined doing—and taught him the martial arts he had created.
All while waiting for that day.
So why?
“Why should this old man—why should I die by your hand? Why!”
The Great Snow Fiend raised his head with that strangled cry and saw a pair of eyes still holding a flame that had not gone out.
A faint voice reached him.
“Because I have a reason.”
What?
“A reason I have to survive, no matter what. A reason I sometimes have to risk dying.”
“That’s the biggest difference between us.”
Jin Taekyung reached out with a trembling hand. His blood-soaked fingers closed around the spear lodged in his chest.
SPLASH. DRIP, DRIP.
He drew the spearhead out slowly. Blood came with it, spattering across the Great Snow Fiend’s face.
Jin Taekyung convulsed in agony, and the Great Snow Fiend laughed as though he had lost his mind.
“Follow me soon. I’ll be waiting in the afterlife.”
SWISH.
The wavering spearhead touched his throat. Jin Taekyung muttered, his voice worn thin.
“Idiot. Go find your parents.”
And that was the end.
SHNK.
The cold blade pierced his throat.
In a moment that seemed to stretch on while everything else stood still, the Great Snow Fiend watched the world darken. It was nowhere near enough time to look back over the century he had lived.
Damn it.
The curse never left his lips. The old monster who had dominated an era fell into deep darkness.
No one survives a spearhead through the throat.
Not a Supreme Peak master with several jiazi of Yin-Cold Qi. Not a fiend who has lived nearly a century.
Just as it was now.
SHNK.
The transparent spearhead pierced his throat, and that was it.
The Supreme Peak master once known as the Great Snow Fiend was gone.
I stared blankly down at the corpse, its eyes wide open and its body frozen in place, then let out a short groan.
It was over. Finally.
The moment I recognized reality along with the thought filling my mind, the world tilted.
SLIP.
No. I was tilting.
I tried to stay on my feet, but there was nothing I could do. The last scrap of strength left my hand, and the spear shaft slipped from my grip.
THUD.
My vision blurred. Pain, exhaustion, and relief—everything I had managed to forget for a moment—came crashing over me.
I collapsed where I stood and lay gasping, staring into the air.
System You have defeated Level 155 Hanbaek! - You have acquired a massive amount of EXP! - You have acquired a massive amount of Fame!
That was all.
There were three numbers in the holographic window visible through my blurred vision. None of them announced a level-up, and the System remained silent.
And I...
This would be pretty lame if it were a hidden-camera prank.
I laughed at the stupid thought. There was no particular reason. The corners of my blood-crusted mouth lifted, and a hollow chuckle escaped.
Fuck. Hidden-camera prank, my ass.
Right. So that’s how it is.
How long could I last like this?
Fifteen minutes? Seven and a half?
Should I just be glad Muyaho got away alive?
It was strange. My last hope had fallen apart, but I felt calm enough to surprise myself.
Maybe I had seen it coming, somewhere deep down.
Luck doesn’t come twice in a row.
The level-up I had gained from killing the Black Hand Fist Demon had been a gamble in the first place. Without a way to see my exact EXP, I could only guess.
That should be enough to level up.
Or:
No. That won’t do it.
Unfortunately, this time it was the latter.

The Great Snow Fiend had left behind a massive amount of EXP, just as the System said. But it was less than what I had earned on the way to the Poisonblood Grounds and from the Black Hand Fist Demon combined.
Or maybe my earlier stroke of luck had raised the amount I needed for the next level.
Either way, the conclusion was simple. My first gamble had paid off. My second hadn’t.
As if Heaven had decided my fate from the start.
Damn fate.
Fate. I had hated that word for a long time.
It could mean something good, sure. But it was also two little characters you could use to lump together every fucked-up thing that happened in the world.
Some things in life were too cruel and hopeless to shrug off as fate.
Like the memory of a certain day I kept hidden in one corner of my heart.
“Um, Mr. Kim?”
“Oh! Yes, Vice Principal. What brings you here all of a sudden...?”
“Sorry to interrupt your class, but could we talk outside for a moment?”
Even now, I remembered it like a scene from a cheap black-and-white movie.
Scene one: The bald vice principal appeared, cleared his throat, and left with my homeroom teacher.
Scene two: Through the glass window in the classroom’s front door, I watched my homeroom teacher’s bewildered face slowly harden.
And scene three: After returning to the classroom, my homeroom teacher called out a student’s name after a brief silence.
“Taekyung. Could you come outside for a moment?”
That was how I went from Extra Number One to the star of the movie.
No. I had never wanted to be the star. I wished it really had been a movie. Then I could have half-killed the screenwriter and director behind that shitty story until they called for another take.
But life is one take.
With every moment and every choice, the story flows with me at its center.
I had never given life a serious thought until I saw my father beneath a white sheet.
Cause: a Monster Wave. Cause of death: crushing.
That was when I understood. My father’s story had ended because of that damn word, fate, and mine had begun.
“...COUGH.”
SPLASH. DRIP, DRIP.
But I didn’t want the last scene of my story to be me bleeding from my seven apertures on the cold ground.
No soft music over ending credits listing my family, friends, and comrades, either.
I still had a chance to defy this damn fate. A third chance to put my life down as the stake before it burned to ash and scattered.
I want to live.
That single thought filled my head.
It was as simple as that. I didn’t want to die here. There was too much I still had to do, too many people I had left behind.
CRUNCH.
I mustered what little strength remained and bit my tongue. The sharp pain brought my fading sight and mind back into focus, if only a little.
Now.
I opened my trembling hand and gave the command in my mind.
Inventory Open. Summon.
SWISH.
Something cool and smooth settled against my palm. At the same time, two very different System alerts sounded in my ear.
DING.
System Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence has been summoned successfully!
BEEP!

System Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence contains an immense amount of qi unlike any ordinary elixir. Exercise extreme caution before consuming it! - Your Scorching Yang Qi is incompatible with the water qi contained in Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence! This is extremely dangerous. Exercise caution!
I knew. I knew this was insane.
What I was about to do went against the principles of Yin and Yang and the Five Elements—the foundation of most internal energy cultivation techniques.
Pouring water on fire. It was like trying to evolve Charmeleon into Blastoise.
But...
There’s no time.
To hell with incompatibility. Whether I bled to death in fifteen minutes or exploded because I couldn’t contain the Origin Essence’s power, I’d be dead either way.
At least the second option gave me a sliver of a chance.
GURK.

I spat up another surge of blood, squeezed out what little strength I had left, and pushed myself upright. Fighting through pain that made my body feel as though it were crumbling, I sat cross-legged and looked up at the sky.
Fuck, look at those storm clouds. Even the sky has to be dark as hell.
It was partly because it was nighttime, but no matter how I looked at it, this was a perfect day to hate dying.
No one was watching, and there wasn’t even anyone to stick a cigarette in my mouth. Not that I’d smoke it if there were.
HAAH.
My trembling breath drifted away instead of cigarette smoke.
Night wasn’t the only reason my briefly clear vision was darkening again.
I was dying. Quickly.
The moment for my final gamble was almost here.
Now.
I lifted my convulsing hand to my mouth and swallowed the blue pearl, filled with impossibly pure and dangerously vast qi.
Or I tried to.
Until cool qi suddenly swept in from somewhere and engulfed me.
FWOOSH!
What?
Every hair on my body seemed to stand on end. I froze like a statue, and one word flashed through my mind.
Enemy!
But it wasn’t. Something had brushed past me, yet I was still alive. Then a thunderous roar in the distance drove the question from my mind.
“GRAAAAH!”
I had been sure he’d escaped. I’d told myself to be glad at least he had survived.
You came back after all.
My sight was blurred, but the snow-white body shone bright enough to recognize even in the dark.
Nor was it difficult to make out the figures of two people sitting on the back of the White Tiger as it raced toward me like the wind.
Heugung. And Yohi.
As their faces came into view, I remembered the Quest I had forgotten for a moment.
Then I stared blankly up at the sky and muttered:
“Just as I thought. It’s a perfect day to hate dying.”
DING.

System Mission: Find Yohi (Complete). - Quest I Can See Your Tracking Scent has been completed successfully! - You have acquired a substantial amount of EXP! - You have acquired a substantial amount of Fame! Level Up!
I could feel it.
Death falling away from me. A gentle warmth wrapping around my wounded, exhausted body.
DING. DING. DING.
Clear bells rang beneath the storm-clouded sky. I slowly closed my eyes.
SLIP.
With no moonlight to be seen, the sleep demon came pouring down instead.
It was stronger than any enemy I had ever faced.

chapters.title: Chapter 686
paragraphs: Jin Taekyung fell into a sleep so deep it was almost unconsciousness. At nearly the same moment, Muyaho, who had been racing like the wind, stopped in his tracks.
THUMP.
Leaning against a shattered boulder, Jin’s head drooped.
Yohi caught her breath. Heugung had climbed down from Muyaho’s back a step ahead of her and was checking Jin’s pulse. He let out a sigh.
“Whew. Fortunately, he’s still alive.”
It was good news, but Yohi’s face did not brighten.
“Still?”
Only then did Heugung realize how his words had sounded.
“I misspoke in my haste. He’s not at death’s door. I don’t think you need to worry too much.”
“Not at death’s door? Looking like that?”
Yohi had every reason to doubt him.

Jin Taekyung was drenched in blood from head to toe. His clothes were torn and slashed all over, and the unidentified armor covering his upper body was shattered at the chest, as though something had pierced it.
It was hard to believe he was alive at all.
Yet Heugung was telling the truth.
“I’ve examined him. His injuries aren’t as serious as we might think. But these wounds... I can hardly believe what I’m seeing.”
Although their internal energy had been sealed for the time being, both of them were martial artists who had reached the Peak realm.
The two Great Chieftains could not reconcile the wounds they saw with Jin’s condition, but they breathed a sigh of relief when they realized his life was not in immediate danger.
That relief had barely settled when they noticed someone lodged in the massive boulder Jin was leaning against.
Yohi stifled a cry.
The unidentified old man was frozen there with his eyes wide open. He was already dead. Blood still flowed from his throat, pierced by a snow-white spearhead.
THUD. DRIP, DRIP.
Yohi stared at the old man, every bit as blood-soaked as Jin, and murmured, “That’s him.”
“Who?”
“The one who spoke to Black Hand as if that old man were his subordinate.”
“Ah.”
“And if I’m right...”
Yohi swept her gaze across the area. It stopped on the corpse of the Black Hand Fist Demon.
He had slaughtered the warriors of the Western Yao Estate with the prowess of a fiend. Now he lay dead with a gaping hole in his chest.
This is impossible.
Yohi’s eyebrows trembled. She had begun to suspect it when she found the unidentified old man, but what had happened here went far beyond anything she had imagined.
She was not alone.
“How did he...”
Heugung swallowed the rest. It made no sense, but the scene before them was real.
The surroundings had been devastated by a force unlike anything they had seen. Two old men lay dead. One young man slept alone.
The conclusion was plain.
Jin Taekyung had fought and won—against two Supreme Peak masters who had devoted several times as many years to martial arts as he had been alive.
“...Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.”
The sobriquet slipped from Yohi’s red lips like a groan. Awe filled her eyes as she looked at Jin.
Whether it should have been possible no longer mattered. He had made it possible, willingly risking his life to save them, though they were only southern tribespeople to him.
Now it was their turn to act for him.
It may already be too late. But I have to act now.
Some of Nanman’s venomous beasts shed their skins at certain times. They molted.
A new body did not come easily. Succeed, and the creature emerged more beautiful and stronger. Fail, and it slowly died in its old, ailing body.
Yohi chose the first path.
If I wait any longer, it’ll all be over. I have to tell everyone what happened.

They had to expose Baeksang’s conspiracy and stop Dark Heaven. Her own wrongdoing would come to light along with it, but she had made up her mind. She would bear the full cost of the path she had chosen.
I never should have done it.
Looking back, she felt nothing but regret.
Baeksang had laid a broad, beautiful road of silk before her. Yohi had walked it all the way here, turning a blind eye to everything happening around her.
But when she reached the end and happened to look down, she saw that her feet had long since become covered in blood.
Not her own. The blood of other Nanman people.
Now she wanted to wipe it away. If she could not, she would cut off her feet.
One person, more than any other, had brought her to that decision.
Jin Taekyung.
A stranger from a foreign land. Yet he had fought for Nanman more than anyone—just as the former Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan had done centuries ago, before he passed into legend.
I may be a Great Chieftain, but I can’t be worse than a Han Chinese person.
If a bitch like me can even call herself a Great Chieftain...
Yohi swallowed the self-mocking words and immediately sprang into action.
RRRIP.
Without a moment’s hesitation, her slender white hands tore at her ornate gown. She removed her gold and silver jewelry as well, baring her arms and legs. Heugung’s eyes widened.
“Yohi.”
“There’s no time to talk. We need to move now.”
Heugung studied her in silence for a moment, then nodded.
“You’re right. More enemies could arrive at any time.”

“Considering how quiet it’s been around us until now, it’s safe to assume there aren’t any others. No, they probably decided Dark Heaven didn’t need to send more support after arranging for two Supreme Peak masters to come here.”
“Probably. They knew about the tracking scent you carried. They must have meant to use us as bait to draw in Palace Lord Yayul. He would be Dark Heaven’s greatest obstacle right now.”
But Jin Taekyung, not the Beast Miao King, had taken the bait. The hunters had become the hunted.
No one, not even Dark Heaven, could have predicted that.
The longer they talked, though, the heavier Yohi’s heart grew.
“What if Jin Taekyung didn’t come in the Palace Lord’s place? What if the Palace Lord couldn’t come?”
“That...”
“My tribespeople were massacred. The Western Yao Estate. Nothing like this has ever happened before. The Inner Palace must be in an uproar by now.”
“Then shouldn’t we go to the Inner Palace as quickly as possible?”
Yohi shook her head. She had shut her eyes and ears for the sake of her ambitions, but she was no fool.
Dark Heaven had won over Baeksang, the Beast Miao King’s sworn younger brother, then waited decades for the right moment.
She remembered what the unidentified old man now buried in the boulder had said.
“If you act rashly when the grand plan is so close, I will not forgive you.”
The grand plan.
Yohi sensed indescribable danger and anxiety in those two words. She also realized that their abduction had been a carefully calculated act.

At nearly the same moment, Muyaho, who had been racing like the wind, stopped in his tracks.
THUMP.

Yohi caught her breath.

Looking like that?”

It was hard to believe he was alive at all.

“I’ve examined him.

But these wounds...

Yohi stifled a cry.
The unidentified old man was frozen there with his eyes wide open.
He was already dead.
Blood still flowed from his throat, pierced by a snow-white spearhead.
THUD.
DRIP, DRIP.
Yohi stared at the old man, every bit as blood-soaked as Jin, and murmured, “That’s him.”
“Who?”
“The one who spoke to Black Hand as if that old man were his subordinate.”
“Ah.”
“And if I’m right...”
Yohi swept her gaze across the area.
It stopped on the corpse of the Black Hand Fist Demon.
He had slaughtered the warriors of the Western Yao Estate with the prowess of a fiend.
Now he lay dead with a gaping hole in his chest.
This is impossible.
Yohi’s eyebrows trembled.
She had begun to suspect it when she found the unidentified old man, but what had happened here went far beyond anything she had imagined.
She was not alone.
“How did he...”
Heugung swallowed the rest.
It made no sense, but the scene before them was real.

Two old men lay dead.
One young man slept alone.
The conclusion was plain.
Jin Taekyung had fought and won—against two Supreme Peak masters who had devoted several times as many years to martial arts as he had been alive.
“...Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.”

Awe filled her eyes as she looked at Jin.
Whether it should have been possible no longer mattered.
He had made it possible, willingly risking his life to save them, though they were only southern tribespeople to him.
Now it was their turn to act for him.
It may already be too late.
But I have to act now.
Some of Nanman’s venomous beasts shed their skins at certain times.
They molted.
A new body did not come easily.
Succeed, and the creature emerged more beautiful and stronger.
Fail, and it slowly died in its old, ailing body.
Yohi chose the first path.
If I wait any longer, it’ll all be over.
I have to tell everyone what happened.
They had to expose Baeksang’s conspiracy and stop Dark Heaven.
Her own wrongdoing would come to light along with it, but she had made up her mind.
She would bear the full cost of the path she had chosen.
I never should have done it.
Looking back, she felt nothing but regret.
Baeksang had laid a broad, beautiful road of silk before her.
Yohi had walked it all the way here, turning a blind eye to everything happening around her.
But when she reached the end and happened to look down, she saw that her feet had long since become covered in blood.
Not her own.
The blood of other Nanman people.
Now she wanted to wipe it away.
If she could not, she would cut off her feet.

chapters.title: Chapter 687
paragraphs: SLICE. THUD!
For a moment, the world seemed to stop.
“Grrrk.”
The massive White Tiger lay panting where it had fallen, like a rotten log. Jin Taekyung was completely unconscious.
In Yohi’s eyes, one man held him in his arms and went on speaking calmly.
“I told you. I should have hidden myself first.”
Enlightenment and shock flashed through Yohi’s mind like lightning. Her eyes, usually calm and deep, widened.
“Heugung, you—”
“You don’t call me big brother anymore. I rather liked hearing it.”
She had called him that until just a few shichen ago. But she could never call him that again.
The kindly, heavyset middle-aged man before her was not the Heugung she knew.
“Why?”
Heugung shrugged at the question in her voice. “It’s simple. Just as you used me, I used you.”
“...So you were working with Baeksang after all. You too.”
“That’s a strange way to put it. Weren’t we all working together?”
Yohi went rigid. Heugung gave a short laugh.
“Don’t deny it. No one watched you and Baeksang more closely than I did.”
“Then your sudden visit to the Western Yao Estate...”
“All part of the plan. You, Jin Taekyung, the Beast Miao King—even Baeksang. Of course, none of you knew who I really was... Come to think of it, saying we were all working together is rather funny.”
Yohi swallowed a groan. She could understand why she had not known. Though she had sided with Baeksang, her part in it had gone no further than looking the other way.
But the fact that he had hidden his identity even from Baeksang meant...
“You’ve been watching us all this time. Baeksang and me.”
“Congratulations. One step closer to the answer. Two more to go.”
“On the Demon Empress’s orders?”
“Good. One last step.”
“You were the knife she kept hidden up her sleeve in case something went wrong.”
Clap. Clap.
Heugung slowly clapped his hands and smiled.
“Clever. That’s right. Though even I never dreamed things would go this far.”
Heugung slowly looked around. The entire area had been reduced to ruins. His gaze passed over the two dead old monsters before finally coming to rest on one person.

“Jin Taekyung, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon. The Third Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, and the heir of the Fire King who will one day inherit the orthodox lineage of the Fire Gate Clan.”
His voice was low. A strange glint crossed his eyes as he stared at Jin, who lay unconscious in his arms.

“When I found him here, I knew something had gone wrong. If everything had gone according to plan, he’d have been locked in the underground prison, or the Demon Empress would already have taken him. But...”
Jin Taekyung had followed the tracking scent to the Poisonblood Grounds. There, he had killed the two Supreme Peak masters the Demon Empress had stationed to await the Beast Miao King—and survived.
“Fools. She told them to be careful.”
Heugung muttered under his breath and spat out a wad of phlegm. Then he turned back to Yohi with his usual friendly smile, as if nothing had happened.

“I don’t know if capturing him alive is still the right choice, given how things have turned out... Still, I’m glad I can set things right. Ah, but first I should tell you our destination has changed.”
“...The Inner Palace. You’re taking us to the Inner Palace.”
Heugung nodded at her strained whisper.

“If I return, things should get interesting. The testimony of a Great Chieftain who survived a Han Chinese plot will throw Nanman into turmoil. Every warrior and beast in this land will gather at the Inner Palace, ready to fight the Central Plains.”
“But people aren’t fools. They’ll wonder how a man who’s only at the Peak realm escaped a deadly place like this on his own.”
“Not bad. But what if I were a Supreme Peak master?”
“What are you talking about...?”

“A Supreme Peak master believed to be strong enough to subdue Jin Taekyung. A man with the goodwill and standing to win over even those who would never side with Baeksang. Wouldn’t everyone believe him?”
Yohi froze.
“You... Don’t tell me—”
“That’s right.”
Heugung smiled and summoned his internal energy. From the Western Yao Estate until now, it had never once been sealed. It shifted his bones and flesh and twisted his muscles.
CRACK. CRACK.
The eerie sounds of flesh being torn apart pierced Yohi’s ears.
Faint moonlight broke through the clouds. Beneath it, Heugung’s shadow changed, growing taller and more powerfully built.
“Ghk.”
With one last pained groan, the changes ended. A short title slipped from Yohi’s frozen lips.
“...Palace Lord?”
She stared at the man before her in disbelief.
He was Heugung, yet he was the Beast Miao King. The Beast Miao King, yet unmistakably Heugung. He studied his enlarged shadow with a satisfied smile.
“People think the Bone-Shrinking Technique can only make a person smaller. But master it to Great Completion, and you can become someone else entirely.”
“Now, here’s what we’ll do. I—or rather, the Beast Miao King—came here and subdued Jin Taekyung. You survived his wicked plot and returned to the Inner Palace to tell everyone this.”
He went on slowly as Yohi stared at him, stunned.

“That everything that has happened recently was a conspiracy by Jin Taekyung and the Murim Alliance to swallow Nanman whole. That we must mobilize every human and beast in this land, regardless of age or sex, and invade the Central Plains. What do you think?”
Yohi did not answer. She could not. Fear and rage seemed to squeeze the breath from her body, and the world swam before her eyes.
“H-How could you...”
“Ah. I forgot to mention one thing. Refuse, and Boshan will run red with blood. The four great tribes that rule Nanman will become three.”
CRUNCH.
A thin line of blood trickled between Yohi’s red lips as she struggled to contain her rage. She glared at Heugung, her eyes blazing, and spat out the words.
“You son of a bitch.”
“You wound me. Is that any way to speak to your future husband?”
“Shut your mouth. Who said I was going to marry you?”
“You probably will, once you’ve watched more than five thousand Yao people lose their heads, one after another, before your eyes.”
“You’re a stubborn woman, and I’m a patient man. So I’ll wait until all five thousand heads have hit the ground.”
Heugung spoke without a hint of hurry. Then he beamed at Yohi as brightly as he always had, as though nothing had happened.
“I love you, Yohi.”
A chill swept through her, making every hair stand on end. She squeezed her eyes shut.
She could scarcely believe it: a plan that had been unfolding for who knew how long, and the true face of the wastrel everyone had dismissed.
The dark shadow of Dark Heaven hanging over her head.
Haa.
She breathed out, thoughts racing through her mind. Then she opened her eyes, drew the flexible sword at her waist, and spoke.
“You filthy traitor.”
“Filthy traitor? Please don’t be so hard on yourself.”
“I won’t deny it. I became a traitor too. But do you think Dark Heaven—the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—will let you live? What about the Yi people you lead?”
Her words rang out sharp and clear. Heugung blinked, then burst into hearty laughter.
“That has nothing to do with me.”
“What?”

“Some forty years ago, the former chieftain of the Yi people died in the Great Faction War. His only legitimate son left in Nanman was six years old. The able-bodied men and women had gone to war. His mother died before she ever saw his face. All he had beside him was an old nurse whose sight and hearing were failing.”
“Yohi.”
Heugung—or rather, the man who had become Heugung—continued with a faint smile.
“I was never a traitor. Not for a single moment.”
CLANG.
The flexible sword slipped from Yohi’s grasp and struck the ground with a clatter.
Breathing hard, she tried to pick it up, but her body would not obey.
What is this?
Her eyelids trembled. Was the shock of everything she had learned making her freeze?
No. She could not move because a sinister, clinging qi had already spread through her entire body.
“Y-You...”
Her voice weakened, and her vision began to fade. Heugung’s approaching figure wavered like a heat haze. His voice seemed to come from far away.
“This is why I can’t help loving you. So breathtakingly beautiful, and so innocent too.”
“That... wasn’t an antidote...”

“Unfortunately, I’m not the Beast Miao King. Even crossing swords with you would be more than I could manage. Please forgive this sorry husband of yours, my dear wife. When you wake, I hope you’ll make the choice that’s best for everyone.”
Yohi wanted to scream for someone to come and kill this horrible man. To pull them out of this dark pit and stop the vast scheme that threatened to swallow Nanman.
But the scream that rose in her throat never escaped her lips. And Jin Taekyung, seized by the monster known as the sleep demon, did not open his eyes until the very end.
Then—
SWISH. THUD.
Yohi collapsed like a puppet with its strings cut. Heugung caught her gently in his arms.
A smile appeared at the corner of his mouth, which now wore the face of the Beast Miao King.
“Even asleep, you’re beautiful.”
Heugung truly loved Yohi. It did not matter that she did not want him.
She would make the right choice eventually. In time, she would come to love him.
Dark Heaven—the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—would keep her promise. After all the years he had spent hiding who he was, his reward would be tenfold, twentyfold.
But first...
I need to finish this.
He kissed Yohi on the forehead and slowly turned.
He walked toward the culprit who had dared to jeopardize the grand plan.
Jin Taekyung.
No one had anticipated him. His appearance had dealt a severe blow to a plan on the verge of success. Two Supreme Peak masters, either of whom could turn the tide of a battle, had been lost.
But nothing had changed.
The grand plan will succeed. There are still others to take their place.
Jin Taekyung would not wake for at least several days. Once Heugung brought him and Yohi back to the Inner Palace, it would all be over.
Yes. Over.
He smiled in satisfaction, passed the panting White Tiger, and grabbed Jin Taekyung by the nape to lift him up.
He was about to lift him when—
Whoooooosh.
A chill wind blew in from somewhere. Heugung looked up.
In the pale moonlight, he saw the shape of something.
“What is that...?”
Before he could finish the question—
SHWAAAASH!
The bleak wind turned into a blade and engulfed his entire body.

CRACK.
CRACK.
The eerie sounds of flesh being torn apart pierced Yohi’s ears.
Faint moonlight broke through the clouds.
Beneath it, Heugung’s shadow changed, growing taller and more powerfully built.
“Ghk.”
With one last pained groan, the changes ended.
A short title slipped from Yohi’s frozen lips.
“...Palace Lord?”
She stared at the man before her in disbelief.
He was Heugung, yet he was the Beast Miao King.
The Beast Miao King, yet unmistakably Heugung.
He studied his enlarged shadow with a satisfied smile.
“People think the Bone-Shrinking Technique can only make a person smaller.
But master it to Great Completion, and you can become someone else entirely.”
“Now, here’s what we’ll do.
I—or rather, the Beast Miao King—came here and subdued Jin Taekyung.
You survived his wicked plot and returned to the Inner Palace to tell everyone this.”
He went on slowly as Yohi stared at him, stunned.
“That everything that has happened recently was a conspiracy by Jin Taekyung and the Murim Alliance to swallow Nanman whole.
That we must mobilize every human and beast in this land, regardless of age or sex, and invade the Central Plains.
What do you think?”
Yohi did not answer.
She could not.
Fear and rage seemed to squeeze the breath from her body, and the world swam before her eyes.
“H-How could you...”
“Ah.
I forgot to mention one thing.
Refuse, and Boshan will run red with blood.
The four great tribes that rule Nanman will become three.”
CRUNCH.
A thin line of blood trickled between Yohi’s red lips as she struggled to contain her rage.
She glared at Heugung, her eyes blazing, and spat out the words.
“You son of a bitch.”
“You wound me.
Is that any way to speak to your future husband?”
“Shut your mouth.
Who said I was going to marry you?”
“You probably will, once you’ve watched more than five thousand Yao people lose their heads, one after another, before your eyes.”
“You’re a stubborn woman, and I’m a patient man.
So I’ll wait until all five thousand heads have hit the ground.”
Heugung spoke without a hint of hurry.
Then he beamed at Yohi as brightly as he always had, as though nothing had happened.
“I love you, Yohi.”
A chill swept through her, making every hair stand on end.
She squeezed her eyes shut.
She could scarcely believe it: a plan that had been unfolding for who knew how long, and the true face of the wastrel everyone had dismissed.
The dark shadow of Dark Heaven hanging over her head.
Haa.
She breathed out, thoughts racing through her mind.
Then she opened her eyes, drew the flexible sword at her waist, and spoke.
“You filthy traitor.”
“Filthy traitor?
Please don’t be so hard on yourself.”
“I won’t deny it.
I became a traitor too.
But do you think Dark Heaven—the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—will let you live?
What about the Yi people you lead?”
Her words rang out sharp and clear.
Heugung blinked, then burst into hearty laughter.
“That has nothing to do with me.”
“What?”
“Some forty years ago, the former chieftain of the Yi people died in the Great Faction War.
His only legitimate son left in Nanman was six years old.
The able-bodied men and women had gone to war.
His mother died before she ever saw his face.
All he had beside him was an old nurse whose sight and hearing were failing.”
“Yohi.”
Heugung—or rather, the man who had become Heugung—continued with a faint smile.
“I was never a traitor.
Not for a single moment.”
CLANG.
The flexible sword slipped from Yohi’s grasp and struck the ground with a clatter.
Breathing hard, she tried to pick it up, but her body would not obey.
What is this?
Her eyelids trembled.
Was the shock of everything she had learned making her freeze?
No.
She could not move because a sinister, clinging qi had already spread through her entire body.
“Y-You...”
Her voice weakened, and her vision began to fade.
Heugung’s approaching figure wavered like a heat haze.
His voice seemed to come from far away.
“This is why I can’t help loving you.
So breathtakingly beautiful, and so innocent too.”
“That... wasn’t an antidote...”
“Unfortunately, I’m not the Beast Miao King.
Even crossing swords with you would be more than I could manage.
Please forgive this sorry husband of yours, my dear wife.
When you wake, I hope you’ll make the choice that’s best for everyone.”
Yohi wanted to scream for someone to come and kill this horrible man.
To pull them out of this dark pit and stop the vast scheme that threatened to swallow Nanman.
But the scream that rose in her throat never escaped her lips.
And Jin Taekyung, seized by the monster known as the sleep demon, did not open his eyes until the very end.
Then—
SWISH.
THUD.
Yohi collapsed like a puppet with its strings cut.
Heugung caught her gently in his arms.
A smile appeared at the corner of his mouth, which now wore the face of the Beast Miao King.
“Even asleep, you’re beautiful.”
Heugung truly loved Yohi.
It did not matter that she did not want him.
She would make the right choice eventually.
In time, she would come to love him.
Dark Heaven—the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—would keep her promise.
After all the years he had spent hiding who he was, his reward would be tenfold, twentyfold.
But first...
I need to finish this.
He kissed Yohi on the forehead and slowly turned.
He walked toward the culprit who had dared to jeopardize the grand plan.
Jin Taekyung.
No one had anticipated him.
His appearance had dealt a severe blow to a plan on the verge of success.
Two Supreme Peak masters, either of whom could turn the tide of a battle, had been lost.
But nothing had changed.
The grand plan will succeed.
There are still others to take their place.
Jin Taekyung would not wake for at least several days.
Once Heugung brought him and Yohi back to the Inner Palace, it would all be over.
Yes.
Over.
He smiled in satisfaction, passed the panting White Tiger, and grabbed Jin Taekyung by the nape to lift him up.
He was about to lift him when—
Whoooooosh.
A chill wind blew in from somewhere.
Heugung looked up.
In the pale moonlight, he saw the shape of something.
“What is that...?”
Before he could finish the question—
SHWAAAASH!
The bleak wind turned into a blade and engulfed his entire body.
