If you defy what is ordained, that is defying Heaven.
Had I done nothing, you would have died, unable to overcome the power left behind by the imugi.
I watched him walk along the endless cliff.
“Not once, but twice.”
—What do you mean?
“You saved me twice.”
The Black Tiger gave a small snort.
—I merely felt sorry for someone who had handed everything they possessed to a foolish human.
Without that reason, you deserved to die.
“That’s a little unfair.
I don’t know why you hate humans, but I’ve never done anything bad enough to deserve that.”
—Even after you tried to take innocent lives and set fire to their peaceful home?
“What?”
Instead of answering, the Black Tiger nodded toward the foot of the cliff.
Countless beasts, their bodies blackened in places, drank from an unfamiliar stream.
There were thousands of them by my rough estimate.
With all the others that might be sheltering somewhere in this seemingly boundless place, I couldn’t begin to guess the total.
What the hell...?
I stood on the cliff, staring down at them.
—The inferno you unleashed is still devouring the entire mountain.
If the flames had spread unchecked, everything would have burned away long ago.
—Yes, I led them here.
Just as I did seven days and nights ago.
Seven days and nights ago.
That had been the very day the Beast Miao King and I received the emergency report and headed for Ailao Mountain.
I searched my memory, and realization struck.
The beasts.
I remembered clearly.
Of the three hundred or so warriors stationed at Ailao Mountain, about two hundred had returned alive.
The beasts hadn’t.
I hadn’t seen them anywhere—not on Ailao Mountain, not in the Poisonblood Grounds.
“You were the one who did that too.
You saved the wild beasts.”
—Monsters that should never have been there were set loose.
I had not interfered in human affairs for hundreds of years, but that time I could not stand aside.
Ordinarily, I might have let that pass.
But I was listening closely to the Black Tiger’s thoughts, and I caught the oddity at once.
“Set loose?”
—You did not know?
Faint contempt entered his blue-white eyes.
—Humans did all of it.
Your kind has done such things since long ago, and I have remained here and watched.
Damn it.
I’d only been able to guess what had happened at Ailao Mountain.
Now the Black Tiger had confirmed it.
Dark Heaven had been behind that, too.
If only we’d found out a little sooner.
With belated regret, I looked at the Black Tiger.
I thought I was beginning to understand why he had acted that way that day.
I remembered his back as he repeatedly appeared and disappeared, even though he could have escaped at any time.
“You weren’t attacking us that day.”
—Yes.
That was not my mission.
“You were trying to show us where the Thousand-Year Spider was.”
—I could not simply watch while a foul monster disturbed this mountain.
Humans planted the seed, so humans should reap it.
That is the natural order.
He walked on.
The path along the cliff grew narrower and steeper, and birds nesting on rugged peaks above the clouds watched us with curious eyes.
How long had we been walking?
Clouds and mist surrounded us, and the ground below seemed impossibly far away.
I’m sure this place wasn’t this big.
When I first woke, I’d thought it was a forest around a small pond.
Now I could see vast mountain ranges, valleys, and green pastures.
What the hell is this place?
I could no longer begin to guess.
Staring at the impossible landscape, I finally asked, “Where are we?”
—A land filled with life.
A place where all things live in harmony.
What kind of nonsense was that?
For some reason, I remembered the church deacon who used to give me spicy rice cakes when I was little while shouting, “Jesus, heaven!
Unbelievers, hell!”
“Even so, this can’t be heaven.”
—The kingdom of heaven?
A fitting description, in its way.
But this place lies deep within the land, where no one can enter without my permission.
It is very close to where you were.
“Then... are we in the Poisonblood Grounds?”
A few paces ahead, the Black Tiger gave a small nod.
—It is.
“But this place...”
The words stuck in my throat.
The Poisonblood Grounds?
I wouldn’t have believed we were anywhere on Ailao Mountain.
There were no raging flames here, none of the eerie feeling that hung over the mountain.
—Enough.
This is a place that you humans can neither invade nor understand.
He was right.
Murim had all manner of strange things, Mystic Gate Formations among them, but what lay before me went far beyond anything they could do.
“Ha.
The Poisonblood Grounds.
This is the Poisonblood Grounds.”
Laughing hollowly, I followed him up the peak.
As we neared the summit, his thought reached me again.
—Poisonblood Grounds is its current name.
As I did, humans changed many things over the passage of time.
“What was it called before?”
—The Sacred Land.
“What?”
—That was in a past as distant as the imugi’s memories.
Beasts, not humans, ruled this land then.
The few humans lived in groups within their own territories and worshiped us.
“Huh.”
I had no words.
This forbidden place, where no one could set foot, had once been called the Sacred Land.
And if there had been so few people in Nanman back then... how long ago was that?
Five hundred years?
A thousand?
This is driving me crazy.
Even if I’d put every point into Intelligence from the start, I’d have felt like an idiot right now.
I shook my head and opened my mouth toward the Black Tiger, who had stopped walking before I noticed.
“Then you.
What exactly are you?”
—Did you not call me an apparition yourself?
“I’m asking what they called you when this place was the Sacred Land.”
The Black Tiger was silent for a moment before moving his massive body.
Something wistful passed through his blue-white eyes.
—A guardian spirit.
“What?”
—Long ago, that was what people called me.
The mountain lord who guarded Ailao Mountain.
A guardian spirit born alongside the sacred stone.

chapters.title: Chapter 693
paragraphs: The Beast King Stone.
The name felt familiar. A memory from not so long ago surfaced with it.

About seven days and nights earlier, on our way to Ailao Mountain, the Beast Miao King had told me a story from the distant past. Why Ailao Mountain had become a forbidden land. How the Five Poisons Sect had given rise to the Nanman Beast Palace as it existed today. The Great War that had stained all of Nanman with blood.
And... a vanished divine artifact.

It’s a legend passed down only by word of mouth. The Beast King Stone is our Palace’s divine artifact, said to have been carried by the first Palace Lord. Supposedly, it could make every wild beast under Heaven obey.
I remembered the Beast Miao King’s offhand remark.
—Look.
At the quiet thought echoing in my head, the apparition—no, the being I should now call a guardian spirit—slowly stepped aside.
Only then could I see it.
Ssshhh.
The Black Tiger’s massive body had been blocking my view. Beyond him, at the summit of a peak shrouded in thick mist, stood a colossal boulder.
No way.
I knew at once why the Black Tiger had brought me here. I knew what that boulder was.
Step.
I walked forward as if entranced, passed the Black Tiger, and stopped before the stone. It stood nearly thirty feet tall.
Ssshhh.
I could feel an unknown energy wrapped around it like an embrace.
Here, at the highest point of this impossible land, the boulder shed a faint, ink-dark glow. It looked mysterious and dangerous—like a divine artifact from some legend buried by the ages.
“...The Beast King Stone.”
The three words escaped with the breath I’d been holding. The Black Tiger appeared beside me like a ghost and gave a small nod.
—Yes. Long ago, a human gave it that name.
“The human you mean wouldn’t happen to be...”
—He was refreshing as the wind, clear as water, and steadfast as a tree. He was also the only human who could enter and leave this place freely without my permission.
“Without your permission? Was that possible?”
This place had remained hidden for hundreds of years, perhaps nearly a thousand. We had entered only because the Black Tiger had opened the way for us.
—It was. I did not know it myself, but the sacred stone that guards this land accepted him before I ever gave my permission.
The sacred stone, I realized, was the Beast King Stone’s original name. And I had a fair idea who the human was.
Since people had first settled in Nanman, dozens of tribes had fought one another without end. He was the only leader who had ever united them under a single banner.
And that wasn’t all.
The man who had etched the five characters Nanman Beast Palace into this land had also been the first and last owner of the Beast King Stone during its brief appearance.
No. Maybe owner wasn’t the right word.
What the Black Tiger told me next turned that suspicion into certainty.

—Then, one day, a great war broke out. Mountains and grasslands burned. The rivers filled with more human and animal corpses than anyone could count. As the years passed, the land grew more tainted, and the sacred stone slowly lost its power.
“Lost its power?”
—Commanding a hundred beasts was only one of its powers. We call it the sacred stone because it protected this land’s abundance for ages beyond memory.
I looked away from the Black Tiger and back at the boulder. Its faint, ink-dark glow hadn’t changed. Cracks ran through it, and pieces had broken away.
“Abundance is about the last thing that comes to mind.”
How far was it from looking abundant? About as far as I’d traveled from Henan to Nanman.
Its grimy black color was one thing. The ominous energy seeping from it made even me uneasy.
This really isn’t what I expected.

Divine artifacts didn’t come with factory specifications, but I’d still had a picture in my head: a small, gleaming white stone. Not something that made Seoraksan’s Rocking Stone look modest and practically blasted ominous pressure in every direction.

“...I don’t know about abundance, but I think I understand why it was called the Beast King Stone. If you smashed something’s head with this, what beast wouldn’t obey? You could probably rule humans with it too.”

And the first Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace had supposedly owned this thing, if only for a while. How hard had he trained? Had he hung an elephant from a pull-up bar and put up a five-thousand total on the big three?
While I wondered how a legendary figure had measured his total, the Black Tiger fixed me with a somber gaze.
—Because of your kind.
“What?”
—Once, this land was filled with peace and abundance. All things followed the natural order. The sacred stone did not look as it does now.
I realized what he was getting at.
“...It started losing power when humans settled here.”
—More precisely, when they began killing one another.

I was beginning to understand. The stone the people of Nanman called the Beast King Stone was practically one with this land. The more death and destruction spread across it, the more power the stone lost.
“So that’s why you helped the first Palace Lord? Three hundred years ago, as the Five Poisons Sect stained Nanman with blood, the sacred stone’s power would have weakened too?”
Something crossed the Black Tiger’s eyes. Longing, perhaps. Or regret.
—We did not help him.
I stopped short. His calm thought continued.
—My mission was to guard the sacred stone. Its duty was simply to exist alongside this land. All we could do was watch.
“You just... watched?”
—Yes. Like a certain being you know.

I thought of the Water God Dragon I’d met several months ago. The imugi had spent hundreds of years guarding its river and pursuing enlightenment. For all its strange, tremendous power, it had kept to its territory rather than actively intervening in human affairs.
But if that was true...
“Then what was the legend of the Beast King Stone? The story passed down to the people here...”
—A legend. Yes, it was exactly that—a legend. Something that clearly existed, but could only be fabricated as fiction.
Bitterness flickered through his blue-white eyes.
—He was the only human who could understand our mission, and he wanted peace more than anyone. So, to end this war, he created the Beast King Stone himself.
—I watched from where no one could see. I watched him name a powerless stone the Beast King Stone, become a chosen hero, unite the tribes, and fight other humans. I watched until the day he fell.
My breath caught in my throat. It was as though a book densely filled with the legend of a distant past had opened before my eyes.
—That was how he died. The thing humans had revered as the Beast King Stone vanished as though it had never existed. The war continued for another hundred years. And I...
Grrrr.
His growl trembled. He stared at the sacred stone as if he were searching the distance for something he could never reach. Then his blue-white eyes turned to me.
—For two hundred years, I regretted it.
A brief silence followed.
Wind blew from somewhere. I stood facing the Black Tiger and asked, “Why?”
I didn’t wait for an answer. I hadn’t expected one.

“Because the land grew barren as the war continued, causing the sacred stone to lose its power? Because you thought that even the tiny bit of power it had left would soon disappear when what is about to happen arrives? Is that why you regretted it? Because you should have helped him back then—a pointless regret?”
His reply weighed heavily in my head.
—Are you condemning me?
“No. Honestly, I don’t care much about that. I’m grateful you helped us, whether you believe it or not.”
I didn’t care about the sacred stone or the guardian spirit. I didn’t think I had any business caring about either.
It had already happened hundreds of years ago, and whatever their mission might have been, the fact remained that they had saved my life and the lives of my companions.
The thought had just come to me.
“For a guardian spirit, you’re pretty petty and cowardly. This much should be okay, right?”
“Not okay? If I offended you, I’ll take it back.”
The Black Tiger stared at me without a word. His body looked endlessly ominous, but his blue-white eyes were large and clear.
And then.
—For two hundred years, I regretted it every day, every moment. I should have saved that human, even if it meant defying the natural order.
—Reckless, young human. You were not wrong. I let a single mission bind me for far too long, and it led me to a mistaken judgment. Will you give me a chance?
“A chance...?”
—I want to restore whatever power I can to the sacred stone. And this time, I want to put right the choice I made in the past.
Ssssh.
The enormous tiger slowly opened his jaws. A crystal of clear blue energy came into view.
Ding. Ding. Ding.

System —Conditions met! New information has been updated! —Apparition of Ailao Mountain has changed to guardian spirit! —Hidden text has been revealed! —You have discovered the Hidden Sacred Land! —You have met the activation conditions for a hidden Quest! —A hidden Quest has been created! —The hidden Quest Last Chance has been created!
Bells and System notifications rang out without warning. One final holographic window appeared before my eyes.
System Would you like to enhance the Ancient Sacred Stone with the Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence? Y / N
A tooth for a tooth. An eye for an eye.
And...
Spiritual energy for spiritual energy, huh?
Muttering inwardly, I suddenly looked up at the sky.
It was blue. Just like the eyes of the Black Tiger watching me.
No—the guardian spirit.
Some had gone. Others had stayed behind.
Yohi and Muyaho.
They were waiting by the pond for the one person who had yet to return when something else arrived first.
Rrrrrumble!
The earth shook. Water surged across the pond in waves.
Hundreds, perhaps thousands, of birds took flight at once. Even more beasts rose from the grass.
Yohi reflexively jerked her head up. A faint gasp of shock escaped her lips.
“Th-that’s...”
Kwaaaang!
A pillar of light shot up as if to pierce the sky, enveloping the mysterious space.

chapters.title: Chapter 694
paragraphs: The moon was hidden on a night so dark that only faint flames marked the mountain valley.
One torch, then two, then three. Soon there were hundreds, and the ground began to shake.
Rrrrrumble!
Tremors ran through the earth. Beneath the torches swaying in the wind, shadows large and small pressed forward, their rough breathing unbroken.
Grrrr.
Huff. Huff.
An army.
Humans and beasts, moving as one.
Armed with swords, spears, and bows, the Nanman warriors searched the darkness from their saddles. Beside them, beasts with sharp teeth and claws kept running.
There were three thousand of them. They had left the Outer Palace around noon at one man’s command, their destination set from the start.
Ailao Mountain.
The name came to the Captain of the Guards as he rode at the front. At that moment, someone behind him shouted.
“I see it!”
So did everyone else.
Far ahead, an enormous inferno blazed with a force that made their hundreds of torches seem like nothing.
Crack! Whoosh!
Ancient trees toppled one after another. The flames swallowed everything they touched and grew larger still.
The warriors groaned at the sight of a fire unlike any in the past hundred years—and perhaps any in the next hundred.
“H-how can this be?”
“So it really was true...”
Hearing about it was one thing. Seeing it was another.
Shock and fear passed through the warriors’ eyes as they stared at Ailao Mountain in flames.
Jin Taekyung.
The rumors about him were all true.
He shook off all those pursuit parties and made it here. What kind of monster is he?
Most of the warriors had never faced Jin Taekyung. More precisely, they had never seen what he was capable of.
Until now, he had been merely an outsider from the Central Plains: a young man with features that looked a little strange to the people of Nanman.
Now they had to fight him.
Their orders were to surround Ailao Mountain so tightly that nothing could slip through, then kill Jin Taekyung whenever he emerged.
But...
Can we stop that monster?
The same question troubled them all.
They had grown up hearing stories of Ailao Mountain, the forbidden land whose history stretched back to the founding of the Nanman Beast Palace. One name always came up in those stories.
The Fire Gate Clan.
An unknown clan said to exist somewhere in the distant Central Plains.
Long ago, its Sect Leader had come to Nanman and ended the Great War against the Five Poisons Sect—a war that had continued for more than a century after the Nanman Beast Palace was founded.
The Five Poisons Sect’s deadly poison, which had taken countless lives, and the venomous beasts it commanded had melted like candle wax before the flames he summoned.

It was even said that the Sect Leader of the Five Poisons Sect at the time—who had reduced one hundred of the Nanman Beast Palace’s finest warriors to a mere handful of poisonous water—could not withstand his power and fell to his knees.
No. The story said he burned alive.
That old legend, so entertaining when they were children, had stepped out of the past and into the present.
Right before their eyes.
Gulp.
Someone swallowed, the sound strangely loud. Hands tightened around reins that had been held loosely moments before. Anxious glances spread through the ranks.
Then the Captain of the Guards spoke.
“What are you so afraid of?”
His voice, carrying internal energy, reached every warrior. He went on, firm and clear.
“He is one man. We are three thousand.”
Shoulders that had hunched without their owners noticing began to straighten. One by one, the warriors steadied their gazes.
That’s right. No matter how strong he is, he’s made of flesh and blood.
Even if every rumor is true, he can’t stand against all of us.
Three thousand.
For the killing of one man, it was an absurd number.
The Fire Gate Clan’s Sect Leader had supposedly destroyed the Five Poisons Sect through sheer martial prowess. The stories they had grown up with still frightened them, but a legend was a legend.
No—even if he came back to life, it was impossible for him to face three thousand Nanman warriors and beasts of prey alone.
It had to be impossible.
“Have you forgotten? Jin Taekyung is a traitor who put Nanman in danger. He’s a Han Chinese man worse than a beast, one who has forgotten the debt of the Great Faction War.”
As the inferno drew closer, the Captain’s voice grew stronger.
Shing.
“Warriors of Nanman! My proud brothers!”
He drew his sword. Its edge gleamed as moonlight and wavering torchlight broke across the white blade.
“Hunt him down!”
“Waaaaaah!”
Clang! Clang! Clang!
Hundreds, then thousands of weapons came free. Torches flared, and the army urged its mounts toward Ailao Mountain with a roar.
At that instant—
Whoosh!
The Captain of the Guards saw it. Every human and beast there saw it.
A pillar of light rose through the blood-red flames. Against the fire stood the silhouette of a black hill.
No. It wasn’t a hill.
Rrrrrumble!

He did not know that the three thousand beasts charging relentlessly toward Ailao Mountain had stopped in place as though by prior agreement.
Grrrr.
The tiger that had spent its life at his side gave a low growl and bowed its head.
It was not alone.
Leopards, bears, wolves—every beast, large and small, did the same.
Rustle.
They curled their tails and lowered their massive bodies to the ground.
It was an instinct etched into them at birth: reverence for a king returned after long ages, and a command they could not resist.
—Kraaaaaar!
Along with a roar that devoured the world, blue-white eyes shone in the darkness.
Step. Step.
Quiet footsteps echoed down the silent corridor.
The guards’ sharp gazes swept over the maids and servants. Every guard had reached the Peak, and the servants dropped facedown as trembling cries followed.
“W-we pay our respects to the Palace Lord!”

They came from different tribes and were of every age: children still round-cheeked with baby fat, middle-aged men and women, and an old woman whose hair had gone entirely white.

You’ve grown old.

Because she was one of the few who remembered him as he had been?

Thousands of them. Tens of thousands.

chapters.title: Chapter 695
paragraphs: At first, no one paid any attention.
No—no one had time to pay attention to anything else.

Major incidents had followed one after another, and the general mobilization order had swelled their forces by the day. Even ordinary tribespeople in the Outer Palace held their breath, while nearly ten thousand warriors and beasts waited in the Inner Palace for their new Palace Lord.
Yet amid all this, some still stood watch.
“I’m dying out here. It’s hot, everyone’s on edge, and I’m stuck at the North Gate. Should’ve asked for the East or West Gate. They’ve got it easy.”
The young warrior had just returned from patrol. His senior, a graying middle-aged man seated in the shade against the North Gate wall, clicked his tongue.
“Tsk, tsk. Listen to you. Young man with his whole life ahead of him, already looking for a chance to slack off.”
“You’ve been sitting in the shade the whole time I was on patrol.”
“I’m old. If I can’t rest now, when can I?”
“Well, you’ve got me there.”
The Nanman Beast Palace had three gates in total: the East, the West, and the North Gate where they were stationed.
There had never been a South Gate. The sheer cliff behind the Inner Palace was stronger than any gate.
“How was your patrol? What’s the Outer Palace like?”
“Not a rat in the marketplace.”
“...Of course. Everyone’s worried.”
The older warrior sighed.

Nearly ten thousand warriors had gathered in the Inner Palace alone—an army large enough to belong to a small country. Not since the Great Faction War some fifty years ago had so many assembled in one place.
History repeated itself.
Those old enough to remember the past fell silent. Parents pulled their children close and barred their doors. Everywhere, people feared that a vast war was about to begin.
“But... are we really going to war with the Central Plains?”
The older warrior answered his junior’s cautious question in a low voice.
“Who knows? One thing’s certain, though.”
“What’s that?”
“Before we fight in the Central Plains, we’ll shed blood right here in Nanman.”

“You know the former Palace Lord is still alive. The five tribal chieftains who support him have left the Outer Palace. The higher-ups will want to settle that before they march on the Central Plains.”
The older warrior was hardly the only one to see it coming. Anyone with a little sense and experience could guess what awaited them.
Civil war. Their first in some three hundred years.
To pass through the road leading to the Central Plains, they would have to walk over the corpses and blood of comrades with whom they had shared hardship until only a few days ago.
A shadow fell across the young warrior’s usually carefree face. Among the tribespeople who had left the Outer Palace were close friends he had known since childhood.
The older warrior watched him for a moment, then quietly got to his feet.
“Where are you going?”
“I’ve slacked off enough. I’ll take a look around the wall. My body aches from sitting still.”
“Why not keep resting? The other squad’s covering the wall anyway—”

“You think those fools are keeping watch? They’ve probably sneaked down to sit in the shade, same as us. If the higher-ups catch them, I’m the gate captain. I’ll be the one getting my ass chewed out.”
He had a point. Outsiders almost never came through, so security had never been especially tight. Since nearly ten thousand warriors had taken up position, it had grown laxer still.
Anyone mad enough to attack the Nanman Beast Palace now might as well kill himself.
Besides...
They’re all troubled.

Far fewer warriors were eager for a fight than one might expect. Yayul Cheok, now branded a traitor to Nanman, had been a Palace Lord everyone respected. And after three hundred years together beneath the Nanman Beast Palace’s banner, the tribes had grown close. They dreaded the civil war and Great War looming before them.
But what could they do? When the people above gave an order, you obeyed.
“Whew.”
The older warrior sighed and climbed onto the wall. Just as he had expected, it was quiet up there.
Well, there was at least one man left behind. The problem was that he was asleep and snoring loudly.
...Fine. Rest while you can.
This was the calm before the storm. Today might be the last chance his sorry subordinates had to rest.
Shaking his head, the older warrior stood atop the wall and gazed into the distance.
It was noon.
The sun blazed high overhead. Beyond the North Gate, the broad pasture and the tall hill overlooking the Outer Palace shimmered in the heat haze—
Wait.
What was that? Had he seen it wrong?
His eyes widened. He blinked several times, then rubbed them hard with his sleeve. The sight before him did not change.
“What...?”
The dazed word escaped him before he knew he had spoken.
Far off in the direction he was staring, a massive White Tiger took a step forward.
Step.
Its pure white fur gleamed almost silver. An enormous forepaw brushed the grass, and a wind swept through the forest behind the hill.
Whoosh!
Tangled branches swayed. Countless leaves trembled. Beneath the shade of the dense forest, another forest began to move.
Rumble.
The ground shook. The air shuddered. The wind scattered. Countless eyes with long, slit pupils gleamed in the dark.
The older warrior’s mouth slowly fell open.
Beasts. More beasts than he could begin to count.
He was only an ordinary warrior. He had no way to guess how many lurked behind the trees, or where all those predators with their sharp teeth and claws had come from.
But he could guess one thing.
The one leading that chilling host of beasts might be a person, just like him.
Whoosh!
Two silver figures, one large and one small, raced across the pasture on the cool wind.
By then, the number of White Tigers had increased to two. They stopped before the enormous iron gate, along with the man and woman riding on their backs.
Th-that’s...
The older warrior’s pupils trembled.

Someone else might not have recognized the pair at once. But he had been responsible for the North Gate for ten years, and the moment he saw their faces, it felt as if someone had struck the back of his head with an iron club.
How could he fail to know them?
The woman was one of Nanman’s only four Great Chieftains, while the other young man was...
Jin Taekyung.
Merely thinking his name made it hard to breathe.
It was him. The first outsider to come to this land in the centuries since the Five Poisons Sect’s destruction. The eye of the vast storm hanging over Nanman.
Jin Taekyung had come to the Nanman Beast Palace of his own accord—with countless beasts and Yohi, the Great Chieftain of the Yao people whom he had supposedly abducted.
Wh-what is going on...?
Before he could finish the thought, the young man who had kept his lips shut until now spoke.
“A word of advice. Take your hand off that.”
The middle-aged warrior froze just as he instinctively began to sound the alarm. Watching him, Jin Taekyung inwardly let out a sigh of relief.
Thank God. I’m not too late.
One look at the warrior’s face had told him Dark Heaven’s scheme had not yet begun. If the rift had opened, this place would already be a hellscape where no one could live.
And yet, within this stillness—a stillness so quiet that it felt ominous—he sensed a bomb with its fuse burning down.
“Right, Whitey?”
The enormous body beneath his backside flinched.
The guardian spirit of the sacred stone had regained its former appearance, a White Tiger befitting its title. It sent him a thought.
—...How dare you call this body a name like that?
“You’d have been Blackie before. Not that I’m a racist.”
—I have no idea what you’re babbling about. Mad human.
A madman, huh? Yeah, I’ve heard that a fair few times.
Muttering inwardly, Jin Taekyung gave a quiet laugh and lowered the spearhead in his hand.
Was he afraid of what lay ahead? Of course he was.
But he had survived countless brushes with death to reach this place, and he had done everything he could with what he’d been given.
Baeksang. The Southern Heaven Demon Empress. Dark Heaven.
It no longer mattered who stood in his way. He would simply stake his life and fight back.
That’s right. Stake my life.
Tens of thousands of lives hung on this battle. Hundreds of thousands. Perhaps more.
Blood might flow like rivers, and corpses might pile up into mountains.
But...
I have to do it.
Someone had once said:
Do everything in your power, then leave the result to Heaven and wait.
But Jin Taekyung thought differently. Only when a person could even change the will of Heaven could it truly be called Will.
Isn’t that right?
He looked up at the sky. Scorching, dazzling sunlight answered him.
He couldn’t die on a day like this.
Then again, he didn’t want to die in any weather. He had no intention of it.
Even if the Lord of Heaven was waiting behind the iron gate.
Swish! Slash!
In an instant, a blue-white Force tore through the air like a flash of light and split the enormous iron gate in two.
The guardian spirit, reborn as a dazzling silver White Tiger, let out a roar that shook Heaven and Earth.
—GRAAAAAAAWR!
Its jaws opened wide enough to swallow the world. But teeth harder than steel and a red tongue were not all that lay hidden inside.
Fwoosh!
Brilliant light burst forth, bathing the world in its radiance.
From the sacred stone held in the guardian spirit’s mouth, a pillar of light surged over the walls and pierced the sky.
BOOOOM!
It could be seen from a hundred li away. Perhaps even a thousand.
Everyone saw that strange power, that wondrous sight: the ten thousand warriors gathered in the Inner Palace, and the innumerable beasts filling the hill.
—Kyaaaaaaau!
—GRAAAWR!
Their roars broke an invisible dam. The beasts that had waited for their master’s command surged like a wave across the vast grassland.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
Thud, thud, thud!
Beneath the blazing sun, the earth shook and the wind scattered.
At the head of them all was one man.
“Let’s go.”
The quiet words slipped from his lips. At the same time, the guardian spirit powerfully kicked off the ground.
Whooosh!
The Great War that would decide Nanman’s fate had begun.

“I’ve slacked off enough.
I’ll take a look around the wall.
My body aches from sitting still.”
“Why not keep resting?
The other squad’s covering the wall anyway—”
“You think those fools are keeping watch?
They’ve probably sneaked down to sit in the shade, same as us.
If the higher-ups catch them, I’m the gate captain.
I’ll be the one getting my ass chewed out.”
He had a point.
Outsiders almost never came through, so security had never been especially tight.
Since nearly ten thousand warriors had taken up position, it had grown laxer still.
Anyone mad enough to attack the Nanman Beast Palace now might as well kill himself.
Besides...
They’re all troubled.
Far fewer warriors were eager for a fight than one might expect.
Yayul Cheok, now branded a traitor to Nanman, had been a Palace Lord everyone respected.
And after three hundred years together beneath the Nanman Beast Palace’s banner, the tribes had grown close.
They dreaded the civil war and Great War looming before them.
But what could they do?
When the people above gave an order, you obeyed.
“Whew.”
The older warrior sighed and climbed onto the wall.
Just as he had expected, it was quiet up there.
Well, there was at least one man left behind.
The problem was that he was asleep and snoring loudly.
...Fine.
Rest while you can.
This was the calm before the storm.
Today might be the last chance his sorry subordinates had to rest.
Shaking his head, the older warrior stood atop the wall and gazed into the distance.
It was noon.
The sun blazed high overhead.
Beyond the North Gate, the broad pasture and the tall hill overlooking the Outer Palace shimmered in the heat haze—
Wait.
What was that?
Had he seen it wrong?
His eyes widened.
He blinked several times, then rubbed them hard with his sleeve.
The sight before him did not change.
“What...?”
The dazed word escaped him before he knew he had spoken.
Far off in the direction he was staring, a massive White Tiger took a step forward.
Step.
Its pure white fur gleamed almost silver.
An enormous forepaw brushed the grass, and a wind swept through the forest behind the hill.
Whoosh!
Tangled branches swayed.
Countless leaves trembled.
Beneath the shade of the dense forest, another forest began to move.
Rumble.
The ground shook.
The air shuddered.
The wind scattered.
Countless eyes with long, slit pupils gleamed in the dark.
The older warrior’s mouth slowly fell open.
Beasts.
More beasts than he could begin to count.
He was only an ordinary warrior.
He had no way to guess how many lurked behind the trees, or where all those predators with their sharp teeth and claws had come from.
But he could guess one thing.
The one leading that chilling host of beasts might be a person, just like him.
Whoosh!
Two silver figures, one large and one small, raced across the pasture on the cool wind.
By then, the number of White Tigers had increased to two.
They stopped before the enormous iron gate, along with the man and woman riding on their backs.
Th-that’s...
The older warrior’s pupils trembled.
Someone else might not have recognized the pair at once.
But he had been responsible for the North Gate for ten years, and the moment he saw their faces, it felt as if someone had struck the back of his head with an iron club.
How could he fail to know them?
The woman was one of Nanman’s only four Great Chieftains, while the other young man was...
Jin Taekyung.
Merely thinking his name made it hard to breathe.
It was him.
The first outsider to come to this land in the centuries since the Five Poisons Sect’s destruction.
The eye of the vast storm hanging over Nanman.
Jin Taekyung had come to the Nanman Beast Palace of his own accord—with countless beasts and Yohi, the Great Chieftain of the Yao people whom he had supposedly abducted.
Wh-what is going on...?
Before he could finish the thought, the young man who had kept his lips shut until now spoke.
“A word of advice.
Take your hand off that.”
The middle-aged warrior froze just as he instinctively began to sound the alarm.
Watching him, Jin Taekyung inwardly let out a sigh of relief.
Thank God.
I’m not too late.
One look at the warrior’s face had told him Dark Heaven’s scheme had not yet begun.
If the rift had opened, this place would already be a hellscape where no one could live.
And yet, within this stillness—a stillness so quiet that it felt ominous—he sensed a bomb with its fuse burning down.
“Right, Whitey?”
The enormous body beneath his backside flinched.
The guardian spirit of the sacred stone had regained its former appearance, a White Tiger befitting its title.
It sent him a thought.
—...How dare you call this body a name like that?
“You’d have been Blackie before.
Not that I’m a racist.”
—I have no idea what you’re babbling about.
Mad human.
A madman, huh?
Yeah, I’ve heard that a fair few times.
Muttering inwardly, Jin Taekyung gave a quiet laugh and lowered the spearhead in his hand.
Was he afraid of what lay ahead?
Of course he was.
But he had survived countless brushes with death to reach this place, and he had done everything he could with what he’d been given.
Baeksang.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Dark Heaven.
It no longer mattered who stood in his way.
He would simply stake his life and fight back.
That’s right.
Stake my life.
Tens of thousands of lives hung on this battle.
Hundreds of thousands.
Perhaps more.
Blood might flow like rivers, and corpses might pile up into mountains.
But...
I have to do it.
Someone had once said:
Do everything in your power, then leave the result to Heaven and wait.
But Jin Taekyung thought differently.
Only when a person could even change the will of Heaven could it truly be called Will.
Isn’t that right?
He looked up at the sky.
Scorching, dazzling sunlight answered him.
He couldn’t die on a day like this.
Then again, he didn’t want to die in any weather.
He had no intention of it.
Even if the Lord of Heaven was waiting behind the iron gate.
Swish!
Slash!
In an instant, a blue-white Force tore through the air like a flash of light and split the enormous iron gate in two.
The guardian spirit, reborn as a dazzling silver White Tiger, let out a roar that shook Heaven and Earth.
—GRAAAAAAAWR!
Its jaws opened wide enough to swallow the world.
But teeth harder than steel and a red tongue were not all that lay hidden inside.
Fwoosh!
Brilliant light burst forth, bathing the world in its radiance.
From the sacred stone held in the guardian spirit’s mouth, a pillar of light surged over the walls and pierced the sky.
BOOOOM!
It could be seen from a hundred li away.
Perhaps even a thousand.
Everyone saw that strange power, that wondrous sight: the ten thousand warriors gathered in the Inner Palace, and the innumerable beasts filling the hill.
—Kyaaaaaaau!
—GRAAAWR!
Their roars broke an invisible dam.
The beasts that had waited for their master’s command surged like a wave across the vast grassland.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
Thud, thud, thud!
Beneath the blazing sun, the earth shook and the wind scattered.
At the head of them all was one man.
“Let’s go.”
The quiet words slipped from his lips.
At the same time, the guardian spirit powerfully kicked off the ground.
Whooosh!
The Great War that would decide Nanman’s fate had begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 696
paragraphs: Rumble, rumble, rumble!
Buildings shook. The earth trembled.
The silence surrounding the Nanman Beast Palace had long since shattered.
In the Outer Palace, tribespeople hiding behind locked doors pulled their young children close. Warriors idling away their shifts atop watchtowers turned their heads—and stared.
“W-what is that...?”
GRAAAAAAAWR!
A tremendous roar that shook Heaven and Earth swallowed the dazed voice that had slipped between someone’s lips.
One warrior finally came to his senses and shouted at the top of his lungs.
“Th-the enemy!”
Most of the others did not move. They could not.
How could they? All they could do was stand with their mouths open and watch an army of beasts race along the dozen or so broad roads through the Outer Palace.
Th-this can’t be.
The sight was as terrifying as it was wondrous.
Thousands—tens of thousands—of beasts ran as one.
No one there had ever seen anything like it. Not even the oldest person in the land. Probably not even his grandfather.
A calamity. Or a miracle.

Faced with something beyond their understanding, the ordinary warriors stood frozen like statues. Even their superior’s shout, the first to break through the shock, reached them like an echo from far away.
“The alarm bell! Ring the alarm bell! Tell the Inner Palace, now!”
“You idiots!”

The enraged superior shoved aside his dazed subordinate. Then, just as he reached for the rope connected to the alarm bell, he realized that the sunlight that had been beating down fiercely only moments ago had vanished.
Whoooooosh.
Dark clouds?
No. The dark clouds he knew did not move this fast or hang so low.
A strange sound reached him. As the darkness drew nearer, he finally saw what it was.
“...Goddamn it.”
The dark cloud—or rather, countless flying beasts that had flown in and dyed a section of the vast sky black—descended upon him.
Whoooooosh!
Flap, flap, flap!
He could tell neither how many there were nor what kinds. Sharp cries, flashing beaks, and flying feathers filled the air.
The flying beasts, transformed into one enormous monster, swept through five watchtowers like a storm.
No. They smashed them apart.
CRACK! CRUNCH!
“The watchtower’s coming down!”
“AAAAARGH!”
Charging together, the birds were a living battering ram.
The world tilted. For an instant, the warriors felt themselves floating. Then they fell with the shattered watchtowers.
Rumble, rumble, rumble! Daaang!
An alarm bell nearly as large as a grown man hit the ground first and rolled. The warriors twisted in midair and landed after it, stumbling but upright.
Panting, they raised their heads. A vast shadow fell over them.
“Where is Baeksang?”
The quiet voice bored into their ears. Yet everyone there felt a chill that seemed to freeze their hearts.
Was it the enormous White Tiger, so large that looking at it made their knees weak? Or the countless beasts behind it?
No. The White Tiger felt strangely warm and mysterious, and the beasts facing them up close had gentle eyes.
What froze the warriors was the gaze of the man on the White Tiger’s back, looking down at them.
He was tall and perfectly proportioned, with carelessly tousled hair and striking features unlike those of the Nanman people.
And in his hand was a pure-white spear.
“Jin Taekyung!”
At someone’s shriek, the warriors instinctively reached for the weapons at their waists.
They tried to draw them.
At least, they did until Jin Taekyung opened his mouth.
“If you pull those out, you won’t like what happens.”
“And if you’ve got eyes, look around. Who else is here besides me?”
Jin Taekyung was the monster blamed for throwing all of Nanman into an uproar. Since he had appeared with an enormous number of beasts, they had thought there could be nothing left to surprise them.
Then they recognized another face.
Step.
A second, smaller White Tiger approached. On its back rode a beautiful woman whose exhaustion did nothing to hide her looks.
“Su-surely not...”
“Great Chieftain Yohi?”
Yohi spoke, her voice clear.
“Do you recognize me?”
How could they not? Every year, when she appeared before the public for the Tribal Grand Council, people packed the streets for a glimpse of her.

But what confused them most was seeing her beside Jin Taekyung, neither afraid nor bound. After the incident at the Western Yao Estate a few days earlier, rumors of her death had spread quietly through Nanman.
And now she was at the head of an immense host of beasts.
“G-Great Chieftain. Why are you with a monster like him...?”
“A monster...”
Yohi muttered quietly and turned her head to look at Jin Taekyung, but Jin Taekyung was not looking at her.
His eyes were fixed on the enormous iron gate separating the Outer Palace from the Inner Palace, at the far end of the road. Something about it felt ominous.
“There comes the monster,” he said.
The next moment, the gate began to open with a heavy grinding sound.
Rumble, rumble, rumble.
Countless arrowheads appeared along the high stone walls of the Inner Palace.
Click, click, click!
Sunlight flashed on their tips. Nearly a thousand archers aimed from the walls, bowstrings drawn taut, their breathing tight with tension.
Then the figure hidden behind the iron gate came into view.
Step.
His footsteps rang out with unusual clarity.
The hem of his spotless white robe brushed the ground. His calm gaze crossed the distance and met one man’s eyes.
“You came. In the end, you did.”
Baeksang.
His voice carried powerful internal energy. Jin Taekyung lowered his spearhead and answered.
“Yes. I came.”
You fucking bastard.
Baeksang.
The moment I saw his face, I felt the internal energy throughout my body boil like lava.
I wanted to charge out immediately.
I wanted to kick off the guardian spirit’s back, race toward him like the wind, and kill him with the fastest, strongest strike I could deliver.
But...
Slick.
A slender finger caught hold of my sleeve. Yohi’s trembling voice reached my ears.
“No. Not yet.”
Yes. I knew that too.
If I cut Baeksang’s head off right now, it would be like lighting the fuse of a bomb with no time left on it.

Baeksang—he could not die like that. He had to die not as the Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, but as the traitor and usurper who had deceived all the Nanman people and joined forces with Dark Heaven.
The Palace Lord’s death would bring a brutal battle. But no warrior would fight for a traitor.
It was the only way to spare even a few needless deaths. And Yohi, beside me, was the one person who could expose the truth and stop the battle bearing down on us.
“Let’s go.”
The guardian spirit and Muyaho nodded at my whisper and started forward.
We moved at a steady pace. A thousand arrowheads tracked us, ready to loose a rain of arrows at a single command.
But as we drew closer, their flashing tips began to waver. Taut bowstrings slackened. Unease spread along the Inner Palace walls as the archers recognized Yohi.
There was one exception.
Baeksang.
I stared at his unshaken face.
“The Great Chieftain you used to eat with has come back alive. You could at least ask how she is. Don’t you think?”
Charged with internal energy, my voice carried in every direction.
The unease swelled. Baeksang parted his lips.
“What affection is there between us that I should greet her? We were bound together only by our separate aims.”
My face stiffened. Yohi’s probably had too.
We were thinking the same thing.
Why?
This was not the Baeksang I knew. He was sly and cunning. His scheming, more frightening than his martial arts, was one of the chief reasons Nanman had fallen into chaos.
Yet he had acknowledged Yohi. In front of everyone who followed him.
My grip tightened around the spear shaft. I clenched my teeth and glared at him.
“What the hell is this...? What kind of bullshit are you pulling?”
“Did you think I would deny it?”
Baeksang turned to look behind him.
Beyond the wide-open gate, countless Nanman warriors stood amid a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords. They and the archers on the walls stared at him, eyes wide.
“What more is there to say? Everything you know—and everything they will soon realize—is true.”
“Yes. That is correct.”
Baeksang looked away from his warriors and up at the sky.
Not a cloud marred it. Hot sunlight fell across his face.
“I betrayed everyone.”
His quiet voice, charged with internal energy, broke the suffocating silence that had settled over the area.
It traveled on the air, pierced through the wind, crossed the broad road running through the Outer Palace, passed over the stone walls of the Inner Palace, and reached everyone.
“I lived each day as though it were ten years. To achieve one goal, I became an unforgivable turncoat. And at last, I came this far.”
My breath caught.
This was not a confession in which he admitted the sins he had committed and begged for forgiveness.
No. It was...
Relief that it was over. And despair.
Something altogether different from giving up.
Baeksang was letting out what he had held down every day for decades. He made no attempt to hide his despair, even though he had achieved the goal he had wanted for so long.
No way.
A thought flashed through my mind like lightning. Every hair on my body stood on end.
Then a scream burst from my lips.
“Everyone, fall back—!”
And the next moment—
Rumble, rumble, rumble! Flash!
Thunder shook Heaven and Earth. Dark clouds spread over everyone’s heads.
In a world where not even a single ray of sunlight could be found, someone’s voice bored into my ears.
“What a shame. It’s already too late.”

chapters.title: Chapter 697
paragraphs: “What a shame. It’s already too late.”
A languid voice reached my ears. No—not just mine. Everyone here could hear it.
It heralded the arrival of someone fatally alluring, and more dangerous still.
“The Southern Heaven Demon Empress!”
I whipped my head around at the thunderous shout. Above the heads of everyone frozen by her sudden appearance, billowing robes fluttered atop a pavilion that rose high into the sky.
The catlike eyes looking down at us curved into half-moons.
“Oh my. Who could this be?”
The woman’s face was unfamiliar. Her voice and the feeling she gave me were not.
I knew it was her. I forced the words out through clenched teeth.
“It’s me, you fucking bitch.”
Heat churned in my gut as if I’d swallowed lava. My fingers trembled around the spear shaft, and my heart hammered against my ribs.
A tidal wave of emotion raged through me—far more fiercely than when I had faced Baeksang.
But simple hostility and anger were not the only things that had seized me.
She’s strong.
Was she always this strong?
Just meeting her eyes made my heart sink.

Several months had passed since the incident in Hubei Province. The insights I’d gained since then let me glimpse a little more of my opponent’s true nature. The Southern Heaven Demon Empress standing before me was a greater monster than I had imagined.

No one else here could even guess at her realm. Yet my eyes and sharpened senses could trace the power she concealed: the ferocity behind her gently curved eyes, the immense darkness coiled within her slender frame.
“You fucking bitch.”
“Ahaha! Just as I expected. Just as I expected!”
Whatever amused her so much, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress clutched her stomach and laughed despite the insult. Then she smiled at me.
“You’re so refreshingly straightforward. That’s why I like you, Benefactor.”
“What?”
“Have you forgotten already? Who saved me that day, on cold Dongting Lake, with corpses floating in the water?”
As if I could forget. I’d thought back on that moment and regretted it countless times.
Was it because I’d saved the Southern Heaven Demon Empress with my own hands?
No. The person I’d saved that day was Honglan.

In Hubei, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had been nothing more than a beautiful singing courtesan favored by some idiot from the Huang tribe. She had approached me deliberately from the start, and she would have survived even if I hadn’t come.
The one thing I regretted was being too stupid to recognize the culprit standing right in front of me.
My anger at myself for failing to realize I had been toyed with for someone else’s amusement.
And my guilt at failing to prevent an even greater sacrifice.
Rustle.
“Now I can finally greet you properly.”
Honglan—no, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—lifted her billowing robes and dipped her head.
“This lowly woman, Honglan, greets her Benefactor.”
I thrust out a palm as fast as lightning.
Fwoosh!
Moisture evaporated in an instant. The force of the Flame Divine Palm, carrying terrible heat, reached her in a heartbeat.
But—
Slice!
In even less time, the powerful palm force—one Baeksang himself would have struggled to stop—was split in two like tofu.
Boom!
Beneath the dark clouds that now covered the sky, the two halves flew off course and exploded in midair.
Cries of shock rose around us.
“W-what was that?”
“D-did you see what I just saw? That woman...”
“The Southern Heaven Demon Empress. Someone definitely called her the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.”
Some here knew that title. Others didn’t. It hardly mattered. Soon they would all know who she was—and how much viciousness and terrifying power that monster had kept hidden.
I stared coldly at the edge of the pavilion. Standing there, straightening her disheveled court robes, was a woman far too beautiful to be called a monster.

“Hmm. I went to the trouble of being polite, but I don’t much like the way you answered my greeting. Still, I’ll be generous and let it pass. I do owe you my life. I can’t gouge out my Benefactor’s eyes just yet.”
I could feel the killing intent beneath her innocent tone. If anything, it made me calmer.
“Shut your fucking maw.”
“What rough language. A maw is something a beast has. For example...”
Her voice trailed off as her gaze shifted slightly downward, toward the enormous White Tiger baring its teeth.
“Yes. That word suits that hideous beast perfectly.”
Grrrrr.
The guardian spirit growled low and glared at the Southern Heaven Demon Empress. I could feel its muscles tense as it prepared itself.
“A hideous beast, you say. Then what should a human like you be called?”
Until now, its thoughts had been much like Sound Transmission. This time, its voice reached everyone.
The warriors surrounding the Inner Palace, inside and out, caught their breath. The Southern Heaven Demon Empress widened her eyes, then gave a quiet laugh and looked at me.
“I stand corrected. It’s not merely hideous. It’s an interesting beast, too.”
“I don’t know about that.”
I tightened my grip on the spear. Dozens of movements and forms flashed through my mind—ways to end her life with the fastest, deadliest strike I could deliver.
“You’ll find it even more interesting in a moment. This one’s going to bite through the back of your neck.”
“A beast is still a beast. The same was true of a certain foolish imugi that waited for Heaven’s call.”
“He was not foolish. He was kind. Kind enough to sacrifice his life and the cultivation he had built over hundreds of years.”
The guardian spirit fixed its blue-white eyes on her as though it could see straight through her.
“I know you.”
A faint smile touched her lips.
“That’s hardly welcome news. I have no interest in a beast that reeks like you do.”
“I saw you in the imugi’s memories. A human, endlessly dark and filled with malice.”
“Memories?”
“Everything that makes up the world possesses an essence and traces. And in that sense, you in its memories were...”
“Beautiful, I suppose. Dazzlingly so.”
“Old and hideous. So much so that it was hard to believe you were human.”
“That is your essence. You have denied and hated your true form, clinging to life through the long years. You are no different from a Fiend.”
Silence followed the guardian spirit’s words. The people who had been murmuring in shock fell quiet. The countless growling beasts held their breath and lowered themselves to the ground.
And at the center of it all stood one person.
Fwoosh!
The sleeves of her court robes swelled as though they might burst. A terrifying surge of qi pressed down in every direction with the weight of a mountain, freezing every living thing in place.
Crack. Crack.
The wind stopped. The pavilion roof began to collapse under the pressure.
“...Is that so?”
Her smile was gone. Her darkened eyes looked down on the world below.
“Old and hideous. Yes. So that’s what I am.”
She spoke calmly, then turned to stare at me.
“I’ll give you credit for making it this far. If you’d arrived a day earlier—no, even half a day—I couldn’t have guaranteed the outcome myself.”
Her tone had changed. So had the air around her.
Yet I felt calmer. People were most frightening when they kept their true nature hidden. Once they lost the smile and composure they’d held on to until the end, an opening appeared.
Besides...
I still had a card up my sleeve. A move I could make even if the worst happened, as long as I had the strength to use it.
That was why I could speak.
“Hmm. I’m genuinely curious about something.”
Just like this.
“How ugly is your face, really, for someone to say something like that to you?”
“Were you a mortar in your past life?”
The next moment—
“I’ll make you regret that.”
Her cold voice broke the brief silence. Dark clouds swallowed the sky.
And then...
Fwoosh!
A mass of pitch-black light poured from the enormous cliff behind the Inner Palace.
That’s...
The sight alone made it hard to breathe.
It was a rift.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
The earth shook. The world shook. With a deafening roar, the enormous cliff that had stood there for hundreds—no, thousands—of years began to split apart.
“Ah. Ahhh...”
Someone groaned in shock at the strange, terrifying sight.
So it has come to this. At long last.
Someone else spat out a despairing mutter in the depths of their heart.
“It’s over. All of it.”
And someone who had been consumed by anger watched what they had brought about with rapture in their eyes.
At last. At last!
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress trembled, already forgetting the anger she had felt moments before.
How could she not? This was the fruit of long years of endurance.
That rift, far larger and more powerful than the one in Hubei Province, was her creation. It marked the moment the omnipotent Lord of Heaven’s will descended upon this land.
Kraaaaaaash!
A blade-sharp gale swept in every direction. Through the widening gap in the cliff, an intensely dark and viscous energy began to crawl out, gnawing away at the world.
Demonic qi that would corrupt life and conquer this land!
—Krrk, krrrk!
—Kyaaaaa!
“Ghk. Guhk!”
“W-what’s happening all of a sudden—krrk!”
The rift had not even opened completely, yet its power was already spreading in every direction.
Look at that surging darkness. At the countless beasts and humans writhing with the whites of their eyes showing, awaiting the change to come.
And soon, the change caused by the rift would begin.
No. That’s not right.
This was not change. It was evolution.
They would be reborn as stronger, more beautiful beings. It was a blessing the omnipotent Lord of Heaven bestowed upon lowly creatures.
A lingering smile spread across the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s lips. Then her gaze fell on one person.
Jin Taekyung.
A young man stood tall, staring at the unbelievable, overwhelming spectacle unfolding before him.
To the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, he looked absurd—and pitiful. Enough to make her want to rip his throat out in one go.
You... should never have come here.
She was about to launch herself toward Jin Taekyung when—
Fwoosh!
A tremendous radiance burst forth from somewhere and swallowed the darkness.

chapters.title: Chapter 698
paragraphs: What is that?
The question filled the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s mind. Her eyes widened.
Light.
Bigger and brighter than any light she had ever seen.
A tremendous radiance that had erupted without warning swelled as though it might burst, swallowing the approaching darkness as it seeped into the world.
Kwooooooo!
A pillar of light shot toward the distant sky and pierced the heavens. Sunlight poured through a gap in the dark clouds.
The darkness that had surged over the stone walls like a wave faltered the moment it touched the radiance, as though its path had been blocked.
Blocked? Even the demonic qi summoned from the rift?
It was impossible to believe.

The rift’s demonic qi was immensely powerful, a force of pure darkness. Even the imugi, after hundreds of years of cultivation, had been unable to withstand its full power and had fallen to corruption.
Yet the scene before her was real.
The dark clouds were slowly scattering.
The wave of darkness could advance no farther against the radiance.
And then—
“Wow. This really works.”
Jin Taekyung stood at the center of the radiance, grinning at her.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress clenched her teeth.
“How... How in the world?”
Before she could finish, Jin Taekyung shrugged.
“No big deal. Everyone’s got a divine artifact stashed away somewhere, right?”
Divine artifact.
The words struck her like a hammer to the back of the head.
Only then did her gaze slide away from Jin Taekyung and settle on another being.
That beast.
The enormous White Tiger had its jaws open as if roaring. Like the imugi she had corrupted, it was clearly more than a spiritual creature.
Through the dazzling radiance, she could faintly make out something shining with a clear, luminous glow.
At the same time, an ancient legend of this land flashed through her mind.
“...The Beast King Stone.”
The words slipped between her pomegranate-red lips. Jin Taekyung gave a quiet laugh.
“Oh. You know it?”
How could she not?
The symbol of the king before whom every beast in the world bowed. Nanman’s divine artifact, lost for hundreds of years.
No, she could hardly have failed to recognize it. She was the one who had combed every inch of Nanman’s rugged terrain for the Beast King Stone.
For more than ten years.

Yet even after enough time had passed for mountains and rivers to change, she had failed to find so much as the slightest trace of the Beast King Stone itself. In the end, she had left the ancient legend behind and begun her grand plan.
But why? Why now?
“You bastaaaaards!”
Whoooooosh! Crack!
A terrifyingly immense surge of qi rose and pressed down on everything around it.
The countless beasts that had been baring their teeth and growling tucked their tails between their legs. Pavilions throughout the area began to collapse as though a giant had stepped on them.
Tribespeople fleeing the Outer Palace in terror spotted the figure suspended in the air and gaped.
Darkness.
A woman wrapped from head to toe in surging darkness looked down upon the ground.
Like a god—or a Fiend out of legend—she seemed to be weighing how much life they had left.
Yet while everyone else stared at her in fear, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had eyes for only one thing.
“Hand it over.”
Rumble.
The dark clouds filling the sky gave a great roar.
Her chilling voice rang through the world of light and darkness, reaching every ear.
“It is something the Lord of Heaven must rightfully take. It is not an object that insignificant beings like you are fit to possess.”
Beasts and humans alike froze before her overwhelming power. They forgot to scream, forgot to run, and stared blankly up at her.
All except two people.
No—two beings.
“Bullshit, you crazy bitch.”
—How dare a mere human covet the sacred stone?
Jin Taekyung and the guardian spirit stared at the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
They could feel it: the unprecedented power coiled inside that small body.

The qi pressing down around them was greater than any the guardian spirit had encountered in a human over the past several hundred years. It surpassed even that of the Western Heaven Demon Lord, whom Jin Taekyung had fought while narrowly escaping death time and again.
Strong.
And frightening.
Fear was something every living creature knew. But feeling it and surrendering to it were different things.
They knew that even now, they had to endure the fear pressing down on their entire bodies and advance. Only then could they win.
—Much blood will flow, human.
“Fuck. If I survive this, I won’t even take a piss toward Nanman again.”
Jin Taekyung muttered through clenched teeth and tightened his grip on White Flame’s shaft.
Then he spoke quietly to Yohi, who stood frozen behind him.
“You know what to do, right?”
“Get the people out of here. Now. Run like hell, and take them as far away as you can.”
Countless tribespeople lived in the Outer Palace, beyond those he could see.
Jin Taekyung did not want them caught in the horrific hellscape about to unfold here.
It was enough for those with power to bleed. The tribespeople, with neither weapons nor sharp teeth, had to survive.
Even if everyone who remained here died at the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s hands.
But... I’ll stop her. We’ll stop her.
For now, the sacred stone’s power was holding back the demonic qi pouring from the rift.
He did not know how long this tense standoff would last, but before the situation grew any worse, they had to defeat the Southern Heaven Demon Empress and close the rift.
No matter what it takes.
Whoosh.
Jin Taekyung drew a deep breath and glared at the figure high above the wreckage of the pavilions.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress. The beginning and end of everything that had happened in this land.
Someone had to fall before this cruel story could end.
“Let’s go.”
The low voice had just slipped between his lips when—
—Kraaaaaaang!
A fierce roar tore through the wind.
The radiance that had been fading against the darkness swelled once more, rousing the terrified beasts and people.
Fwoosh! Kwoooooosh!
Light burst forth with the roar. Flames blazed around the silver spearhead.
The outsider who had come to this land after hundreds of years soared upward as one with the enormous White Tiger.
Bang!
He kicked off the ground.
Pop!
He stepped on the invisible air and wind.
Whoooooosh!
Toward the darkness spread across the distant sky.
No.
Toward the being made still stronger by that darkness.
“Southern Heaven Demon Empress!”
His flame-wreathed azure dragon’s roar flew with the spearhead, cleaving through space.
A chilling look crossed the woman’s face, now twisted like a Fiend’s, with not a trace of beauty left.
“The Lord of Heaven desires it.”
At that moment—
Flash!
Light and darkness mingled in a blinding flash that washed over the Nanman Beast Palace.
Rrrrrumble.
A roar like the sky splitting apart accompanied a tremendous surge of qi that swept in every direction.
Baeksang instinctively shut his eyes against the blinding flash. A gale struck his entire body, and he swallowed a groan.
Hngh.
What kind of overwhelming power was this?
Even as a Supreme Peak master, he could barely keep his balance against the aftershock.
When he finally opened his eyes, the area around him had already been reduced to ruins. The tribespeople who had barely survived thanks to the protection of the beasts were fleeing while screaming.
“Kyaaaaaa!”
“Hoya! Hoya! Where are you?”
“M-Mother!”
Pavilions and houses built over many years collapsed one after another. A grown son cried out at the sight of his elderly mother pinned beneath a fallen stone wall.
Screams and death. Blood and bodies.
Only days ago, these streets had been full of laughter and music. Now there was no trace of either—only an endless din of roars and screams.
Bang! Kwoooooang!
Light and darkness shot toward each other and tangled together, again and again, in the space of an instant.
Baeksang stared hollowly at the hellscape beneath the murky flashes and sky-splitting roars. Then he reached out in one direction.
Boom!
The force of his palm crossed the distance and knocked a large boulder away.
A half-gray-haired middle-aged man who had been struggling to save an old woman trapped beneath the stone wall widened his eyes.
“Y-You...”
Something about the man’s face was familiar. Perhaps they had met somewhere.
Baeksang watched him help the old woman up, anger and gratitude mingling on his face. Then he saw her face and understood.
He looks like her. So much.
It was the old palace attendant he had personally ordered expelled from the Inner Palace before any of this began.
One of the few people left who remembered the man he had once been was bleeding and groaning before him.
“Cough. Mmm...”
“M-Mother!”
She had a child?
Baeksang watched the man hurriedly check on his mother, then found himself walking toward them.
He did not know why. He simply felt that he should.
“D-Don’t come any closer!”
The cry was full of hostility.
People could shut their doors and lock them, but they could not close their ears.

By now, everyone in the Nanman Beast Palace knew their Palace Lord, the Great Chieftain of the Bai people, had betrayed them. They knew Baeksang was responsible for the screams and deaths that continued even now.
The man before him knew it too. He stood between Baeksang and his mother, clutching a sharp piece of stone he had picked up somewhere.
“If you take one more step...”
Swish! Crack!
Finger Qi pierced the stone, and it crumbled in his hand.
Baeksang passed the frozen man and reached toward the old woman.
Tap. Tap!
The blurred hand moved like lightning, touching the old woman’s acupoints. At the same moment, her furrowed brow smoothed.
“Cough.”
She spat out stagnant blood, and her face relaxed.
The man hastily checked his mother, then looked up at Baeksang, unable to understand.
“W-Why?”
Why?
Baeksang could not answer even that simple question. Perhaps he would not be able to answer it in ten years, or a hundred.
He did not know the answer himself.
When he finally broke the brief silence, he gave no answer.
“Leave with the others. Get as far away as you can.”
“S-Sir!”
“Do you intend to let your mother die like this? Or...”
Baeksang’s gaze darkened.
“Will you make her watch you die?”
“Go. If you head for the East Gate, a way out will open.”
Baeksang turned away. Behind him, the man’s hoarse voice rang out.
“Do you think this will... Do you think this will make the sins you committed forgivable!”
Baeksang answered the angry shout only in his heart.
No. I never once thought I would be forgiven.
Rumble, rumble!
A deafening roar rolled behind him as he headed toward the Inner Palace.
He sped onward without a trace of hesitation.
It was time to face the moment he had pictured for decades.
