A terrifyingly immense surge of qi rose and pressed down on everything around it.
The countless beasts that had been baring their teeth and growling tucked their tails between their legs.
Pavilions throughout the area began to collapse as though a giant had stepped on them.
Tribespeople fleeing the Outer Palace in terror spotted the figure suspended in the air and gaped.
Darkness.
A woman wrapped from head to toe in surging darkness looked down upon the ground.
Like a god—or a Fiend out of legend—she seemed to be weighing how much life they had left.
Yet while everyone else stared at her in fear, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had eyes for only one thing.
“Hand it over.”
Rumble.
The dark clouds filling the sky gave a great roar.
Her chilling voice rang through the world of light and darkness, reaching every ear.
“It is something the Lord of Heaven must rightfully take.
It is not an object that insignificant beings like you are fit to possess.”
Beasts and humans alike froze before her overwhelming power.
They forgot to scream, forgot to run, and stared blankly up at her.
All except two people.
No—two beings.
“Bullshit, you crazy bitch.”
—How dare a mere human covet the sacred stone?
Jin Taekyung and the guardian spirit stared at the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
They could feel it: the unprecedented power coiled inside that small body.
The qi pressing down around them was greater than any the guardian spirit had encountered in a human over the past several hundred years.
It surpassed even that of the Western Heaven Demon Lord, whom Jin Taekyung had fought while narrowly escaping death time and again.
Strong.
And frightening.
Fear was something every living creature knew.
But feeling it and surrendering to it were different things.
They knew that even now, they had to endure the fear pressing down on their entire bodies and advance.
Only then could they win.
—Much blood will flow, human.
“Fuck.
If I survive this, I won’t even take a piss toward Nanman again.”
Jin Taekyung muttered through clenched teeth and tightened his grip on White Flame’s shaft.
Then he spoke quietly to Yohi, who stood frozen behind him.
“You know what to do, right?”
“Get the people out of here.
Now.
Run like hell, and take them as far away as you can.”
Countless tribespeople lived in the Outer Palace, beyond those he could see.
Jin Taekyung did not want them caught in the horrific hellscape about to unfold here.
It was enough for those with power to bleed.
The tribespeople, with neither weapons nor sharp teeth, had to survive.
Even if everyone who remained here died at the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s hands.
But...
I’ll stop her.
We’ll stop her.
For now, the sacred stone’s power was holding back the demonic qi pouring from the rift.
He did not know how long this tense standoff would last, but before the situation grew any worse, they had to defeat the Southern Heaven Demon Empress and close the rift.
No matter what it takes.
Whoosh.
Jin Taekyung drew a deep breath and glared at the figure high above the wreckage of the pavilions.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
The beginning and end of everything that had happened in this land.
Someone had to fall before this cruel story could end.
“Let’s go.”
The low voice had just slipped between his lips when—
—Kraaaaaaang!
A fierce roar tore through the wind.
The radiance that had been fading against the darkness swelled once more, rousing the terrified beasts and people.
Fwoosh!
Kwoooooosh!
Light burst forth with the roar.
Flames blazed around the silver spearhead.
The outsider who had come to this land after hundreds of years soared upward as one with the enormous White Tiger.
Bang!
He kicked off the ground.
Pop!
He stepped on the invisible air and wind.
Whoooooosh!
Toward the darkness spread across the distant sky.
No.
Toward the being made still stronger by that darkness.
“Southern Heaven Demon Empress!”
His flame-wreathed azure dragon’s roar flew with the spearhead, cleaving through space.
A chilling look crossed the woman’s face, now twisted like a Fiend’s, with not a trace of beauty left.
“The Lord of Heaven desires it.”
At that moment—
Flash!
Light and darkness mingled in a blinding flash that washed over the Nanman Beast Palace.
Rrrrrumble.
A roar like the sky splitting apart accompanied a tremendous surge of qi that swept in every direction.
Baeksang instinctively shut his eyes against the blinding flash.
A gale struck his entire body, and he swallowed a groan.
Hngh.
What kind of overwhelming power was this?
Even as a Supreme Peak master, he could barely keep his balance against the aftershock.
When he finally opened his eyes, the area around him had already been reduced to ruins.
The tribespeople who had barely survived thanks to the protection of the beasts were fleeing while screaming.
“Kyaaaaaa!”
“Hoya!
Hoya!
Where are you?”
“M-Mother!”
Pavilions and houses built over many years collapsed one after another.
A grown son cried out at the sight of his elderly mother pinned beneath a fallen stone wall.
Screams and death.
Blood and bodies.
Only days ago, these streets had been full of laughter and music.
Now there was no trace of either—only an endless din of roars and screams.
Bang!
Kwoooooang!
Light and darkness shot toward each other and tangled together, again and again, in the space of an instant.
Baeksang stared hollowly at the hellscape beneath the murky flashes and sky-splitting roars.
Then he reached out in one direction.
Boom!
The force of his palm crossed the distance and knocked a large boulder away.
A half-gray-haired middle-aged man who had been struggling to save an old woman trapped beneath the stone wall widened his eyes.
“Y-You...”
Something about the man’s face was familiar.
Perhaps they had met somewhere.
Baeksang watched him help the old woman up, anger and gratitude mingling on his face.
Then he saw her face and understood.
He looks like her.
So much.
It was the old palace attendant he had personally ordered expelled from the Inner Palace before any of this began.
One of the few people left who remembered the man he had once been was bleeding and groaning before him.
“Cough.
Mmm...”
“M-Mother!”
She had a child?
Baeksang watched the man hurriedly check on his mother, then found himself walking toward them.
He did not know why.
He simply felt that he should.
“D-Don’t come any closer!”
The cry was full of hostility.
People could shut their doors and lock them, but they could not close their ears.
By now, everyone in the Nanman Beast Palace knew their Palace Lord, the Great Chieftain of the Bai people, had betrayed them.
They knew Baeksang was responsible for the screams and deaths that continued even now.
The man before him knew it too.
He stood between Baeksang and his mother, clutching a sharp piece of stone he had picked up somewhere.
“If you take one more step...”
Swish!
Crack!
Finger Qi pierced the stone, and it crumbled in his hand.
Baeksang passed the frozen man and reached toward the old woman.
Tap.
Tap!
The blurred hand moved like lightning, touching the old woman’s acupoints.
At the same moment, her furrowed brow smoothed.
“Cough.”
She spat out stagnant blood, and her face relaxed.
The man hastily checked his mother, then looked up at Baeksang, unable to understand.
“W-Why?”
Why?
Baeksang could not answer even that simple question.
Perhaps he would not be able to answer it in ten years, or a hundred.
He did not know the answer himself.
When he finally broke the brief silence, he gave no answer.
“Leave with the others.
Get as far away as you can.”
“S-Sir!”
“Do you intend to let your mother die like this?
Baeksang’s gaze darkened.
“Will you make her watch you die?”
“Go.
If you head for the East Gate, a way out will open.”
Baeksang turned away.
Behind him, the man’s hoarse voice rang out.
“Do you think this will...
Do you think this will make the sins you committed forgivable!”
Baeksang answered the angry shout only in his heart.
No.
I never once thought I would be forgiven.
Rumble, rumble!
A deafening roar rolled behind him as he headed toward the Inner Palace.
He sped onward without a trace of hesitation.
It was time to face the moment he had pictured for decades.

chapters.title: Chapter 699
paragraphs: Rumble! Crash!
Unable to withstand the fierce vibrations, the stone walls of the Inner Palace crumbled helplessly, and the iron gate that had broken free slammed into the ground with a heavy roar.
It was like watching a small hill collapse.
Baeksang slipped past the debris and shot forward.
Whoooosh!
Wind brushed across his entire body. His sharpened senses caught the metallic scent of blood and the screams echoing from every direction.
He felt the internal energy churning inside him and took a deep breath.
I must not let it overwhelm me.
A massive cliff rose behind the Inner Palace like a folding screen. Demonic qi flowed from a gap in it—a gap that could only be called a rift now. Even Baeksang could not take it lightly.

Only because he was a Supreme Peak master could he move through the Inner Palace like this. Unless one walked the Demonic Path, even a fairly skilled internal-energy master would have had his internal energy thrown into disarray and lost his composure the moment he entered the demonic qi’s domain.
Just like the middle-aged man now staggering into his path to block him.
“P-Palace Lord? Is that you, Palace Lord?”

Baeksang knew his face. Greedy like his father, the man had inherited his position as tribal chieftain without any particular ability and lived in luxury. He had been one of Baeksang’s most ardent supporters.
But the man who used to greet Baeksang with an oily, flattering smile was now crying out with blood running from his seven apertures.
“Please, please save me! I don’t want to die ye—!”
His flailing hand brushed Baeksang’s white collar. Baeksang quietly looked down at the fallen tribal chieftain, who had lost his balance, and opened his mouth.
“Why should I?”
“P-Palace Lord?”
“You must have known already. That what I intended to do would bring great harm to Nanman.”
“We each got what we wanted and paid a fair price for it. So don’t think you’ve been wronged.”
I won’t, either.
The last words never left his lips. Finger Qi shot from his fingertips.
Puhk!
The attack pierced the crown of the chieftain’s skull, and he collapsed. His eyes remained wide with disbelief. Even in death, they seemed to ask Baeksang a question.
Why? How? How can you still stand so proudly even in the face of this hellscape?
And Baeksang answered the dead man’s question in his heart.
Because I had already made up my mind.
Even so, his breath trembled.
If that man had begged him to save the tribespeople instead of his own life, would Baeksang have saved them?
No. Perhaps meeting such a peaceful death was actually an act of mercy for a man with such poor martial arts.
Ten thousand.
A full ten thousand warriors and beasts were bleeding and writhing in the grip of the demonic qi. Their screams seemed to squeeze his heart and rake through his mind like blades.
Baeksang did not stop.
Whoooosh!

He sped across the vast training ground, where screams filled the air. The stable where he and Yayul Cheok had hidden whenever they got into trouble as children flashed past, then the storehouse they used to sneak into for fruit wine.
Vengeance. Anger. Regret.
The emotions that had piled up layer after layer with every step whipped around him.
If only I hadn’t taken my only son to the battlefield. If only I’d drawn my sword instead of clasping hands with the Southern Heaven Demon Empress the day she came.
If only I’d told my one sworn elder brother the whole truth. He’d trusted me more than anyone—even more than I trusted myself.
Or...
If only I’d carried it all alone and taken my own life.
Step.
His feet stopped before a tightly closed door. His eyes had long since gone bloodshot.
In his mind, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s voice echoed from the night before.
“Noon. Tomorrow at noon. Gather every warrior in the palace at the Inner Palace.”
“Tomorrow... at noon?”
“Yes. That’s the end of your part. After that, we’ll take care of—”
“Our promise.”
“Hmm?”
“Please keep the promise you made me long ago.”
“You’re rather impudent, aren’t you? Interrupting an adult while she’s speaking.”
She had laughed. Baeksang had dropped to his knees without hesitation.
Only after watching the new lord of the Nanman Beast Palace repeatedly strike his head against the floor for quite some time did she finally give him the answer he had so desperately wanted.
“A polite child deserves a reward. Fine. Once the grand plan begins, return to your office.”
“My... office?”
“Yes. This very place. That’s when I’ll fulfill my promise.”
Her amused voice faded from his ears. Baeksang’s only hand trembled as he reached toward the door, slowly, so slowly.

He had never wondered how. If the Southern Heaven Demon Empress and Dark Heaven said it was so, then it was so. All the things they had done—things that seemed to defy nature—made it easier still to believe.
However many eyes watched the Inner Palace, the promise would be kept.
At last.
He had made it here.
Baeksang closed his eyes. A wave of distant memories rose and swallowed him.
Long years of suffering.
But even this lonely story had a final chapter. He opened his eyes as though waking from sleep and pushed the door wide.
Creak.
His spacious office came into view.
Simple, crude furnishings that still held the warmth of their former owner. A table that had preserved the traces of many long years.
And, out of place among them, a large mirror.
And then. And then...
That was all.
Nothing. There’s nothing here.
The impossible truth bore down on him like a massive boulder. Baeksang stared at the office with hollow, empty eyes, then suddenly let out a hollow laugh.
“Heh. Heh heh. Heh heh heh.”
He laughed because he could not cry. Because he could do nothing else.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress had not kept her promise. Decades of his life, everything he had done—all of it turned to ash and blew away.
So this was how it ended.
“Ha-ha-ha-ha-ha!”
Baeksang laughed as though he were a boy again. He clutched his stomach and rolled across the floor, tears streaming down his face.
No. He was crying.
“Ha—ha-ha! Aaaaaah!”
The laughter broke into a scream. Baeksang struck the floor and walls with a fist that held not a trace of internal energy.
Bang! Bang! Krrr-boom!
He kept punching. The office was not the only thing that broke.
The callused back of his hand split open, and white bone showed faintly through the blood covering his fist.
It hurts.
More than it ever had.
Drip. Drip-drip.
Blood pooled in the spiderweb cracks across the floor. Baeksang staggered to his feet and approached the window.
He had thought the world had stopped. Beyond the open window, everything was still moving at a furious pace.
“Graaah!”
“P-Please, just kill me...!”
—Grrk, grrrk!
Humans and beasts struggled as they resisted the demonic qi devouring their bodies and minds. Shapes large and small raced toward them as they screamed.
Thud-thud-thud-thud!
Countless beasts thundered across the ground, climbed over the collapsed stone walls, and descended upon them—not to kill, but to rescue them.
—Graaaar!

With the roar of a familiar White Tiger at the head of the group, the beasts moved in perfect formation. They bit the arms, legs, or scruffs of the nearest people and beasts, then raced toward the Outer Palace.
Away from the demonic qi. One step farther toward the light.
Baeksang clenched his fist. His nails dug into his palm, and blood welled around them.
He looked into the distance, where light and darkness clashed without pause.
Rumble!
He could feel waves of unimaginable power. With every clash, the light faded a little more, and one figure fell again.
Boom! Crack!
The figure hurtled toward the ground like a meteor. Two pavilions collapsed, and the earth shook.
But only for a moment. Blue flames stepped on empty air and shot toward the thick darkness.
Without a moment’s rest. As though it could burn away even the death waiting for it.
Jin Taekyung.
Why go so far? Why?
The question remained trapped in Baeksang’s mouth. Another question, heard not long ago in a corner of a dark underground prison, echoed in his ears.
“How much more blood do you mean to spill, Baeksang?”
Baeksang stared blankly out the window and finally gave his answer.
“I don’t know. I don’t know either.”
It was a secret he had been unable to tell anyone.

After losing his son, he had dreamed of revenge. Meeting the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had given him hope. Then one day he had realized he’d crossed a river he could never cross back, and despair had followed.
And now, at the end of the thorny path he had walked, he found nothing at all.
Step.
Baeksang staggered back from the window. He could no longer bear to watch the hellscape he had made with his own hands, or the young outsider risking his life to stop it from becoming complete.
What was any of it for?
He turned away from the window with a question he would never answer—and froze.
Someone covered in blood and dust was looking back at him.
A man who had lost everything and become an empty shell. An old man who had held the years at bay through sheer martial power, surviving as a monster.
The large mirror occupying one corner of the office reflected his figure.
But Baeksang saw something else, too.
“Ah.”
Hwi.
He reached toward him with a call that could never reach him. Or tried to.
The mirror’s clear, smooth surface rippled like water.
Ssssrrrk.
Only then did Baeksang understand who had given him the mirror, and why the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had said her promise would be fulfilled here.
She hadn’t lied.
In his cold heart, an ember of hope he had thought extinguished began to burn again.
The mirror clouded with darkness. Before Baeksang’s trembling eyes, it spat out a black-clad figure—and a cold sword blade imbued with Force.
Puhk!
Flash.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress thrust out a foot smaller than a boy’s palm.
The moment it met the side of my spearhead, a force greater than a giant’s surged through me.
Crack—bang!
“Human!”
I heard the guardian spirit’s cry as I fell. The impact drove me deep into the ground and jolted through my back, forcing my mouth open.
Cough.
Blood ran from the corner of my mouth. I’d already suffered serious Internal Injury, and my cracked bones creaked and ached whenever I moved.
Monster.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress was a bitch for the ages, and a monster to match. Her martial arts surpassed anyone I’d faced—even the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
But...
Get up. As many times as it takes.
A few times. A few dozen. It didn’t matter.
There was nowhere left to retreat. If I took even one step back, that place would become hell.
Not only me, but every living thing in Nanman—and even the Central Plains—would inevitably be swallowed by the flames.
I have to stop her.
I wiped the blood from the corner of my mouth with my sleeve and stood.
Before I could summon my internal energy again, I realized things could still get worse.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
I turned my head on instinct.
“...Fuck.”
Darkness descending thickly over the collapsing Inner Palace.

As many times as it takes.
A few times.
A few dozen.
It didn’t matter.
There was nowhere left to retreat.
If I took even one step back, that place would become hell.
Not only me, but every living thing in Nanman—and even the Central Plains—would inevitably be swallowed by the flames.
I have to stop her.
I wiped the blood from the corner of my mouth with my sleeve and stood.
Before I could summon my internal energy again, I realized things could still get worse.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
I turned my head on instinct.
“...Fuck.”
Darkness descending thickly over the collapsing Inner Palace.

chapters.title: Chapter 700
paragraphs: Me, the guardian spirit, and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Less than fifteen minutes had passed since the battle began, but if I was being generous, we’d been evenly matched.
Until now.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
“...Fuck.”
The curse slipped out before I could stop it.
Not just because the Inner Palace was collapsing. It might have been the symbol and pride of the Nanman Beast Palace, but in the end, it was only a building.
The problem was that as the largest structure in the Nanman Beast Palace crumbled like a sandcastle, the darkness pouring from the rift grew thicker.
Kraaaaaash!
Demonic qi. Also known as magical power.
That pure, dangerous energy surged outward in a wave. It swallowed the enormous dust cloud, crossed the open space, and reached the living beings who had yet to escape the Inner Palace.
“Grrk, keugh!”
—Kyaaaaaa!
Humans and beasts screamed.
The eyes that had begun to regain focus turned white. Their trembling bodies contorted with a sickening sound of tearing flesh.
Crack. Crrrunch.
Death flashed through my mind, but that wasn’t it.
What awaited them was pain worse than death, and the changes that would soon come over them would make them forget even the pain.
No. I should call it a mutation, not a change.
I knew what I was seeing. I’d seen it once before—and experienced it myself.

The magical power from the rift had been strong enough to corrupt a five-hundred-year-old imugi. The Water God Dragon had borne it alone, so its case was different. Even so, ordinary beasts and most martial artists had no hope of shaking off its influence by themselves.
Not unless someone helped them.
And apparently, that someone is me.
Fuck.
I hesitated at the thought of leaving the guardian spirit to fight alone, but only for a moment.

Several thousand humans and beasts were still inside the Inner Palace. Their lives were reason enough. But if the magical power consumed them completely and turned them into mutants, the hellscape the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had envisioned would be complete.
Whatever else happened, a horrific slaughter would begin as they killed one another.
In a moment too short to call an instant, I wasn’t the only one to realize it.
—Go! Hurry!
The thought rang through my head almost at the same time I kicked off the ground.
Boom!
Compression. Then explosion.
A violent wind struck my body, and the scenery changed around me.
I shot forward like a cannonball, leaving a small crater behind and clearing more than sixty yards in a single bound. As my toes touched down lightly, flames of manifested qi flickered beneath them.
Flamefire Path.
Kraaaaaash!
In a world gone slow, blue-white light-flames burst forth.

The guardian spirit vanished from my sight as it charged the Southern Heaven Demon Empress with a roar that shook the sky. So did Muyaho, racing out of the Outer Palace with all his strength at the very rear of the survivors.
Whoooosh.
Wind carrying the scent of blood brushed across my entire body. By then, beneath the feet I had planted in midair, I could see countless beasts and humans writhing as darkness engulfed them.
And...
I can feel it.
After reaching the Supreme Peak realm, each new insight had taught me the same thing: everything in the world had a flow. Just because I couldn’t see it didn’t mean I couldn’t feel it.
The formless wind. Rock hard enough to turn aside steel. Still water. Each had its flow, or a faint gap within it.
Its grain.
Now!
Fwoooosh!
Certain of my aim, I slashed downward with my spear.
Three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi coiled around its transparent blade, burning through the darkness as it cut through the air.
I aimed for the grain in the pitch-black darkness wrapped around thousands of lives. For that fine, invisible flow I could sever in a single stroke.
And then—
Whoooosh—boom!
A roar like the sky splitting apart rang out as flames streaming from White Flame’s blade exploded in a brilliant burst.
My eyes widened.
The battles had left me exhausted and injured, but that strike had been nearly everything I had. I’d been sure I could scatter at least some of the demonic qi, if not all of it.
And he knocked it away?
I’d seen it clearly, brief as it was: Force flying out of the darkness like a ray of light. Though it was far too dark and ominous to deserve the name.
Tap.
I landed softly and glared into the darkness.
No—at the hazy figure walking slowly out of the Inner Palace ruins, half-hidden by the dust.
“...A mask? Who the fuck are you?”
The answer to my question was a single flash of light that glinted from more than thirty yards away.
Shwaaaak! Slash!
I missed it by a hair.
I twisted my head like lightning and glanced over my shoulder. A pavilion that had somehow retained its shape until now had been crushed and split in half.
Crack. Rumble!
Watching the pavilion collapse half a beat late, I muttered inwardly.
Fast.
The power behind that attack was savage and unrefined. Rough, yes—but devastating. If I failed to dodge even once, there wouldn’t be enough of my body left to find.
But the same was true of me.
Puhk. Whoooosh!
I didn’t need to summon anything from my Inventory. Weapons lay scattered everywhere. I pulled an iron spear from the ground, took it in a reverse grip, and hurled it with all my strength.
Boom!
Force stopped the spear and sent it bouncing away. Just as I’d expected.
I’d launched myself forward the instant I threw it. Now I drove White Flame at the masked man.
Shu-whoom! Boom!
Compressed air burst from the spearpoint. The masked man twisted aside by no more than a sheet of paper’s width, seized the shaft, and stepped in.
At the same time, dark sword-light flashed from his fingertips.
Slash!
A faint sting.
I’d dodged, but not quite enough. Wind from the powerful sword strike grazed the bridge of my nose, drawing blood.
A few drops were cheap. I was about to get far more in return.
If you think I’m like other martial artists, you’ve got it wrong.

Martial artists valued their weapons as much as their lives. Most trained in arts that used them, knowing a few clumsy fist, palm, finger, or kicking techniques wouldn’t see them through a life-and-death duel.
I was different.

I had physical abilities beyond human limits and the Fire Gate Clan’s fist, palm, finger, and kicking techniques—arts worthy of being called divine. I also had an Inventory with nearly limitless capacity, full of weapons.
Crack!
Even a divine weapon was useless if it couldn’t reach its target.
I let go of the spear shaft, caught the wrist of his sword hand, and shot out my free hand. At the same time, I gave a command only I could understand.
Inventory open. Summon.
Whoosh!
I missed his heart, but the rusty dagger, glowing red with Scorching Yang Qi, pierced Body-Protecting Qi harder than armor and sank into his chest.
Puhk!
He went rigid without so much as a groan.
I wasn’t stopping there.
Finish him.
I didn’t know his name or sobriquet. I did know he served the Southern Heaven Demon Empress. If I held back and let him live, I’d pay for it.
He had to die here. Now.
Crack! Crunch!
Still gripping his wrist, I drove my knee up like lightning and felt his bones shatter. The arm with the crushed elbow went limp, and his sword began to slip from his fingers.
Srrk.
One of those fingers twitched.
From a blind spot I couldn’t see came the sound of something slicing through the air.
Whoooosh!
Everything had a grain and a flow. So did the sounds weapons made.
What is that?
I’d heard it somewhere before. The recognition was almost there, along with a sharp sense that something was wrong, but I had no time to follow it.
Only an instant to choose.
Trust my instincts and the Fire Dragon Armor, and finish him? Or leave him with the grievous wounds he’d already taken and protect myself?
I made my choice. Turning, I thrust out my hand.
No—both palms.
One toward the masked man. The other toward the two streaks of light already upon me.
Boom! Crash!
The Flame Divine Palm struck his chest and sent him flying like a cannonball into the ruins of the Inner Palace.
But...
Crrrunch!
Had I been too greedy, trying to catch two birds at once?
The impact drove me backward. I carved a deep furrow into the ground for ten steps before the burning pain reached me.
Tap. Drip-drip.
Blood ran down my fingers and struck the ground. I staunched the bleeding from my left hand, its flesh and muscle torn half to shreds, then bit my lip.
Because it hurt? No. I’d taken injuries like this often enough as a Hunter.
An injured hand was bad news when I needed to conserve every bit of strength I could, but I could still use it.
It was the tremendous rebound force I had felt when my Flame Divine Palm struck the masked man’s chest—and the identity of the flash whose sound alone had caused that sense of incongruity.
This is...
The shape and size were different, but I knew what I was holding.
I stared at the twin wheels caught in my left hand and slowly turned, thinking of the old fiend whose last words had been a promise to wait for me in the afterlife.
“What’s your connection to the Great Snow Fiend?”
I hoped he wouldn’t answer. I hoped the force I’d felt at the end had been my imagination.
But my ominous suspicion had already become reality.
Rumble. Rustle.
Within the cloud of dust that had yet to settle, heavy rebar and timber shifted, and a pale figure rose to its feet.
Then a flashing streak of light crossed more than sixty yards and hurtled at me.
Whoosh! Crrrunch!
It came with ferocious force. I caught it in a hand filled with internal energy and fell silent.
A dagger.
The same dagger I’d driven into his chest moments ago.
Blood that wasn’t mine stained its heavily rusted, handspan-long blade. My attack had landed.
If so, he should have suffered a fatal wound... How the hell?
I knew all too well that humans—Supreme Peak masters in particular—didn’t die as easily as one might think.
They were monsters capable of fighting a hundred men alone even with a dagger buried in their chest.
But not when the one who put it there was a Supreme Peak master of equal or greater skill.
This isn’t a fight between street thugs.
In a life-and-death duel between masters, the greatest danger wasn’t the blade. It was the internal energy carried on it—energy that entered through the wound and tore apart the blood vessels within.
Even a Supreme Peak master couldn’t escape Internal Injury from a hit like that. The Great Snow Fiend himself, with all his martial arts and profound internal energy, hadn’t been an exception.
And yet...
He got up like nothing happened, pulled the dagger out of his chest, and threw it? With this much internal energy behind it, when suppressing the Internal Injury alone should have been a struggle?
The dagger wound wasn’t even all he’d taken. One arm was crippled at the very least, and I’d struck him square in the chest with the Flame Divine Palm.
Even a master at the level of the Ten Kings could not be that unharmed.
“...What the fuck are you?”
That wrongness had spread through my whole body, bringing a cold wariness with it.
But before the masked man could answer my question, a tremendous roar rang out.
Kraaa-boom!
A silver figure struck the ground like a meteor.
The guardian spirit lay there, its body covered in wounds, panting for breath. Above its head in midair, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress stood with a smile.
“My hunting dog. I took great care training him.”
